{{Short description|none}} {{Use Hiberno-English|date=August 2015}} {{Use dmy dates|date=January 2021}} {{Infobox football match | title = 2009 All-Ireland Hurling Final | image = 2009 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final programme.jpg | image_size = 250 | event = [[2009 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]] | team1 = [[Kilkenny county hurling team|Kilkenny]] | team1association = [[File:Colours of Kilkenny.svg|40px]] | team1score = 2–22 | team2 = [[Tipperary county hurling team|Tipperary]] | team2association = [[File:Colours of Tipperary.svg|40px]] | team2score = 0–23 | details = | date = 6 September 2009 | stadium = [[Croke Park]] | city = [[Dublin]] | man_of_the_match1a = [[P. J. Ryan (hurler, born 1977)|P.J. Ryan]] | referee = [[Diarmuid Kirwan]] ([[Cork GAA|Cork]]) | attendance = 82,106 | weather = Light Rain
{{convert|16|°C|°F}}[https://web.archive.org/web/20101230175712/http://met.ie/climate/monthlyBulletins/sep09lores.pdf] . Met Éireann, Monthly Weather Bulletin, 24hr Max & Min Temps | previous = [[2008 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2008]] | next = [[2010 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2010]] }} The '''2009 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final''' was a [[hurling]] match played on 6 September 2009 in [[Croke Park]], Dublin, between [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] and [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]].{{cite web|title=GAA Hurling All Ireland Senior Championship | The Official Website of the GAA |url=http://www.gaa.ie/page/gaa_hurling_all_ireland_senior_championship3.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090805183920/http://www.gaa.ie/page/gaa_hurling_all_ireland_senior_championship3.html |archive-date=5 August 2009 |url-status=dead |access-date=2009-08-16}} It was the first time the two teams had met in the All-Ireland final since [[1991 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1991]]. Kilkenny's win was their fourth in a row, an accomplishment last matched by [[Cork GAA|Cork]] between 1941 and 1944.{{cite web|url=https://www.gaa.ie/hurling/news/flashback-2009-all-ireland-shc-final-kilkenny-v-tipperary/ |title =Flashback: 2009 All-Ireland SHC Final - Kilkenny v Tipperary|date=24 March 2020|work=GAA.ie|access-date=25 March 2020}} Kilkenny's victory gave them a record seventh title of the decade and a record 18th consecutive Championship win. Following the match, Kilkenny manager [[Brian Cody]] announced details of the release of his autobiography, ''Cody''.{{cite web|url=http://www.eveningecho.ie/news/index.aspx?c=sport&jp=eycwojqlkfey |title=Release date set for Cody autobiography |date=2009-09-09 |access-date=2009-09-09 |work=[[Evening Echo]] |quote=Kilkenny hurling boss Brian Cody will release his autobiography 'Cody' on September 28. |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110720012347/http://www.eveningecho.ie/news/index.aspx?c=sport&jp=eycwojqlkfey |archive-date=20 July 2011 }}{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2009/0909/codyb.html |title=Cody book set for September release |date=2009-09-09 |access-date=2009-09-09 |publisher=[[RTÉ]] |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090911080344/http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2009/0909/codyb.html |archive-date=11 September 2009 }} Kilkenny hurler [[Henry Shefflin]] was named as the sport's Opel GPA Player of the Month for August after the win; Shefflin contributed 1–14 of Kilkenny's score in the final.{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2009/0910/gpa.html |title=Canty and Shefflin take GPA awards |date=2009-09-10 |access-date=2009-09-10 |publisher=[[RTÉ]] |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090914185418/http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2009/0910/gpa.html |archive-date=14 September 2009 }} Shefflin was named on The Etihad 125 Dream Team before the final.{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/shefflin-replaces--langton-in-etihad-125-dream-team-1878081.html|title=Shefflin replaces Langton in Etihad 125 'Dream Team|date=2009-09-04|access-date=2009-09-20|work=[[Irish Independent]]}} He also claimed his ninth [[GAA All Stars Awards|All Star Award]]. Prior to the game, Kilkenny were hailed as already being "the greatest side ever to play the game" by Eamonn Sweeney in the ''[[Sunday Independent (Ireland)|Sunday Independent]]'' as the Cork side who had already achieved four consecutive titles over sixty years previously did so against the backdrop of a [[foot-and-mouth disease]] outbreak which led to fewer games being played.{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaa-championships/hurling/codys-cats-have-record-books-all-figured-out-1879506.html|title=Cody's Cats have record books all figured out|date=2009-09-06|access-date=2009-09-07|work=[[Irish Independent]]}} Rock singer [[Shane MacGowan]] attended the final to support his team Tipperary.{{cite web|author=Fiona Dillon |url=http://www.herald.ie/entertainment/around-town/macgowan-laughs-off-swine-flu-to--cheer-his-tipperary-team-in-final-1879313.html |title=MacGowan laughs off swine flu to cheer his Tipperary team in final |date=2009-09-05 |access-date=2009-09-20 |work=[[Evening Herald]] |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091022082004/http://www.herald.ie/entertainment/around-town/macgowan-laughs-off-swine-flu-to--cheer-his-tipperary-team-in-final-1879313.html |archive-date=22 October 2009 }} ==Background== Kilkenny went into the 2009 hurling final as defending champions, having won it in three consecutive years from 2006 to 2008. They were aiming for their fourth consecutive All-Ireland Senior Hurling title, a feat only previously achieved in hurling by Cork from 1941 to 1944.{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2009/0907/kilkenny4.html|title=Finals are cool for Cats|date=2009-09-07|access-date=2009-09-07|publisher=[[RTÉ]]}} ==Ticketing== On 1 September 2009, the GAA confirmed that the final was an 82,000 sell-out. GAA Ticketing Manager Ronan Murphy said "Sunday's All-Ireland final is a sell-out. In fact both Tipperary and Kilkenny had been back to us looking for more tickets. There is an ancient rivalry between Tipperary and Kilkenny and the fact that Kilkenny are going for the four in a row also adds to the interest ... Throughout the country the demand for tickets was very strong".{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2009/0901/kilkenny_tipperary.html |title=Kilkenny v Tipperary is a sell-out |date=2009-09-01 |work=RTÉ Sport |access-date=2009-09-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090904040448/http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2009/0901/kilkenny_tipperary.html |archive-date=4 September 2009 |url-status=dead}} ==Team news== Tipperary manager [[Liam Sheedy]] kept faith with the same team that beat [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] in the Semi-final. Vice captain [[Conor O'Mahony]] was passed fit after suffering a 'dead leg' the previous week and lead the team from the centre-back position. [[Willie Ryan (Tipperary hurler)|Willie Ryan]], who was named team captain at the start of the season, had to make do with a place on the substitutes bench. Goalkeeper [[Brendan Cummins (Tipperary hurler)|Brendan Cummins]], full-forward [[Eoin Kelly (Tipperary hurler)|Eoin Kelly]] and right-corner forward [[Lar Corbett]] were the only survivors from the last Tipperary team to play in an All-Ireland final in [[2001 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2001]].{{cite web|url=http://www.setanta.com/uk/Articles/other-sports/2009/09/04/Sheedy-sees-no-need-for-change-/gnid-58571/ |title=Sheedy sees no need for change |date=2009-09-04 |work=Setanta Sports |access-date=2009-09-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090918033511/http://www.setanta.com/uk/Articles/other-sports/2009/09/04/Sheedy-sees-no-need-for-change-/gnid-58571/ |archive-date=18 September 2009 |url-status=dead}} Kilkenny manager [[Brian Cody]] in naming his team, omitted [[2008 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2008]] All-Ireland-winning captain [[James "Cha" Fitzpatrick]] for the final in favour of [[Derek Lyng]]. In total Cody made two personnel changes to the side which beat [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] in the Semi-final stage, [[Richie Hogan]] also started at right half-forward, with [[Henry Shefflin]] moving to centre-forward, [[Martin Comerford]] was the player to drop out of the team.{{cite web|url=http://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/cody-names-kilkenny-final-team-425168.html |title=Cody names Kilkenny final team |date=2009-09-05 |work=Irish Examiner|access-date=2009-09-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090916011757/http://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/cody-names-kilkenny-final-team-425168.html |archive-date=16 September 2009 |url-status=live}} Comerford later revealed he had received advance word of this, but not from management.{{cite web|author=Frank Roche |url=http://www.herald.ie/opinion/columnists/frank-roche/phone-tipoff-alerts-supersub-comerford-of-his-bench-role-1882823.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130218050353/http://www.herald.ie/opinion/columnists/frank-roche/phone-tipoff-alerts-supersub-comerford-of-his-bench-role-1882823.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=2013-02-18 |title=Phone tip-off alerts supersub Comerford of his bench role |date=2009-09-10 |access-date=2009-09-12 |work=[[Evening Herald]] }} ==Match summary== [[File:2009 All Ireland Final teams marching before game.jpg|thumb|550px|Both teams parade around [[Croke Park]] before the start of the game]] ===First half=== An early effort on goal by Kilkenny's [[Henry Shefflin]] was blocked by Tipperary goalkeeper [[Brendan Cummins (Tipperary hurler)|Brendan Cummins]]. Tipperary then entered the lead following a point by [[Lar Corbett]] and two frees converted by [[Eoin Kelly (Tipperary hurler)|Eoin Kelly]]. However, five points were then scored by Kilkenny in quick succession, with [[Eddie Brennan]], [[Eoin Larkin]] and [[Tommy Walsh (hurler, born 1983)|Tommy Walsh]] amongst the scorers. Tipperary's Kelly followed by Lar Corbett twice then scored. Kelly scored his eighth point of the match to give Tipperary the lead seven minutes before half-time. Five of six scores at the end of the first half came from Kilkenny though; amongst the scorers were Shefflin and Brennan. The sides were level in score on seven occasions throughout the first half but by the end it was Kilkenny who led by 0–13 to Tipperary's 0–11.{{cite web|url= https://www.the42.ie/kilkenny-tipperary-2009-all-ireland-hurling-final-takeaways-5099039-May2020/|title =5 big picture takeaways from Kilkenny's 2009 All-Ireland hurling final victory over Tipperary|date=17 May 2020|work=The 42|access-date=18 May 2020}} ===Second half=== The first notable action of the second half occurred when Kilkenny goalkeeper [[P. J. Ryan (hurler, born 1977)|PJ Ryan]] saved from a [[Séamus Callanan]] effort on goal. Callanan, however, soon scored two points to bring the scores level, with [[Shane McGrath (hurler)|Shane McGrath]] scoring the point that put Tipperary ahead once again. Ryan soon saved another effort by Tipperary's Kelly and Kilkenny players Shefflin and Hogan scored some more points. Tipperary substitute [[Benny Dunne]] was sent off in the 53rd minute for hitting out at Walsh. However Tipperary continued to dominate as Kelly, [[Noel McGrath (hurler)|Noel McGrath]] and Callanan each scored points to keep their team two points ahead. A controversial penalty awarded against Tipperary was scored by Shefflin and within one minute [[Martin Comerford]] on as a substitute consolidated Kilkenny's lead with a second goal. The last points of the match were scored by Eoin Larkin to seal Kilkenny's victory. ==Trophy presentation== Prior to the final, the GAA stated that the All-Ireland final post-match presentation of the [[Liam MacCarthy Cup]] would be returned to the centre of the pitch. The Association were considering a return to the centre of Croke Park for All-Ireland day presentations since the 2008 [[Gaelic football|football]] decider between [[Tyrone GAA|Tyrone]] and [[Kerry GAA|Kerry]] when Kerry's [[Colm Cooper]] was jostled by rival supporters as he left the field following the final whistle. From 1999 to 2001, presentations were made in the centre of Croke Park and passed off largely without incident.{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/croker-pitch-to-take-centre-stage-for-final-presentations-1874284.html|title=Croker pitch to take centre stage for final presentations|date=2009-09-01|work=Irish Independent|access-date=2009-09-01}} However, a [[pitch invasion]] by fans following the 2009 hurling final meant plans to change the style of trophy presentation were cancelled, with Kilkenny captain [[Michael Fennelly (hurler)|Michael Fennelly]] receiving the Liam MacCarthy Cup in the Hogan Stand of Croke Park.{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2009/0907/gaa_pitchinvasion.html |title=Cooney disappointed by pitch invasion |date=2009-09-07 |access-date=2009-09-07 |publisher=[[RTÉ]] |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090909022526/http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2009/0907/gaa_pitchinvasion.html |archive-date=9 September 2009 }}{{cite news| url=http://www.irishtimes.com/kilkenny-hurling/all-ireland-hurling-final-2009/ |work=The Irish Times | title=All-Ireland Hurling Final 2009 | first=Seán | last=Moran| access-date= 31 August 2011 }} [[List of Presidents of the Gaelic Athletic Association|GAA President]] [[Christy Cooney]] later spoke of his disappointment about the pitch invasion but indicated that it confirmed his belief that the invasions must stop. He said:
Despite all pre-match communications, press publicity and big-screen appeals, it was extremely disappointing to see our plans were not realised. Even allowing for all the exuberance and joy of supporters on the day, it was disappointing to see the disregard for the safety of others amongst fans intent on getting on the pitch and ignoring safety appeals.
The Kilkenny County Board later complained about the presentation.{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2009/0923/kilkenny.html |title=Kilkenny to complain over on-pitch ban |date=2009-09-23 |access-date=2009-09-23 |publisher=[[RTÉ]] |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090925072258/http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2009/0923/kilkenny.html |archive-date=25 September 2009 }} ==Reaction== Kilkenny manager [[Brian Cody]] called the victory "very special", saying it felt "outstanding, terrific".{{cite web|author=Fintan O'Toole|url=http://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/cody-that-win-was-special-100340.html|title=Cody: That win was special|date=2009-09-07|access-date=2009-09-07|work=[[Irish Examiner]]}} However, he spoke of his annoyance at a question put to him by RTÉ's [[Marty Morrissey]] in his post-match interview which questioned the decision-making of the referee when he gave the penalty.{{cite news|author=Ian O'Riordan|url=http://www.irishtimes.com/newspaper/sport/2009/0908/1224254070816.html|title=Cody's drive for number five begins|date=2009-09-08|access-date=2009-09-08|work=The Irish Times |quote=But Cody turns serious again when asked about the line of questioning RTÉ’s Marty Morrissey took in the immediate aftermath of Sunday’s win – and the suggestion the Kilkenny penalty should never have been: "Did I sound annoyed? Yeah I was, I was. It was, to me, a question I didn’t understand to be honest. At no stage did I consider the referee at all in the game. He was there, he was doing his job at all times. I only look for one thing from a referee – that he appears to be trying to do his very, very best; to be totally impartial and I never questioned at any stage in my head Diarmuid Kirwan’s impartiality and knowing the guy to a very limited extent I wouldn’t expect anything else from him. You’re there having won the All-Ireland final, four-in-a-row, and suddenly the question turned to maybe a poor display of refereeing. I couldn’t comprehend the sense of that at all to be honest. If we were to dissect every mistake by every player and every official at every game we’d gone on forever. I never comment on referees after the game. If anyone thinks it turned out easy for us just look at the free count. I’ve no problem with that, and if we lost the game I wouldn’t be suggesting for one second anything about the referee".}} While later appearing on [[Newstalk]] show ''[[Off the Ball (media company)|Off the Ball]]'', Cody reiterated his irritation with the RTÉ interview and also suggested there was a media "witch-hunt" against Kilkenny hurler Tommy Walsh—"The Tommy Walsh witch-hunt went on and Tommy Walsh rose above everything and proved the kind of player he is".{{cite web|author=Frank Roche |url=http://www.herald.ie/sport/hurling/walsh-victim-of-a-witchhunt-cody-1881449.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130217180500/http://www.herald.ie/sport/hurling/walsh-victim-of-a-witchhunt-cody-1881449.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=2013-02-17 |title=Walsh victim of a witch-hunt: Cody |date=2009-09-09 |access-date=2009-09-09 |work=[[Evening Herald]] }} Tipperary manager [[Liam Sheedy]] said the team could not have done any more, "these lads have done everything I’ve asked of them in last eight months, everything I could possible want them to. So to just come up short is very, very disappointing. We knew we were facing the best team in probably the history of the game".{{cite news|url=http://www.irishtimes.com/newspaper/sport/2009/0907/1224254000520.html |title=Sheedy and Kelly promise [[RTÉ.ie]] recorded 28,076 streams for the minor and senior hurling finals combined.{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2009/0907/audiences.html |title=Huge numbers watch Kilkenny and Ireland wins |date=2009-09-07 |access-date=2009-09-07 |publisher=[[RTÉ]] |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090908145059/http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2009/0907/audiences.html |archive-date=8 September 2009 }} A worldwide audience also watched the match.{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2009/0906/kilkenny_tipperary_.html |title=Kilkenny 2–22 0–23 Tipperary |date=2009-09-07 |access-date=2009-09-07 |publisher=[[RTÉ]] |quote=A scintillating contest had by this stage reached simmering point, with both sides hitting wonderful scores and thrilling a worldwide audience by the sheer intensity of their efforts. |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090925123058/http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2009/0906/kilkenny_tipperary_.html |archive-date=25 September 2009 |url-status=dead }} ==Awards== The nominations for the 2009 [[GAA All Stars Awards]] were announced on 23 September 2009. Carey]] and [[Kerry GAA|Kerry]] [[Gaelic football|football]]er [[Pat Spillane]].{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2009/0923/allstar.html |title=Hurling All Star nominations revealed |date=2009-09-23 |access-date=2009-09-25 |publisher=[[RTÉ]] |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090927071940/http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2009/0923/allstar.html |archive-date=27 September 2009 }} [[Tommy Walsh (hurler, born 1983)|Tommy Walsh]] was nominated for a seventh consecutive year. Despite losing the final, Tipperary achieved one more nomination than Kilkenny, and all but two of the team which started the final were included. First-time nominees for the finalists were [[Pádraic Maher]], [[Paddy Stapleton]], [[James Woodlock]], [[Pat Kerwick]], [[John O'Brien (hurler)|John O'Brien]] and [[Noel McGrath (hurler)|Noel McGrath]] of Tipperary and [[Michael Rice (hurler)|Michael Rice]] of Kilkenny. The '''1991 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final''' was the 104th All-Ireland Final and the culmination of the [[1991 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]], an inter-county [[hurling]] tournament for the top teams in [[Ireland]]. The match was held at [[Croke Park]], [[Dublin]], on 1 September 1991, between [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] and [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]]. The Leinster champions lost to their Munster opponents on a score line of 1–16 to 0-15.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.gaa.ie/hurling/news/flashback-1991-all-ireland-shc-final-tipperary-v-kilkenny/|title =Flashback: 1991 All Ireland SHC Final - Tipperary v Kilkenny|date=21 August 2019|work=GAA.ie|access-date=26 August 2020}}</ref>

==All-Ireland final==
===Overview===
The All-Ireland hurling final was the final match of the 1991 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship.  The match was contested by [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] and [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] on 1 September 1991 at [[Croke Park]], [[Dublin]], and had an attendance of 64,500.  It was Tipperary's third appearance in the championship decider in four years, having lost and won the respective finals of 1988 and 1989.  Kilkenny were lining out in their first final since losing the 1987 decider to [[Galway GAA|Galway]].  Furthermore, it was the first championship meeting of these two great rivals since 1971, when Tipperary were the winners.

Tipperary were red-hot favourites and not just because of their traditional hoodoo over their nearest neighbours.  The team's performances in the provincial championship and their comprehensive defeat of Galway in the All-Ireland semi-final resulted in the premier county being given the bookies nod.  Kilkenny had struggles through each of their provincial games and only scraped past [[Antrim GAA|Antrim]] in the All-Ireland semi-final.

===Match report===
At 3:30pm match referee Willie Horgan of Cork threw in the sliotar and the game was on.  Kilkenny took the game to Tipperary from the throw-in, with veteran hurler [[Christy Heffernan]] causing havoc for the Tipp defence, a group of players who had been lambasted for their earlier performance against [[Cork GAA|Cork]].  On this occasion, however, they rescued the team from wave after wave of Kilkenny attack.  Defensive grit kept Tipperary in the game in the first half and both sides left the field at half-time with 0-9 apiece.

The second-half saw Tipp get the breaks as the vital score of the match had more than a touch of luck about it.  [[Michael Cleary (hurler)|Michael Cleary]], Tipp's ultra accurate free-taker, had been impressive all throughout the year.  Ten minutes into the game he miss-hit a controversial twenty-metre free.  The sliotar skewed into the Kilkenny net at the hill 16 end past a flat-footed Kilkenny defence.  It was the score that gave Tipperary a lift and took the wind out of 'the Cats'’ sails.  Tipperary always had a few points to spare over their rivals after that incident, with [[Pat Fox]] finishing off a wonderful championship campaign with an insurance point that gave his team a merited 1-16 to 0-15 victory.  It was his fifth from play as he collected the man of the match award.  [[Declan Carr]] had the honour of collecting the [[Liam MacCarthy Cup]] on the occasion of Tipperary’s twenty-fourth All-Ireland victory.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.irishtimes.com/newspaper/sport/2010/0901/1224277972067.html|title=Critics silenced as Premier heroes prove their worth|date=2 September 1991|work=The Irish Times|access-date=2010-09-02| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20100902021432/http://www.irishtimes.com/newspaper/sport/2010/0901/1224277972067.html| archive-date= 2 September 2010 | url-status= live}}</ref>

1994.title: 1994 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final
1994.text:
{{Short description|none}} {{Infobox football match | title = 1994 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Final | image = 1994_All-Ireland_Senior_Hurling_Championship_Final_p.jpg | image_size = 250 | event = [[1994 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]] | team1 = [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] | team1association = [[File:Limerick colours.PNG|40px]] | team1score = 2-13 | team2 = [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] | team2association = [[File:Offaly colours.PNG|40px]] | team2score = 3-16 | details = | date = 4 September 1994 | stadium = [[Croke Park]] | city = [[Dublin]] | man_of_the_match1a = [[Brian Whelahan]]{{cite news|url=https://aib.ie/gaa/blog/2018/12/manging-the-gap-with-brian-whelahan|title=Managing the gap with Brian Whelahan|first=Shane|last=Stapleton|date=17 December 2018|quote=Brian Whelahan, more than anyone, came to typify the spirit that saw the Faithful County win a couple of All-Ireland titles in 1994 and 1998. He was man of the match on both occasions…}} | referee = Willie Barrett ([[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]]) | attendance = 54,458 | weather = Dry | previous = [[1993 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1993]] | next = [[1995 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1995]] }} The '''1994 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final''' was the 107th All-Ireland Final and the culmination of the [[1994 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]], an inter-county [[hurling]] tournament for the top teams in Ireland. The match was held at [[Croke Park]], [[Dublin]], on 4 September 1994, between [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] and [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]]. The Munster champions lost to their Leinster opponents on a score line of 3-16 to 2-13. The match is known as 'the five-minute final' due to the sensational comeback by Offaly who scored 2-5 to win the game in the last five minutes.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/the-great-escape-celebrating-the-supreme-heroes-of-94-that-delivered-one-of-the-great-gaa-comebacks-38009389.html |title = The Great Escape - Celebrating the supreme heroes of '94 that delivered one of the great GAA comebacks|date=12 April 2019|work=Irish Independent|access-date=17 April 2019}}{{cite web|url= https://www.gaa.ie/hurling/news/flashback-1994-all-ireland-shc-final-offaly-v-limerick/|title =Flashback: 1994 All-Ireland SHC Final - Offaly v Limerick|date=19 March 2020|work=GAA.ie|access-date=24 March 2020}} ==Summary== With five minutes of normal time remaining, Limerick were leading by 2-13 to 1-11 and looked to be heading to their first title in 21 years when Offaly were awarded a free 20 metres from the goal. Limerick goalkeeper [[Joe Quaid]] later admitted that he was to blame for the resultant goal in that he didn't organise his defence well enough to stop a low-struck free from [[Johnny Dooley (hurler)|Johnny Dooley]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/tale-of-the-sorrowful-mysteries-1.754563|title=Tale of the sorrowful mysteries|date=10 October 2009|publisher=Irish Times|access-date=17 September 2018|first=Keith|last=Duggan}} Quaid was erroneously blamed for Offaly's second goal after what was described as a quick and errant puck-out leading to [[Pat O'Connor (hurler)|Pat O'Connor]] putting Offaly a point ahead with a low shot to the net. Quaid later described the puck-out: "I didn’t rush back to the goals. I went back and picked up the ball, walked behind the goals like I normally would. [[Ger Hegarty|Hegarty]] was out in the middle of the field on his own. I dropped the ball into his hand 70 yards out from goal. He caught the ball and in contact the ball squirted out of his hands." Because the television coverage was still showing a replay of the first goal, very few people got to see the build up to the second and when live transmission was resumed, the sliotar was still dropping towards Pat O'Connor leading people to assume that Quaid rushed his puck-out.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-hurling-home-to-hope-and-hardship-1.1795923|title=Limerick hurling: home to hope and hardship|date=15 May 2014|publisher=Irish Times|access-date=17 September 2018|first=Keith|last=Duggan}} Limerick went on to lose the game by 3-16 to 2-13.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/opinion/yourview/arid-10098744.html|title=Limerick: where broken dreams are a way of life|date=15 August 2009|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=17 September 2018}}{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/offaly-limerick-1994-1653691-Sep2014/|title=20 years ago today Offaly produced THAT All-Ireland final comeback against Limerick|date=4 September 2014|publisher=The 42|access-date=17 September 2018|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}} ==Match details== {{Football box | date = 1994-09-04

O'Connor (0-1). | goals2 = Johnny Dooley (1-4), Joe Dooley (1-2), B. Dooley (0-5), P. O'Connor (1-0), J. Pilkington (0-2), J. Troy (0-1), D. Pilkington (0-1), M. {{Short description|none}} {{Use dmy dates|date=May 2020}} {{Use Irish English|date=May 2020}} {{Infobox football match | title = 1995 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Final | image = | event = [[1995 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]] | team2 = [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] | team2association = [[File:Offaly colours.PNG|40px]] | team1score = 1-13 | team1 = [[Clare GAA|Clare]] | team1association = [[File:Portumna GAA colours.PNG|40px]] | team2score = 2-8 | details = | date = 3 September 1995 | stadium = [[Croke Park]] | city = [[Dublin]] | man_of_the_match1a = [[Seánie McMahon]] | referee = [[Dickie Murphy]] ([[Wexford GAA|Wexford]]) | attendance = 65,092 | weather = Cloudy | previous = [[1994 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1994]] | next = [[1996 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1996]] }} The '''1995 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final''' (sponsored by Guinness) was the 108th All-Ireland Final and the culmination of the [[1995 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]], an inter-county [[hurling]] tournament for the top teams in [[Ireland]]. The match was held at [[Croke Park]], [[Dublin]], on 3 September 1995, between [[Clare GAA|Clare]] and [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]]. The Leinster champions lost to their Munster opponents on a score line of 1-13 to 2-8. It was Clare's first All-Ireland title since 1914.{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/hurling-clare-lay-the-ghost-at-last-1599434.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220501/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/hurling-clare-lay-the-ghost-at-last-1599434.html |archive-date=1 May 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live|title=Hurling: Clare lay the ghost at last |date=2009-09-04|work=The Independent|access-date=2009-11-16 | location=London | first1=Eddie | last1=Wiley}}{{cbignore}} The match was shown live in Ireland on [[RTÉ Two|Network 2]] with match commentary by [[Ger Canning]] with analysis by [[Tomás Mulcahy]]. ==Match details== ===Summary=== Offaly's [[Daithí Regan]] opened the scoring in the game with a long range point into the canal end of the stadium. [[Billy Dooley]] then got a second point for Offaly after a high ball broke to him on the right. [[Seánie McMahon]] got Clare's opening score with a long range point to make the score 0-2 to 0-1 in Offaly's favor. [[Ollie Baker]] scored from a side line ball on the right to put Clare ahead by a point. [[Johnny Pilkington]] got a goal in the second half when he pulled on a loose ball in front of goals that went low and rolled into the net past Clare goalkeeper [[Davy Fitzgerald]]. Clare's goal in the second half came when a long range free from [[Anthony Daly (hurler)|Anthony Daly]] was patted back into play by Offaly goalkeeper [[David Hughes (hurler)|David Hughes]] where it was hit high to the net from the edge of the square by [[Éamonn Taaffe]]. {{football box |date=3 September

Well today that person has been found alive and well, and that person's name is Liam McCarthy".{{cite web|url= https://www.irishexaminer.com/lifestyle/arid-20162483.html|title= This much I know: Anthony Daly|date=30 July 2011|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=4 September 2013}}{{cite book|url= https://books.google.com/books?id=gQ4LIEppWWsC&q=anthony+daly+speech+1995&pg=PT63|title= Raising the Banner|date=April 2011|work=GAA: An Oral History|isbn= 9781845969479|access-date=4 September 2013|last1= Scally|first1= John|publisher= Random House}} ''[[The Sunday Game]]'' (which was broadcast that night) crossed over to the winners hotel in Dublin, with [[Ger Canning]] and [[Marty Morrissey]] interviewing the winning manager [[Ger Loughnane]] and some of the players.{{fact|date=May 2020}} ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== *[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YlePImrU9J4 Match Highlights] *{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20130904181010/https://www.crokepark.ie/Shop-Home/Photos-and-Prints/Match-Programme-Covers/All-Ireland-Hurling-Match-Programme-Covers/Match-programme-cover-for-the-1995-All-Ireland-Hur|title=Match Programme Cover|sec=el}} {{All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship}} [[Category:1995 in hurling|All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final]] [[Category:1990s in Dublin (city)|All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final, 1995]] [[Category:September 1995 sports events in Europe|All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final]] [[Category:All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship finals]] [[Category:GAA finals at Croke Park]] [[Category:Clare county hurling team matches]] [[Category:Offaly county hurling team matches]]

1990.title: 1990 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final
1990.text:
{{Short description|none}} {{Use Hiberno-English|date=July 2024}} {{Use dmy dates|date=June 2020}} {{multiple issues| {{one source|date=April 2020}} {{fanpov|date=May 2010}} {{morefootnotes|date=June 2020}} }} {{Infobox football match | title = 1990 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Final | image = | event = [[1990 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]] | team1 = [[Cork GAA|Cork]] | team1association = [[File:Cork colours.PNG|40px]] | team1score = 5-15 | team2 = [[Galway GAA|Galway]] | team2association = [[File:Galway colours.PNG|40px]] | team2score = 2-21 | details = | date = 2 September 1990 | stadium = [[Croke Park]] | city = [[Dublin]] | man_of_the_match1a = [[Tomás Mulcahy]] | referee = John Moore ([[Waterford GAA|Waterford]]) | attendance = 63,954 | weather = | previous = [[1989 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1989]] | next = [[1991 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1991]] }} The '''1990 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final''' was the 103rd All-Ireland Final and the culmination of the [[1990 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]], an inter-county [[hurling]] tournament for the top teams in [[Ireland]]. The match was held at [[Croke Park]], [[Dublin]], on 2 September 1990, between [[Cork GAA|Cork]] and [[Galway GAA|Galway]]. The Connacht men lost to their Munster opponents on a scoreline of 5-15 to 2-21. The match is regarded as the best championship decider of the decade.{{cite web|url= https://www.gaa.ie/hurling/news/flashback-1990-all-ireland-shc-final-cork-v-galway/|title =Flashback: 1990 All-Ireland SHC Final - Cork v Galway|date=2 April 2020|work=GAA.ie|access-date=16 April 2020}} ==Route to the final== ===Cork=== Cork's senior hurling team made an early start in the 1990 championship. On 20 May the team traveled to [[Austin Stack Park]] in [[Tralee]] and played [[Kerry GAA|Kerry]] in the opening round of the Munster Championship. A score line of 3-16 to 3-7 gave Cork a respectable win, however, the team stumbled at some stages and looked unlikely contenders for Munster and All-Ireland honours. Two weeks later on 3 June Cork played [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] in the Munster semi-final at [[Semple Stadium]] in [[Thurles]]. Waterford had defeated Cork in the championship the previous year and doubts about Cork's team selection surfaced again. In the end Cork made light of the opposition and finished easy winners with a 4-15 to 1-8 victory. Cork's next outing in the championship was a Munster final meeting with arch-rivals [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] at Semple Stadium on 15 July. Tipp, as reigning All-Ireland champions, were installed as the favourites while Cork's problems mounted due to the absence of star players [[Tomás Mulcahy]] and [[Teddy McCarthy]] due to injuries. An infamous interview in which Tipperary manager [[Michael Keating (hurler)|Michael ‘Babs’ Keating]] wrote off Cork's chances by stating that ‘donkeys don’t win derbies’ severely riled the Cork team. It riled the team so much that they played like they had never played before. Cork's centre half-forward [[Mark Foley (Cork hurler)|Mark Foley]] played the game of his life and scored 2-7 from play. Cork won the game by 4-16 to 2-14. All-Ireland hurling semi-final day at [[Croke Park]] was 5 August and Cork faced [[Antrim GAA|Antrim]]. The Ulster men had shocked [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] in the All-Ireland semi-final of 1989 so nothing was left to chance for Cork. In spite of this few people expected an upset and Cork had a reasonable easy 2-20 to 1-13 victory. ===Galway=== Galway, with no provincial championship to participate in advanced directly to the All-Ireland series of games. They opened their championship campaign at Croke Park on 22 July where they played [[London GAA|London]], the All-Ireland ‘B’ champions. Galway had a reasonably comfortable win in their opening game as the exiles fell by 1-23 to 2-11. All-Ireland hurling semi-final day at Croke Park was 5 August and Galway faced [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] in the second game played that day. Offaly were the masters of the Leinster Championship for a third year in-a-row, however, they were out of their depth in the All-Ireland series once again. Again Galway had a comfortable win on a score line of 1-16 to 2-7, however, they had qualified for the All-Ireland final without being tested greatly. ==All-Ireland final== ===Overview=== Sunday 2 September was the date of the 1990 All-Ireland senior hurling final between Cork and Galway. Cork were appearing in their first championship decider since 1986 when they defeated Galway to take the title. Galway were appearing in a fifth All-Ireland final in six years and were hoping to take a third title in four years having defeated [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] and [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] respectively in 1987 and 1988. At the time, Galway had never beaten Cork in an All-Ireland final. The attendance at the match was 63,954. ===Match report=== At 3:30pm referee John Moore of Waterford threw in the sliothar and the game was on in the 103rd All-Ireland hurling final. Straight away Galway went on the attack after just ten seconds of play, however, [[Michael McGrath (hurler)|Michael McGrath]]’s shot failed to hit the target and he registered his team's first wide of the day. Immediately after the puck-out the play switched to the opposite end of the field where the sliothar broke to [[Kevin Hennessy]]. He made no mistake in slotting it into the Galway net for a goal after just 48 seconds of play. The Galway men found it difficult to settle in the game, however, captain [[Joe Cooney]] sent over a point to open the Galway scoring account. Both sides exchanged wides over the next few minutes of play before [[John Fitzgibbon (Cork hurler)|John Fitzgibbon]] stretched Cork's lead again with a point. Joe Cooney responded with a point from a trick angle by the sideline before [[Pete Finnerty]]’s expertly taken sideline cut was stopped on the goal line and cleared by goalkeeper [[Ger Cunningham]]. Joe Cooney quickly tapped over another point before [[Tony Keady]] scored an inspirational point following a great solo run from his usual position at centre half-back. Kevin Hennessy gave the Cork men a two-point cushion once again when he slotted over a free before Joe Cooney had the chance to level the game. Both his shots went wide. Kevin Hennessy was on hand again in the thirteenth minute to send over another free to give Cork some more breathing space. Not long after this the sliothar fell to Galway forward [[Noel Lane (Galway hurler)|Noel Lane]] who was relatively unmarked in front of the Cork goal. There was no doubt about it that he was going for a goal; however, his shot just went over the crossbar for a point. Kevin Hennessy cancelled this point almost immediately when he sent over a point of his own after receiving a facial injury. [[Ger FitzGerald (hurler)|Ger FitzGerald]] got his name on the scoring sheet soon afterwards when he put his team four points clear of their opponents. With the game running away from them the Galway men clicked into gear and began the fight back. [[Martin Naughton (hurler)|Martin Naughton]] got things back on track with a point before Joe Cooney added to his tally with Galway’s first goal of the day. His first shot on target was blocked by Ger Cunningham; however, the rebound allowed him to kick the sliothar into the net to level the scores. [[Éanna Ryan]] pointed in the twentieth minute to give Galway the lead for the first time in the game. Joe Cooney soon chipped in with another point to give his side a two-point lead. Cork’s response was not an accurate one as [[Tony O'Sullivan]] sent a free wide before Noel Lane rifled over another point. Once again it was clear from his facial expressions that Lane was going for a goal. Nonetheless, his effort had the Galway fans on their feet cheering his name to the tune of ‘Olé, Olé, Olé, Olé.’ Both sides exchanged wides following this before [[Teddy McCarthy]] sent over a point to claw one back for ‘the Rebels.’ Noel Lane added to his tally with another point before the game witnessed one of its first controversial moments. Joe Cooney was heading towards the Cork goal with one thing on his mind. He passed the sliothar to Éanna Ryan who tapped it into the net for another goal. Unfortunately, the goal was disallowed as the referee had blown his whistle for a foul on Joe Cooney. The goal didn't stand; however, Cooney converted the free without difficulty. Cork's woes continued with [[Jim Cashman (hurler)|Jim Cashman]] missing a long-range free before Martin Naughton and Joe Cooney both recorded two more points. The finals core of the half was an absolute delightful one as Cork's [[Kevin McGuckin]] sent a sideline cut straight over the crossbar for a point. After the first thirty-five minutes Galway had a 1-13 to 1-8 lead. Immediately after the restart Cork went on the attack, however, their efforts came to nothing. It was Michael McGrath of Galway who registered the first point of the second half as his side stretched their lead even further. [[Anthony Cunningham]] was the last Galway forward to get his name on the scoring sheet when he sent over a point to give his team a lead of six. Cork needed a new plan of attack at this stage and a positional switch of Tomás Mulcahy to the half-forward line paid dividends when he sent over Cork's first point of the second-half. [[Michael Coleman (hurler)|Michael Coleman]] cancelled out this point with one of his own before Kevin Hennessy put another free over the crossbar for Cork. Martin Naughton pointed for Galway before the forwards launched an all-out attack ob Ger Cunningham's goal once again. This attack came to nothing and Cunningham was able to clear the sliothar away down the field towards Tomás Mulcahy. With nine minutes gone in the second-half Cork were given a major boost when Mulcahy rifled a shot into the Galway net for a goal. Both sides exchanged wides after this score before the second turning point of the game occurred. Martin Naughton had the sliothar balanced on his hurley and broke away from his marker and headed for goal. His shot, however, was saved by Ger Cunningham's face and went wide. While a 65-metre free should have been awarded Cunningham was allowed to puck the sliothar out as normal. This set up another Cork attack with Tony O’Sullivan clawing back a point for Cork. Three more wides followed, one for Galway and two for Cork, before [[Mark Foley (Cork hurler)|Mark Foley]] pointed in what was only his sixth championship game. Both sides exchanged further wides before Cork gained some momentum. Another save and a clearance by Ger Cunningham set up another Cork attack at the other end of the field. Kevin Hennessy collected the sliothar on his hurley and headed for a goal. A pass to Mark Foley gave Cork a much needed lift as Foley rifled the sliothar into the net for a Cork lead. Immediately after the puck-out Galway drew level again courtesy of an Éanna Ryan point. Teddy McCarthy responded for Cork with an inspirational point that he scored over his shoulder and not even facing the goal. Up at the other end of the field Noel Lane leveled the scores again when his shot on goal went straight over the crossbar for the third time. Galway decided to freshen up things for the final few minutes of play as Anthony Cunningham made way for the veteran goal-scorer [[Brendan Lynskey]]. While Lynskey's introduction was designed to give Galway a lift the exact opposite happened. The sliothar flew down the field to [[John Fitzgibbon (Cork hurler)|John Fitzgibbon]] who made no mistake in sending his shot straight into the net. It was his fifth goal of the championship. Less than ninety seconds later the sliothar found its way to Fitzgibbon again who made no mistake in sending in his second goal of the day. Straight away after the puck-out Galway turned defence into attack when Brendan Lynskey scored a goal to reduce Cork's lead to three points once again. With six minutes left in this see-saw All-Ireland final no side was celebrating prematurely. Tomás Mulcahy gave Cork some respite again when he sent over another point, however, Martin Naughton fought back immediately when he pointed for Galway. A mistake at this stage of the game could prove costly as both sides were so close to victory. Tony O’Sullivan gave Cork a four-point lead again before Joe Cooney, one of the start players of the game, sent over a point for Galway and the final score of the day. A short few seconds later the referee blew the final whistle and Cork were the All-Ireland champions of 1990 on a score line of 5-15 to 2-21. ===Statistics=== {{football box |date=1990-09-02

1999.text:
{{Short description|none}} {{Use dmy dates|date=October 2020}} {{Use Irish English|date=October 2020}} {{Infobox football match | title = 1999 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Final | image = | event = [[1999 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]] | team1 = [[Cork county hurling team|Cork]] | team1association = [[File:Colours of Cork.svg|40px]] | team1score = 0-13 | team2 = [[Kilkenny county hurling team|Kilkenny]] | team2association = [[File:Colours of Kilkenny.svg|40px]] | team2score = 0-12 | details = | date = 12 September 1999 | stadium = [[Croke Park]] | city = [[Dublin]] | man_of_the_match1a = [[Brian Corcoran]]{{cite news|url=https://www.echolive.ie/corksport/arid-41113678.html|title=Jimmy Barry-Murphy rates Brian Corcoran as the best player he worked with|first=Denis|last=Hurley|date=12 April 2023|quote=Cork manager Jimmy Barry-Murphy and man of the match Brian Corcoran celebrate after the win over Tipperary in the 1999 All-Ireland SHC final.}} | referee = [[Pat O'Connor (referee)|Pat O'Connor]] ([[Limerick GAA|Limerick]]) | attendance = 62,989 | weather = Rain | previous = [[1998 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|1998]] | next = [[2000 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2000]] }} The '''1999 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final''' was the 112th All-Ireland Final and the culmination of the [[1999 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]], an inter-county [[hurling]] tournament for the top teams in [[Ireland]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/championship-flashback-all-ireland-shc-final-september-1999/26466919.html|title=Championship Flashback: All-Ireland SHC final, September 1999|date=3 August 2008|website=Irish Independent}} The match was held at [[Croke Park]], [[Dublin]], on 12 September 1999, between {{GG|Cork|hurling}} and {{GG|Kilkenny|hurling}}. The Leinster champions lost to their Munster opponents on a score line of 0-13 to 0-12.{{Cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41439049.html|title=Jimmy Barry-Murphy to lead out Cork jubilee team at Croke Park|first=John|last=Fogarty|date=18 July 2024|website=Irish Examiner}} Cork had trailed by a point at half time, 0-5 to 0-4, after playing the better hurling. Then Kilkenny pulled into a four-point lead in the second half, they were 0-11 to 0-8 ahead before Cork scored five unanswered points with Kilkenny only managing one more point from a [[Henry Shefflin]] free. Cork, captained by [[Mark Landers]] and managed by [[Jimmy Barry-Murphy]] held out to win their first All Ireland title since [[1990 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1990]].{{cite web|url= https://www.gaa.ie/news/flashback-cluiche-ceannais-iomana-na-heireann-1999-corcaigh-v-cill-chainnigh/|title=Flashback – Cluiche Ceannais Iomána na hÉireann 1999: Corcaigh v Cill Chainnigh|date=12 March 2021|work=GAA.ie|accessdate= 16 March 2021}} It was Cork's 28th All-Ireland hurling title, and the first final in history without a [[Scoring in Gaelic games|goal]].{{cite news|url=http://www.rte.ie/news/1999/0912/gaa.html|title=GAA: All-Ireland Hurling Final: Cork 0-13 Kilkenny 0-12|work=RTÉ News|date=12 September 1999}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.echolive.ie/corksport/arid-41437405.html|title=Seánie McGrath happy to relive glory days of 1999: Looking back, it was a magical time|date=18 July 2024|website=echo live}} {{footballbox | date = 12 September 1999

1989.title: 1989 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final
1989.text:
{{Short description|none}} {{Use dmy dates|date=June 2017}} {{Infobox football match | title = 1989 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Final | image = 1989 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final Programme.jpg | image_size = 250 | event = [[1989 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]] | team1 = [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] | team1association = [[File:Tipperary colours.PNG|40px]] | team1score = 4-24 | team2 = [[Antrim GAA|Antrim]] | team2association = [[File:Antrim colours.PNG|40px]] | team2score = 3-9 | details = | date = 3 September 1989 | stadium = [[Croke Park]] | city = [[Dublin]] | man_of_the_match1a = [[Nicky English]]{{cite news|url=https://tippfm.com/featured/nicky-english-inducted-gaa-hall-fame-2/|title=Nicky English inducted into GAA Hall of Fame|date=17 September 2019|quote=The Lattin-Cullen clubman and 6 time All Star won All Irelands with the Premier County in 1989 – where he won man of the match – and again in 1991…}} | referee = P. Delaney ([[Laois GAA|Laois]]) | attendance = 65,496 | weather = Sunny | previous = [[1988 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1988]] | next = [[1990 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1990]] }} The '''1989 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final''' was the 102nd All-Ireland Final and the culmination of the [[1989 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]], an inter-county [[hurling]] tournament for the top teams in [[Ireland]]. The match was held at [[Croke Park]], [[Dublin]], on 3 September 1989, between [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]], managed by [[Michael Keating (hurler)|Bab's Keating]] and [[Antrim GAA|Antrim]], managed by [[Jim Nelson (hurling manager)|Jim Nelson]]. The game was shown live in Ireland on [[RTÉ Two|Network 2]] with match commentary provided by [[Ger Canning]] and comments throughout provided by [[Jimmy Magee]]. The Ulster champions lost to their Munster opponents on a scoreline of 4-24 to 3-9.{{cite web|url=http://www.gaainfo.com/comp.php?co=intercounty&year=1989&compno=1|title=1989 All Ireland Hurling Championship|work=Gaainfo.com|access-date=6 March 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120921144807/http://www.gaainfo.com/comp.php?co=intercounty&year=1989&compno=1|archive-date=21 September 2012|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}} Tipperary had led at halftime by 1-13 to 0-5, with their goal coming from Declan Ryan, who scored when his high long-range shot for a point hit the hurley of the Antrim goalkeeper [[Niall Patterson]] on its way into the net after 18 minutes.{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1CGLyHwB8WM|title=1989 All Ireland Hurling Final |work=Youtube|access-date=6 March 2012}} The game is notable for a number of reasons. This was Antrim's second-ever appearance in an All-Ireland final, some forty-six years after they lost to [[Cork GAA|Cork]] at the same stage of the championship. [[Nicky English]] set a scoring record for a single player in the modern era as he notched up 2-12 to win his first All-Ireland Senior medal. The victory for Tipperary, eighteen years after their last in [[1971 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1971]], also preserved the county's unique record of winning an All-Ireland title in every decade of the GAA's existence. Tipperary was captained by [[Bobby Ryan (hurler)|Bobby Ryan]].{{cite web|url= https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2020/0517/1138947-bobby-ryans-1989-all-ireland-winning-speech/|title =Bobby Ryan's 1989 All-Ireland winning speech|date=17 May 2020|work=RTE Sport|access-date=18 May 2020}} {{TOC left}} ==Match details== {{football box | date = 1988-09-01

1987.title: 1987 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final
1987.text:
{{Short description|none}} {{Use dmy dates|date=May 2025}} {{Infobox football match | title = 1987 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Final | image = 1987 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final programme.jpg | image_size = 250 | event = [[1987 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]] | team1 = [[Galway GAA|Galway]] | team1association = [[File:Galway colours.PNG|40px]] | team1score = 1–12 | team2 = [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] | team2association = [[File:Kilkenny colours.PNG|40px]] | team2score = 0–9 | details = | date = 6 September 1987 | stadium = [[Croke Park]] | city = Dublin | man_of_the_match1a = | referee = [[Terence Murray (referee)|Terence Murray]] ([[Limerick GAA|Limerick]]) | attendance = 65,596 | weather = | previous = [[1986 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1986]] | next = [[1988 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1988]] }} The '''1987 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final''' was the 100th All-Ireland Final and the culmination of the [[1987 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]], an inter-county [[hurling]] tournament for the top teams in Ireland. The match was held at [[Croke Park]], Dublin, on 6 September 1987, between [[Galway GAA|Galway]] and [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]]. The Leinster champions lost to the Connacht men on a score line of 1–12 to 0–9. It was Galway's third Final success (1923 and 1980 being the other victories). They came in to this game having lost fourteen previous finals. Cyril Farrell and Pat Henderson managed Galway and Kilkenny respectively. Galway went on to successfully defend their title the following year, again captained by Conor Hayes.{{Cite web |last=Cahill |first=Jackie |date=2015-09-03 |title=It's 27 years since Galway won the All-Ireland hurling title…but where are they now? |url=https://www.the42.ie/galway-all-ireland-hurling-1988-2308304-Sep2015/ |access-date=2023-01-30 |website=The42 |language=en}} {{TOC left}} {{Clear}} ==Match== ===Summary=== he half-time score was Galway 0.5 to 0.4 Kilkenny. 41st-minute substitute Noel Lane, set up by Joe Cooney after a long solo run by Eanna Ryan, scored the only goal of the game in the 63rd minute to make it 1.11 to 0.9. Kilkenny's first score from play arrived in the first minute of the 2nd half. Tony Keady scored the last point of the game in the 69th minute. Conor Hayes, aged 29, of the Kiltormer club, captained the Galway team. Ger Canning, on RTE television commentary called it "one of the poorest All-Ireland hurling finals (he'd) seen". This completed a League and Championship double for Galway. ===Match details=== {{Football box | date = 1987-09-06

He scored three-goals in a man of the match performance…}} | referee = [[Michael Wadding (referee)|Michael Wadding]] (Waterford) | attendance = 81,765 | weather = Dull with Light Rain

Met Éireann, Daily data 5/9/10 | previous = [[2009 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2009]] | next = [[2011 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2011]] }} The '''2010 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final''' was the 113th All-Ireland Final and the culmination of the [[2010 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]], an inter-county [[hurling]] tournament for the top teams in Ireland. The match was held at [[Croke Park]], Dublin, on 5 September 2010 and was a repeat of the [[2009 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2009]] final with [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] taking on [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]]. Kilkenny were attempting to win a fifth All-Ireland title in-a-row, a feat never achieved in either hurling or [[Gaelic football]]. This has been referred to as the "Drive for Five".[http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2010/0904/kilkenny_tipperary1.html Kilkenny v Tipperary SHC final preview] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100907000053/http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2010/0904/kilkenny_tipperary1.html |date=7 September 2010 }}. 4 September 2010. The game was watched by more than 80,000 in the stadium as well as a global audience on TV, radio, etc.[http://www.rte.ie/news/2010/0905/hurling.html Kilkenny aim for historic All-Ireland title]. 5 September 2010. The Final attracted the highest ever Irish viewership for an [[All-Ireland Hurling Final|All Ireland Hurling Final]] peaking at 1.236 million viewers in the final minutes of the match, with an average audience of over one million people during the game which was shown live on [[RTÉ2]].{{cite web|url=http://clane.newsfinch.ie/sport-news/rte-highest-ever-viewership-for-hurling-final/ |title=RTÉ – Highest ever viewership for Hurling Final |date=2010-09-13 |work=clane.news finch.ie |access-date=2010-10-07 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110721125516/http://clane.newsfinch.ie/sport-news/rte-highest-ever-viewership-for-hurling-final/ |archive-date=21 July 2011 }} The match was won by Tipperary by a score of 4–17 to 1–18.{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/rampant-tipp-deny-cats-immortality-2326052.html|title=Rampant Tipp deny Cats immortality|date=2010-09-05|work=Irish Independent|access-date=2010-09-06}}{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/northern_ireland/gaelic_games/8970482.stm|title=Kilkenny 1–18 4–17 Tipperary |date=2010-09-05|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=2010-10-07| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20100909063807/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/northern_ireland/gaelic_games/8970482.stm| archive-date= 9 September 2010 | url-status= live}} ==Pre-match== [[File:Croke park.jpg|thumb|300px|[[Croke Park]], the venue for the 2010 final]] ===Background=== Kilkenny were Leinster champions, having beaten [[Dublin GAA|Dublin]] and [[Galway GAA|Galway]] to earn that title. They beat [[Cork GAA|Cork]] in the semi-final on 8 August 2010.{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/northern_ireland/gaelic_games/8895952.stm|title=Kilkenny 3–22 0–19 Cork|date=2010-08-08|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=2010-08-08}}{{cite web|url=http://www.kerryman.ie/breaking-news/sport/kilkenny-crush-cork-to-make-final-2289277.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111003093010/http://www.kerryman.ie/breaking-news/sport/kilkenny-crush-cork-to-make-final-2289277.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=3 October 2011|title=Kilkenny crush Cork to make final|date=2010-08-08|work=[[The Kerryman]]|access-date=2010-08-08}} Tipperary lost to Cork in the first round of the [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster championship]] and went into the All Ireland Qualifiers, where they beat [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]], [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] and Galway, before beating [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] in their semi-final on 15 August 2010.{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120910130322/http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2010/0815/gaa_championship_15_august_live_text.html?gaa|title=As it Happened – Tipperary 3–19 Waterford 1–18}}. 15 August 2010. Kilkenny were bidding for their 22nd successive championship win and had not lost a game since losing to [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 2005|2005 All-Ireland semi-final]]. In 2009 Kilkenny became the first county since Cork in 1941 – 1944 to win the four in a row and was bidding for their 33rd All Ireland title. Tipperary, who lost to Kilkenny by five points in the previous years final were seeking their first All-Ireland title since [[2001 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2001]] and their 26th title in all.{{cite web |url=http://www.tipperary.gaa.ie/cgi-bin/newsdisplay.cgi?rm=viewListing&plugin_data_id=82333&site_id=185 |title=All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final – Tipperary vs. Kilkenny – Match Reports |date=2010-09-05 |work=Tipperary.gaa.ie |access-date=2010-10-07 }}{{dead link|date=June 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}{{cite web|url=http://munster.gaa.ie/2010/09/05/all-ireland-senior-hurling-championship-final-3/|title=2010 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final Preview|work=munster.gaa.ie|access-date=2011-01-13}} The pre-match betting made Kilkenny favourites, with [[Bookmaker]] ''[[Paddy Power]]'' giving odds of 4/11 on a Kilkenny win, Tipperary were 5/2 to win with a draw at 12/1. Paddy Power also pledged to refund a wide range of losing bets on the match if Kilkenny were beaten, risking a potential five figure refund should Tipperary reverse the form book.{{cite web|url=http://www.bettingpro.com/category/GAA/All-Ireland-Hurling-Final-Money-Back-Offer-from-Paddy-Power-201009010039/|title=All Ireland Hurling Final Money Back Offer from Paddy Power|date=2010-09-01|work=bettingpro.com|access-date=2011-01-13}} Before the senior final, Kilkenny beat [[Clare GAA|Clare]] in the [[All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|minor]] hurling final.{{cite web|url=http://www.setanta.com/ie/Articles/2010/09/05/MHC-Final-Clare-v-Kilkenny/gnid-76275/ |title=Kilkenny youngsters claim minor crown |date=2010-09-05 |work=[[Setanta Sports]] |access-date=2010-09-05 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120329054404/http://www.setanta.com/ie/Articles/2010/09/05/MHC-Final-Clare-v-Kilkenny/gnid-76275/ |archive-date=29 March 2012 }}[http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2010/0905/kilkenny_clare.html Kilkenny 2–10 Clare 0–14] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100906101633/http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2010/0905/kilkenny_clare.html |date=6 September 2010 }}. 5 September 2010. ===Team news=== Much of the pre-match build-up centred around the fitness of Kilkenny's [[Henry Shefflin]], who had torn his [[cruciate ligament]] in the semi-final against Cork, an injury which generally takes several months to recover from. Shefflin attended noted physiotherapist, [[Gerard Hartmann]], who specialised in such injuries, and recovered to such a degree that within 3 weeks, he took a full part in a Kilkenny training session watched by around 8,000 fans, without noticeable discomfort.{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/8000-turn-up-as-king-henry-returns-to-training-2312038.html|title=8000 turn up as King Henry returns to training|work=[[Irish Independent]]|date=2010-08-26|access-date=2010-09-06}} Shefflin was then selected to start the All Ireland Final,{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/shefflin-to-start-2324639.html|title=Shefflin to start|work=[[Irish Independent]]|date=2010-09-04|access-date=2010-09-06}} but due in part to slippery conditions on the day, pulled up after 12 minutes in obvious pain, and had to be substituted. Tipperary manager [[Liam Sheedy]] opted to stick with the same team that had defeated Waterford in the semi-final, the team contained eleven of the players that started the [[2009 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2009]] final.{{cite web|url=http://www.irishtimes.com/sports/gaa/2010/0902/1224278121932.html|title=No changes for Sheedy and Tipp|date=2010-09-02|work=The Irish Times |access-date=2010-09-28}}{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2010/0902/tipperary.html |title=Tipperary name unchanged side for final |date=2010-09-02 |work=RTÉ Sport |access-date=2011-01-13 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100903120053/http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2010/0902/tipperary.html |archive-date=3 September 2010 }} ===Referee=== [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]]-based referee [[Michael Wadding (referee)|Michael Wadding]] was named as the referee for the 2010 All-Ireland final on 17 August 2010. The [[Roanmore GAA|Roanmore]] club man, who has been refereeing for twenty-one years, has previously taken charge of All-Ireland championship deciders at minor level in 1997 and at under-21 level in 2003. He was also the referee for the 2010 Leinster final between Kilkenny and [[Galway GAA|Galway]]. Wadding, however, has been involved in three previous All-Ireland finals at senior level – twice as stand-by referee and once as a linesman. The GAA opted against appointing high-profile referees as umpires for the final, as had been suggested in the wake of the controversial end to the [[2010 Leinster Senior Football Championship Final]] between [[Meath GAA|Meath]] and [[Louth GAA|Louth]]. Instead, Wadding will use his usual team of umpires from his native club – Noel Cowman, Pat Byrne, Thomas Martin and [[Noel Crowley (hurler, born 1962)|Noel Crowley]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20128140.html|title=Wadding 'thrilled' to ref final|date=2010-08-18|work=[[Irish Examiner]]|access-date=2010-08-20}} ==Match summary== ===First half=== A [[Henry Shefflin]] free cancelled out Eoin Kelly's opening score before two more Kelly points were added to by a goal by [[Lar Corbett]] after 13 minutes. Corbett shrugged off [[Noel Hickey]] to field a long ball from [[Shane McGrath (hurler)|Shane McGrath]] before lashing the ball to the net from close range. John O'Brien added to Tipperary's lead after Brendan Cummins had saved a goal attempt at the other end by TJ Reid, Henry Shefflin lasted only 13 minutes as he succumbed to his cruciate ligament injury, which saw [[Michael Rice (hurler)|Michael Rice]] introduced as Tipperary increased their lead to 1–6 to 0–3 after 19 minutes following [[Brendan Maher]] and Eoin Kelly points. Richie Power hit 1–5 of Kilkenny's remaining first-half tally of 1–6 including a 32nd-minute goal after [[Eoin Larkin]]'s thrust into the Tipperary defence. Tipperary's six-point lead of the 30th minute dwindled to one point at half time as Kilkenny's dominance began to translate into scores. Tipperary led by 1–10 to 1–9 at half time.{{cite web|url= https://www.gaa.ie/hurling/news/flashback-2010-all-ireland-shc-final-tipperary-v-kilkenny/|title =Flashback: 2010 All-Ireland SHC Final: Tipperary v Kilkenny|date=25 March 2020|work=GAA.ie|access-date=26 March 2020}} ===Second half=== [[TJ Reid]] leveled the scores straight after the interval but Tipperary responded with 2–1 in four minutes as Eoin Kelly's free was added to by goals from Lar Corbett and [[Noel McGrath (hurler)|Noel McGrath]]. Corbett lashed his second goal to the roof of the net after being set up by a pass on the run from Noel McGrath. McGrath's instinct to follow up a long ball into the Kilkenny goalmouth proved inspired as he scrambled the ball to the net from close range for his goal. Kilkenny then hit four unanswered points to leave one point between the sides with 16 minutes left. Substitute [[Séamus Callanan]] then fired over successive points in the 59th and 62nd minutes, followed shortly afterwards by an Eoin Kelly free to extend Tipperary's lead to six points. Richie Power and [[John Mulhall (hurler)|John Mulhall]] then added Kilkenny points before substitutes [[Benny Dunne]] and then [[Séamus Hennessy (hurler, born 1989)|Séamus Hennessy]] scored long-range points for Tipperary . Lar Corbett then got his third goal in injury time from a pass from Patrick Maher to seal the county's 26th [[Liam MacCarthy Cup]].{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2010/0905/gaa_championship_05_september_live_text.html |title=As it Happened – Tipperary 4–17 Kilkenny 1–18 |date=2010-09-05 |work=RTÉ Sport |access-date=2010-10-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100921024947/http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2010/0905/gaa_championship_05_september_live_text.html |archive-date=21 September 2010 |url-status=dead }} Tipperary's final tally of 4–17 is the biggest total ever scored against Kilkenny in a 70-minute final (the 5–17 for Tipperary in [[1971 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1971]] was in an 80-minute decider). Lar Corbett became only the second player in modern times and first since [[Eddie O'Brien (hurler)|Eddie O'Brien]] in [[1970 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1970]] for Cork to score a hat-trick in a final.{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/sheedys-patience-a-virtue-for-tipp-2334600.html|title=Sheedy's patience a virtue for Tipp|date=2010-09-12|work=Irish Independent|access-date=2010-10-07}} Tipperary's win continued their unique achievement of having won a Senior Hurling All-Ireland in every decade since the [[Gaelic Athletic Association|GAA]]'s foundation in 1884. ==Match details== {{Football box |date = 5 September 2010
