Thomas Martin |} ==Trophy presentation== This was the first final in many years where there was no [[pitch invasion]] by the fans at the full-time whistle. This was because of a new [[barricade]] which prevents fans on [[Hill 16 (Croke Park)|Hill 16]] from entering the pitch.{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=134941|title=McKenna confident of no pitch invasion|date=2010-09-04|work=Hoganstand|access-date=2010-10-07}} {{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2010/0807/crokepark.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120910183754/http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2010/0807/crokepark.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=2012-09-10 |title=GAA agree to raise Hill 16 barrier |date=2010-08-07 |work=RTÉ Sport |access-date=2010-10-07 }} The trophy was presented from the [[Croke Park|Hogan stand]] to Tipperary captain [[Eoin Kelly (Tipperary hurler)|Eoin Kelly]] by GAA president [[Christy Cooney]]. Immediately after Kelly's acceptance speech, Tipperary substitute [[Pat Kerwick]] sang '[[The Galtee Mountain Boy]]'.{{cite web|url=http://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/columnists/tony-considine/tipperarys-tactic-win-every-ball-every-battle-129993.html|title=Tipperary's tactic? Win every ball, every battle |date=2001-09-06|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=2011-01-13}} The Tipperary team then paraded the cup around the stadium in a lap of honour. ==Man of the Match== Lar Corbett was named the All Ireland hurling final 'Man of the Match' by the ''[[The Sunday Game|Sunday Game]]'' panel. Other nominees for the award were Tipperary left back [[Pádraic Maher]] and centre forward [[Noel McGrath (hurler)|Noel McGrath]].{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2010/0905/manofthematch.html |title=Corbett is All-Ireland 'Man of the Match' |date=2010-09-05 |work=RTÉ Sport |access-date=2010-10-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101009144445/http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2010/0905/manofthematch.html |archive-date=9 October 2010 |url-status=dead }} The award was presented to Corbett at the Tipperary victory banquet in Dublin's [[Burlington Hotel (Dublin)|Burlington Hotel]] on the night of the final, and was judged by panel members [[Dónal O'Grady]], [[Pete Finnerty]] and [[Michael Duignan (hurler)|Michael Duignan]].{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=135011|title=Corbett is RTE's Man of the Match|date=2010-09-06|work=Hoganstand|access-date=2010-10-07}} ==Reaction== Kilkenny manager [[Brian Cody]] admitted that his Kilkenny team were second best to a 'driven, spirited, genuine and full of hurling' Tipperary in the All-Ireland final,'We have no excuses and no begrudgery in the slightest. No doubt about it, the better team won the All-Ireland final' he said.{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2010/0905/codyb.html |title=Cody – Cats second best to 'driven' Tipperary |date=2010-09-05 |work=RTÉ Sport |access-date=2010-09-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101008195706/http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2010/0905/codyb.html |archive-date=8 October 2010 |url-status=dead }} Tipperary manager [[Liam Sheedy]] was delighted with his team's performance saying "Powerful. Great bunch. they are three years in the journey, there has been a lot of twists and turns and highs and lows. First week in June and a lot of people said we didn’t do qualifiers. I think we saw today what this team could do. We felt today that we were in a very good position. Whether you like it or not, five-in-a-row brings its own pressures. We needed 33 players to do this. I am delighted for that group because I feel they have shipped a lot of criticism unfairly. I am a Tipperary man and a proud one and we put everything we had into this".{{cite web|url=http://www.irishtimes.com/newspaper/sport/2010/0906/1224278289206.html|title=I think we saw today what this team could do|date=2010-09-06|work=The Irish Times |access-date=2010-10-07| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20100915014933/http://www.irishtimes.com/newspaper/sport/2010/0906/1224278289206.html| archive-date= 15 September 2010 | url-status= live}} Tipperary goalkeeper [[Brendan Cummins (Tipperary hurler)|Brendan Cummins]] said "This time last year we were sinking, we were really disappointed after losing the final. This year makes it all worthwhile, I have huge belief in this group, huge trust in this family, I just knew the lads and I knew by the looks on their faces in that losing dressing-room last year. "My aim all year was to win the semi-final because I felt if we won the semi-final, no one would stop us in the final. Kilkenny are a super team, but I knew if the guys got back into that arena after what happened last year they wouldn't leave it go."{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/this-is-the-top-of-the-world-its-amazing-tells-donnchadh-boyle-how-tipp-fulfiled-their-childhood-dreams-2327325.html|title='This is the top of the world. It's amazing' |date=2010-09-07|work=Irish Independent|access-date=2010-09-28}} Hat trick scorer Lar Corbett said after the game "It is no good coming up here and scoring three goals and losing to Kilkenny, the win, that is what it is all about. It is the whole year wrapped up in 70 minutes. What can you say? It is unbelievable".{{cite web|url=http://www.irishtimes.com/newspaper/sport/2010/0906/1224278289311.html|title=The win. It was all about the win, says Corbett|date=2010-09-06|work=The Irish Times |access-date=2010-10-07| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20100915014908/http://www.irishtimes.com/newspaper/sport/2010/0906/1224278289311.html| archive-date= 15 September 2010 | url-status= live}} [[The Sunday Game|Sunday Game]] analyst [[Cyril Farrell]] thought that Henry Shefflin's injury was a serious setback for Kilkenny, writing in the ''[[Irish Independent]]'' he said "credit where it's due, this was a marvellous performance by Tipp, they did to Kilkenny what the Cats have done to so many teams over the years by keeping the pace and intensity at a high level and by crowding the ball carrier".{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/cyril-farrell-hope-springs-eternal-after-tipp-take-crown-2333731.html|title=Cyril Farrell: Hope springs eternal after Tipp take crown|date=2010-09-11|work=Irish Independent|access-date=2010-10-07}} Former Tipperary player and manager [[Nicky English]] writing in the ''[[Irish Times]]'' thoughtthat Tipperary got a day when everything went right and the few breaks that any team needs, "Tipperary were quite magnificent in the intensity and skill they brought to Croke Park yesterday to finally prove that Kilkenny, a great team, weren’t invincible".{{cite web|url=http://www.irishtimes.com/newspaper/sport/2010/0906/1224278289179.html|title=The Premier hit their peak on the biggest day|date=2010-09-06|work=The Irish Times |access-date=2010-10-07| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20100918120018/http://www.irishtimes.com/newspaper/sport/2010/0906/1224278289179.html| archive-date= 18 September 2010 | url-status= live}} Former Tipperary manager [[Michael Keating (hurler)|Babs Keating]], speaking on ''[[Newstalk]]'''s Breakfast Show defended his criticism of Liam Sheedy earlier during the season and claimed the Tipperary management has benefited from his controversial second stint in charge. "Maybe I passed a few comments about Liam Sheedy and the management structure based on what I went through in Tipperary and I made difficult decisions which might have helped Liam Sheedy in the success he had, Keating also stated that the win had dwarfed his own managerial victories and that of Nicky English in 2001. "It probably compares up there if not ahead of those wins in so far as that everyone feared Kilkenny and their dominance. This was a great watermark for the game of hurling."{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20130053.html|title=Babs: Sheedy benefited from my efforts|date=2010-09-07|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=2010-11-01}} ==Civic reception== The Tipperary team arrived back to [[Thurles]] by train the next evening after the traditional stop at Our Ladies Children's Hospital with the Cup earlier in the day. They then boarded an open top bus for the journey to the reception at [[Semple Stadium]] where an estimated 40,000 supporters turned out to welcome the team home to a rainy Thurles.{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2010/0906/tipperary.html |title=Huge crowds welcome Tipperary home |date=2010-09-06 |work=RTÉ Sport |access-date=2010-10-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101009055058/http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2010/0906/tipperary.html |archive-date=9 October 2010 |url-status=dead }} {{cite web|url=http://www.irishtimes.com/newspaper/ireland/2010/0906/1224278286879.html|title='Home of hurling' prepares for party|date=2010-09-06|work=The Irish Times |access-date=2010-09-28}} There was another huge crowd in [[Mullinahone]] the night after when Eoin Kelly, the first southern Tipperary man to captain Tipperary to All-Ireland senior success, brought the cup home.{{cite web|url=http://www.nationalist.ie/13447/Tipperary-whirlwind-blows-away-Kilkenny.6518656.jp |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120909041846/http://www.nationalist.ie/13447/Tipperary-whirlwind-blows-away-Kilkenny.6518656.jp |url-status=dead |archive-date=2012-09-09 |title=Tipperary whirlwind blows away Kilkenny dreams |date=2010-09-09 |work=The Nationalist |access-date=2010-10-07 }} ==Awards== The nominations for the 2010 [[GAA All Stars Awards]] were announced on 24 September 2010. Tipperary had 14 players nominated for awards, winning captain Eoin Kelly was going for his sixth All-Star while final hat-trick scorer Lar Corbett was hoping to pick up his second award. Henry Shefflin was on course for a record 10th All-Star after also being nominated for a ninth successive time along with 11 other Kilkenny players. He was hoping to surpass the record jointly held by his fellow county-man [[DJ Carey]] and former Kerry footballer [[Pat Spillane]], whom he joined on nine awards in 2009.{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2010/0924/hurlingallstars.html |title=Tipperary top hurling All-Stars nominations |date=2010-09-24 |work=RTÉ Sport |access-date=2010-09-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100926200414/http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2010/0924/hurlingallstars.html |archive-date=26 September 2010 |url-status=dead }} At the awards ceremony on 15 October 2010, Tipperary won six All Star awards, Brendan Cummins, Paul Curran, Brendan Maher, Noel McGrath, Lar Corbett and Eoin Kelly won awards, while Kilkenny won five awards, Jackie Tyrrell, Tommy Walsh, JJ Delaney, Michael Fennelly and Richie Power.{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/corbett-shines-brightest-of-tipps-star-men-2382103.html|title=Corbett shines brightest of Tipp's Star men|date=2010-10-16|work=Irish Independent|access-date=2010-10-26}} Lar Corbett was named [[All Stars Hurler of the Year|All Stars Hurler of the year]] while [[Brendan Maher]] collected the [[All Stars Young Hurler of the Year|All Stars Young hurler of the year]] award.{{cite web|url=http://www.irishtimes.com/newspaper/sport/2010/1016/1224281253984.html|title=Corbett crowns a magnificent year|date=2010-10-16|work=The Irish Times |access-date=2010-10-26}} Tipperary's Lar Corbett and Brendan Maher were shortlisted, alongside Kilkenny's Michael Fennelly and Tommy Walsh, for the [[GPA Hurler of the Year|GPA Hurler of the Year award]] for 2010. {{Short description|none}} {{Use Irish English|date=February 2021}} {{Use dmy dates|date=August 2021}} {{Infobox football match | title = 2011 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Final | image = | event = [[2011 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]] | team1 = [[Kilkenny county hurling team|Kilkenny]] | team1association = [[File:Colours of Kilkenny.svg|40px]] | team1score = 2–17 | team2 = [[Tipperary county hurling team|Tipperary]] | team2association = [[File:Colours of Tipperary.svg|40px]] | team2score = 1–16 | details = | date = 4 September 2011 | stadium = [[Croke Park]] | city = [[Dublin]] | man_of_the_match1a = [[J. J. Delaney]]{{cite news|url=https://hoganstand.com/article/index/154440|title=JJ Delaney scoops Man of the Match award|work=Hogan Stand|date=5 September 2011}} | referee = [[Brian Gavin (referee)|Brian Gavin]] ([[Offaly GAA|Offaly]]) | attendance = 81,214 | weather = Rain clearing to sun
{{convert|16|°C|°F}}[http://www.met.ie/climate/monthly-weather-reports.asp Met Eireann: Monthly Summaries - September 2011] | previous = [[2010 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2010]] | next = [[2012 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2012]] }} The '''2011 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final''' took place in [[Croke Park]], Dublin on Sunday, 4 September 2011. The final was contested by [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]]{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/kilkenny-display-killer-instinct-to-dismantle-deise-2842219.html|title=Kilkenny display killer instinct to dismantle Deise|date=8 August 2011|work=Irish Independent|access-date=9 August 2011}} and defending champions, [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]].{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/rising-blues-give-ryans-men-timely-reality-check-2848250.html|title=Rising Blues give Ryan's men timely reality check|date=15 August 2011|work=Irish Independent|access-date=15 August 2011}} Kilkenny were playing in their sixth consecutive final, while the pairing of Kilkenny and Tipperary was the first ever time that the same two teams have played in the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]] Final for three consecutive seasons.{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/allireland-hurling-final-preview-2866168.html|title=All-Ireland Hurling final preview|date= 4 September 2011|work=Irish Independent |access-date=7 September 2011}} Kilkenny won their fifth title in six years after a four-point win against Tipperary, avenging their [[2010 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2010 defeat]].{{cite web|url=http://www.belfasttelegraph.co.uk/sport/gaa/kilkenny-cats-bare-claws-to-reclaim-allireland-crown-16045346.html|title=Kilkenny Cats bare claws to reclaim All-Ireland crown |date= 5 September 2011|work=Belfast Telegraph|access-date=6 September 2011}}{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/regionals/herald/cats-hit-back-in-style/27988337.html|title=Cats hit back in style|date= 5 September 2011|work=Herald|access-date=6 September 2011}}{{cite web|url=http://hoganstand.com/Hurling/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=154432|title=All-Ireland SHC final: Cats are back|date= 4 September 2011|work=Hogan Stand|access-date=6 September 2011}}{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20166499.html|title=The greatest of champions reclaim crown|date= 5 September 2011|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=7 September 2011}} The final which was shown live in Ireland on [[RTÉ2]] attracted the second highest ever viewership for an All Ireland Hurling Final, peaking at 1.1 million viewers in the final minutes. An average audience of 971,000 viewers tuned into the game overall.{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2011/0905/hurling_kilkenny_tipperary.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120909013542/http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2011/0905/hurling_kilkenny_tipperary.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=9 September 2012 |title=Near record audience for hurling final |date=5 September 2011 |work=RTÉ Sport |access-date=6 September 2011 }} ==Pre-match== [[File:Croke park.jpg|thumb|300px|[[Croke Park]], the venue for the 2011 final]] ===Background=== Kilkenny were Leinster champions, having beaten [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] by 1–26 to 1–15 and [[Dublin GAA|Dublin]] by 4–17 to 1–15 in the final to earn that title. They then beat [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] in the semi-final on 7 August by 2–19 to 1–16 to reach the final.{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2011/0807/kilkenny_waterford.html |title=Kilkenny 2–19 Waterford 1–16 |date=7 August 2011 |work=RTÉ Sport |access-date=30 August 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111006012722/http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2011/0807/kilkenny_waterford.html |archive-date=6 October 2011 }} Tipperary opened their campaign as defending champion's against [[Cork GAA|Cork]] in the first round on 29 May and won by a scoreline of 3–22 to 0–23.{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2011/0529/tipperary_cork.html |title=Tipperary 3–22 Cork 0–23 |date=29 May 2011 |work=RTÉ Sport |access-date=30 August 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110903010404/http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2011/0529/tipperary_cork.html |archive-date=3 September 2011 }} They then defeated [[Clare GAA|Clare]] by 4–19 o 1–19 to set up a [[2011 Munster Senior Hurling Championship Final|Munster Final]] meeting with [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]]. Tipperary defeated Waterford by 7–19 to 0–19 to win their third Munster title in four years. [[Dublin GAA|Dublin]] were then defeated by 1–19 to 0–18 to set up a third consecutive All Ireland final against [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]].{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2011/0830/roadtofinal_reports_kilkenny_tipperary.html |title=Reports: Road to the Final |date=30 August 2011 |work=RTÉ Sport |access-date=30 August 2011 }}{{dead link|date=June 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} Match tickets for the final in all of the three Stands increased from €70 to €80 and all Terrace tickets increased by €5 to €40 from the 2010 final prices.{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/price-hike-hits-home-for-struggling-supporters-2866258.html|title=Price hike hits home for struggling supporters|date= 4 September 2011|work=Irish Independent|access-date=6 September 2011}}{{cite web|url=http://hoganstand.com/Hurling/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=154441|title=Relief for GAA as final almost sells out|date= 5 September 2011|work=Hogan Stand|access-date=6 September 2011}} The pre-match betting made Tipperary slight favourites, with [[Bookmaker]] ''[[Paddy Power]]'' giving odds of 8/11 on a Tipperary win, Kilkenny were 6/4 to win with a draw at 11/1.{{cite web|url=http://www.paddypower.com/bet/gaa-sports/gaa-matches/gaa-hurling-matches/Tipperary-v-Kilkenny-2926533.html|title=Tipperary v Kilkenny Betting|date=30 August 2011|work=Paddypower.com|access-date=30 August 2011}} Prior to the senior final, [[Galway GAA|Galway]] claimed the [[All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship 2011|2011 Minor Hurling Championship]] after a 1–21 to 1–12 win against [[Dublin GAA|Dublin]].{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2011/0904/galway_dublin_minor.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120914051717/http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2011/0904/galway_dublin_minor.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=14 September 2012 |title=Galway 1–21 Dublin 1–12 |date=5 September 2011 |work=RTÉ Sport |access-date=7 September 2011 }} ===Team news=== Tipperary manager [[Declan Ryan (hurler)|Declan Ryan]] named an unchanged team from the team that defeated Dublin in the semi-final for the final. In a positional change, [[Séamus Callanan]] started at left half forward with [[Noel McGrath (hurler)|Noel McGrath]] at centre half forward.{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2011/0830/tipperary.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120915112805/http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2011/0830/tipperary.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=15 September 2012 |title=Tipp unchanged for Croke Park final |date=30 August 2011 |work=RTÉ Sport |access-date=30 August 2011 }} Kilkenny's [[Colin Fennelly]] was a major doubt for the final after picking up a hamstring injury in a club match.{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2011/0816/fennellyc.html?gaa |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120912073022/http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2011/0816/fennellyc.html?gaa |url-status=dead |archive-date=12 September 2012 |title=Fennelly doubtful for hurling final |date=16 August 2011 |work=RTÉ Sport |access-date=30 August 2011 }} However, he recovered sufficiently to be named in the starting team. The Kilkenny team had one change from the team that had beaten Waterford in the semi-final. [[Eddie Brennan]] was included, replacing [[TJ Reid]] at right half forward.{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2011/0902/kilkenny_tipperary_brennane.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120909191452/http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2011/0902/kilkenny_tipperary_brennane.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=9 September 2012 |title=Brennan handed starting role for Kilkenny |date=2 September 2011 |work=RTÉ Sport |access-date=5 September 2011 }} ===Referee=== [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]]-based referee [[Brian Gavin (referee)|Brian Gavin]] was named as the referee for the 2011 All-Ireland final on 16 August.{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2011/0816/gavinb_kilkenny_tipperary.html?gaa |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130217213415/http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2011/0816/gavinb_kilkenny_tipperary.html?gaa |url-status=dead |archive-date=17 February 2013 |title=Offaly's Gavin to ref hurling decider |date=16 August 2011 |work=RTÉ Sport |access-date=30 August 2011 }} The Clara native took charge of his first final after previously taken charge of the All-Ireland championship final at minor level in 2004 and at under-21 level in 2006. Barry Kelly of [[Westmeath GAA|Westmeath]] was the standby referee, the other linesman was John Sexton of [[Cork GAA|Cork]] and the sideline official was [[Galway GAA|Galway's]] Alan Kelly.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-30516750.html|title=Gavin to referee All-Ireland SHC final|date=16 August 2011|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=30 August 2011}} ==Match summary== ===First half=== Kilkenny started strongly, scoring the first 5 points on the match, with a free from [[Henry Shefflin]], and points from [[Eoin Larkin]], [[Richie Hogan]], [[Richie Power (1985)|Richie Power]] and [[Henry Shefflin]], all from play. It wasn't until the 16th minute that Tipperary scored their first point, by [[Noel McGrath (hurler)|Noel McGrath]]. Two minutes later, [[Eoin Kelly (Tipperary hurler)|Eoin Kelly]] scored a free to make the score 0–5 to 0–2. In the 19th minute, a melee broke out, leading to the referee, Brian Gavin sustaining a cut on the nose, which had connected with [[Tommy Walsh (hurler, born 1983)|Tommy Walsh]]'s hurl. There was a significant delay while the referee was treated. Eoin Kelly then got a point from another free and a minute later, [[Eddie Brennan]] scored a point. In the 29th minute, Tipperary made their first substitution, bring on [[Brendan Maher]] in place of [[John O'Keeffe (Tipperary hurler)|John O'Keeffe]] in an effort to strengthen their defence. Two minutes later, [[Patrick Maher (hurler)|Patrick Maher]] won a free, which was pointed by Eoin Kelly. Shefflin then scored a free from close to the sideline. In the 35th minute, [[Michael Fennelly (hurler)|Michael Fennelly]] broke through the defence to fire the ball low and past [[Brendan Cummins (Tipperary hurler)|Brendan Cummins]] in the Tipperary goal to score the first goal of the game. Due to the referee's injury earlier in the half, there were to be 5 minutes of additional time to be played. The teams swapped points courtesy of [[Gearóid Ryan]] and [[Michael Rice (hurler)|Michael Rice]]. Tipperary then won a free as [[Patrick Maher (hurler)|Patrick Maher]] was fouled by [[Noel Hickey]] in front of goal, and Eoin Kelly scored to leave the half time score as Kilkenny 1-08 – 0-06 Tipperary.{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2011/0904/live_kilkenny_tipperary.html |title=As it Happened: Kilkenny 2–17 Tipperary 1–16 |date=4 September 2011 |work=[[RTÉ Sport]] |access-date=5 September 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111210094908/http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2011/0904/live_kilkenny_tipperary.html |archive-date=10 December 2011 }}{{cite web|url=http://thescore.thejournal.ie/live-all-ireland-senior-hurling-final-217565-Sep2011/|title=As it happened: All-Ireland senior hurling final|date=4 September 2011|work=thejournal.ie|access-date=5 September 2011}}{{cite web|url=http://www.setanta.com/ie/Articles/2011/09/04/All-Ireland-final-day-LIVE/gnid-107803/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230923011630/http://www.setanta.com/ie/Articles/2011/09/04/All-Ireland-final-day-LIVE/gnid-107803/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=23 September 2023 |title=All-Ireland final day as it happened |date=4 September 2011 |work=[[Setanta Ireland]] |access-date=5 September 2011 }} ===Second half=== Tipperary made two changes at half time, bring on [[Pa Bourke]] and [[Benny Dunne]], and taking off [[Shane McGrath (hurler)|Shane McGrath]] and [[Séamus Callanan]]. Two minutes in, the ball fell to Pa Bourke in front of goal, who shot wide. Benny Dunne and Henry Shefflin then exchanged points. In the 41st minute, Patrick Maher appeared through on goal, when [[JJ Delaney]] got in a flick to put the ball out over the endline for a 65. Eoin Kelly put this over the bar for his 5th point of the game. [[Colin Fennelly]] and Richie Power then pointed for Kilkenny to give them a 6-point lead. [[Conor O'Mahony]] and Eoin Kelly then scored for Tipperary. In the 49th minute, Eddie Brennan burst through on goal and laid the ball off to Richie Hogan, who put the ball past Cummins for the second time. The score was now 2–12 to 0–10. Shefflin and Noel McGrath then exchanged points, before [[Lar Corbett]] fed the ball to Pa Bourke, who put it past [[David Herity]], for Tipperary's first goal. In the 59th minute, Colin Fennelly scored from a sideline cut, and Kilkenny made their first substitution, taking Eddie Brennan off and replacing him with [[T. J. Reid]]. Noel McGrath then pointed from 50 metres and Eoin Kelly added another free, leaving the score 2–14 – 1–14 with six minutes left. Shefflin and Kelly swapped frees, maintaining the gap at three points with two minutes left. T. J. Reid then scored going into injury time, and Gearóid Ryan brought the gap back to three a minute later. Eoin Larkin scored the final point of the game a minute later to ensure that Kilkenny won the game 2–17 to 1–16.{{cite web|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/northern_ireland/gaelic_games/14780939.stm|title=Kilkenny 2–17 1–16 Tipperary|date=4 September 2011|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=7 September 2011|archive-date=6 September 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110906004822/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/northern_ireland/gaelic_games/14780939.stm|url-status=dead}} ==Match details== {{Football box |date = 4 September 2011 |time = 15:30 [[Western European Summer Time|IST]] |team1 = [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] |score = 2–17 – 1–16 |team2 = [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] |report = [https://web.archive.org/web/20120930221446/http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/2011/0904/284374-kilkenny_tipperary_report/ Report] | |goals1 = H Shefflin (0–7, 5f)

Alan Kelly ([[Galway GAA|Galway]]) '''Umpires''' |} ==Trophy presentation== The trophy was presented from the [[Croke Park|Hogan stand]] to Kilkenny captain [[Brian Hogan (Kilkenny hurler)|Brian Hogan]] by GAA president [[Christy Cooney]]. After the presentation the Kilkenny team and management went on a lap of honour around the Croke Park pitch. ==Man of the Match== Kilkenny's [[J. J. Delaney]] was chosen as the man-of-the-match for the final. A panel on ''[[The Sunday Game]]'' on the night of the final, consisting of [[Anthony Daly (hurler)|Anthony Daly]], [[Michael Duignan (hurler)|Michael Duignan]] and [[John Henderson (hurler)|John Henderson]], chose Delaney from a shortlist that also included [[Tommy Walsh (hurler, born 1983)|Tommy Walsh]] and [[Michael Fennelly (hurler)|Michael Fennelly]]. He was presented with his award by the GAA president [[Christy Cooney]] at the team's victory banquet at the [[Citywest Hotel]] in Dublin which was shown live as part of ''The Sunday Game'' on [[RTÉ Two]].{{cite web|url=http://www.breakingnews.ie/sport/delaney-chosen-as-man-of-the-match-519199.html|title=Delaney chosen as man-of-the-match|date= 4 September 2011|work=Breaking News|access-date=6 September 2011}}{{cite web|url=http://hoganstand.com/Hurling/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=154440|title=JJ Delaney scoops Man of the Match award|date= 5 September 2011|work=Hogan Stand|access-date=6 September 2011}} ==Reaction== Kilkenny manager [[Brian Cody]] described the win as "massively sweet". Speaking to [[RTÉ]] he said that "for the last few years we have been coming in as champions and favourites to win the match, this year was very different, Tipperary were great champions, they set very high standards and they were hot favourites to win today, in those situations it becomes sweet to win because we had to play at a serious level to win it from minute one."{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2011/0905/codyb_kilkenny_tipperary.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120908201417/http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2011/0905/codyb_kilkenny_tipperary.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=8 September 2012 |title=Cody calls win 'massively sweet' |date=5 September 2011 |work=RTÉ Sport |access-date=6 September 2011 }} [[Tommy Walsh (hurler, born 1983)|Tommy Walsh]] said that his sixth All-Ireland win was the sweetest of all. Speaking to the ''[[Irish Examiner]]'' he said "It stands as the sweetest because we lost last year, after last year and losing the five-in-a-row it was heartbreaking all last winter and it probably showed out there today how much it affected us".{{cite web|url=http://hoganstand.com/Hurling/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=154444|title=This one was the sweetest, says Tommy|date= 5 September 2011|work=Hogan Stand|access-date=6 September 2011}} Tipperary manager [[Declan Ryan (hurler)|Declan Ryan]] paid tribut to Kilkenny saying "we were lucky to go in only five points down at half-time, Hats off to Kilkenny, they showed they were real champions to come back and play like that today".{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2011/0905/kilkenny_tipperary3.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120911010855/http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2011/0905/kilkenny_tipperary3.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=11 September 2012 |title=Ryan hails 'hungrier' Cats |date=5 September 2011 |work=RTÉ Sport |access-date=6 September 2011 }} Former Tipperary manager [[Nicky English]] writing in ''[[The Irish Times]]'' said that "Kilkenny were by far the best team, with team being the operative word, and fully deserved their success, they were the masters in all areas and, from the word go, set out to dominate the physical exchanges just as much as they did in their pomp and in their glory years".{{cite web|url=http://www.irishtimes.com/newspaper/sport/2011/0905/1224303498967.html|title=Hungry Kilkenny the masters in all areas|date= 5 September 2011|work=The Irish Times |access-date=7 September 2011}} Tipperary coach [[Tommy Dunne]] speaking the day after the match had praise for Kilkenny saying "They have won eight in 12 years so the statistics speak for themselves, they are a fabulous team and they will rightly go down as one of the greatest teams of all time, if not the greatest, and they showed why they are that again on Sunday".{{cite web|url=http://www.irishexaminer.com/archives/2011/0905/sport/the-greatest-of-champions-reclaim-crown-166499.htm|title=Dunne expects Tipp’s 30-somethings to return to lead fight|date= 6 September 2011|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=7 September 2011}}{{dead link|date=April 2026|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/dunne-certain-tipp-veterans-will-stay-on-2867208.html|title=Dunne certain Tipp veterans will stay on|date= 6 September 2011|work=Irish Independent|access-date=7 September 2011}} [[Martin Breheny]], writing in the ''[[Irish Independent]]'', said that "Brian Cody’s Cats with this victory are poised to surpass [[Mick O'Dwyer]]'s [[Kerry GAA|Kerry]] football team of the 1970s and 80s as the greatest GAA team in history".{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/martin-breheny-codyrsquos-cats-poised-to-surpass-mickorsquos-men-as-the-greatest-2868540.html|title=Cody’s Cats poised to surpass Micko’s men as the greatest|date= 7 September 2011|work=Irish Independent|access-date=7 September 2011}} ==Civic reception== The victorious Kilkenny team arrived back at McDonagh Station in [[Kilkenny|Kilkenny City]] the day after the final for an open top bus parade to the civic reception at Market Yard.{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/victorious-cats-return-with-a-muchloved-friend-2867251.html|title=Victorious Cats return with a much-loved friend|date= 6 September 2011|work=Irish Independent|access-date=6 September 2011}}{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2011/0905/kilkenny.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120913052651/http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2011/0905/kilkenny.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=13 September 2012 |title=Kilkenny prepare to bring MacCarthy Cup home |date=5 September 2011 |work=RTÉ Sport |access-date=6 September 2011 }} An estimated 30,000 supporters welcomed the team home to Kilkenny for the celebrations.{{cite web|url=http://hoganstand.com/Hurling/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=154590|title=30,000 welcome champions home|date= 6 September 2011|work=Hogan Stand|access-date=6 September 2011}}{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20166601.html|title=Supercats get heroes' welcome|date= 6 September 2011|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=7 September 2011}} ==Awards== Kilkenny had fourteen players nominated for the 2011 [[GAA All Stars Awards winners (hurling)|GAA-GPA Hurling All-Stars]], with David Herity, Paul Murphy and Colin Fennelly being nominated for their first awards, Tipperary received ten nominations.{{cite web|url=http://www.irishtimes.com/sports/gaa/2011/0929/1224304975300.html|title=Cats dominate All-Star nominations|date= 29 September 2011|work=The Irish Times |access-date=29 September 2011}} This was the first year of the awards being jointly run by the GAA and Gaelic Players Association{{cite web|url=http://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/kilkenny-lead-list-of-hurling-all-star-nominees-522515.html|title=Kilkenny lead list of hurling All-Star nominee|date= 29 September 2011|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=29 September 2011}}{{cite web|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/northern_ireland/gaelic_games/15113160.stm|title=Kilkenny lead All-Star hurling nominations with 14|date=29 September 2011|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=29 September 2011|archive-date=29 September 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110929181545/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/northern_ireland/gaelic_games/15113160.stm|url-status=dead}} In October 2011, Henry Shefflin established a new record when he was awarded his 10th All-Star award and was one of eight Kilkenny players named on the 2011 GAA GPA All Star hurling team. Tipperary received four awards.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20171479.html|title=Shefflin and Cats steal All Star show |date= 21 October 2011|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=16 November 2011}} Kilkenny's [[Michael Fennelly (hurler)|Michael Fennelly]] along with winning an All Star award was also named as the [[All Stars Hurler of the Year|GAA GPA Hurler of the year]].{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2011/1021/allstar.html |title=Fennelly & Brogan named Players of the Year |date=21 October 2011 |work=RTÉ Sport {{convert|16|°C|°F}} | previous = [[2011 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2011]] | next = [[2013 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2013]] }} The '''2012 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final''', the deciding game of the [[2012 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]], was played on 9 September 2012 at [[Croke Park]], Dublin. The final was contested by first-time Leinster Champions [[Galway GAA|Galway]] and [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]], the defeated Leinster finalists and defending All-Ireland champions. This was Galway's first appearance at this stage since [[2005 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2005]], when they lost to [[Cork GAA|Cork]].{{Cite news|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/2012/0812/333298-galway-reach-first-all-ireland-final-since-2005/|title=Galway 0–22 Cork 0–17|work=RTÉ Sport|date=12 August 2012|access-date=12 August 2012}} The match ended level, the first All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final at the end of which the teams finished level since [[1959 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1959]]. Kilkenny won the replay, with [[Henry Shefflin]] becoming the first Gaelic athlete to win nine All-Ireland Senior Championship medals on the field of play.{{Cite news|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/2012/1001/339837-shefflin/|title=Henry Shefflin pays tribute to Kilkenny team after record ninth All-Ireland medal|work=RTÉ Sport|date=1 October 2012|access-date=1 October 2012}}{{Cite web|url= https://www.gaa.ie/hurling/news/flashback-2012-all-ireland-shc-final-kilkenny-v-galway/|title =Flashback: 2012 All Ireland SHC Final – Kilkenny v Galway|date=14 June 2020|work=GAA.ie|access-date=15 June 2020}} == First Final == === Background === {{See also|2012 Leinster Senior Hurling Championship Final}} The first final was played on 9 September 2012. Kilkenny were the defending champions after defeating [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] by four points, 2–17 to 1–16, in the [[2011 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final]].{{Cite news|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2011/0904/live_kilkenny_tipperary.html |title=As it Happened: Kilkenny 2–17 Tipperary 1–16 |work=[[RTÉ Sport]] |date=4 September 2011 |access-date=4 September 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111210094908/http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2011/0904/live_kilkenny_tipperary.html |archive-date=10 December 2011 }}{{Cite news|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/northern_ireland/gaelic_games/14780939.stm|title=Kilkenny 2–17 1–16 Tipperary|work=BBC Sport|date=4 September 2011|access-date=4 September 2011|archive-date=6 September 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110906004822/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/northern_ireland/gaelic_games/14780939.stm|url-status=dead}} However, Galway unexpectedly beat Kilkenny in the [[2012 Leinster Senior Hurling Championship Final|Leinster Senior Hurling Championship Final]] on 8 July 2012, the shock of the year.{{Cite news|url=https://www.thejournal.ie/live-galway-v-kilkenny-leinster-shc-final-514035-Jul2012/|title=LIVE: Galway v Kilkenny, Leinster SHC Final|work=The Journal|date=8 July 2012|access-date=8 July 2012}} Kilkenny recovered and qualified for the 2012 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final via the back door, inflicting upon [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] their heaviest defeat in the All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship since 1897 along the way.{{Cite news|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/2012/0820/334243-ryan-we-were-blown-away/|title=Tipperary manager Declan Ryan admits his side were blown away by Kilkenny|work=RTÉ Sport|publisher=RTÉ|date=20 August 2012|access-date=21 August 2012}} The final was a rematch of the 2012 Leinster Senior Hurling Championship Final against Galway. This was the fifth All-Ireland final clash between the two counties and the first since [[1993 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1993]] with Kilkenny winning three of the previous four. Galway's only win against Kilkenny came in [[1987 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1987]] when they won by six points. It was confirmed on 24 August that Galway would be allocated just 12,000 tickets for the final with 25,000 to 30,000 Galway fans expected to attend the final.{{Cite web|url=https://hoganstand.com/Hurling/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=176017 |title=Galway to receive just 12,000 final tickets|date=24 August 2012|work=Hogan Stand|access-date=27 August 2012 }} Tickets for the final were priced at €80 for stand tickets €40 for terrace tickets. On 20 August 2012, the GAA announced that [[Barry Kelly (referee)|Barry Kelly]] from [[Westmeath GAA|Westmeath]] would referee the 2012 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final.{{Cite web|url=https://www.hoganstand.com/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=176812 |title=Who will take hurling's big prize?|date=4 September 2012|work=Hogan Stand|access-date=5 September 2012 }} It was the third All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final of his refereeing career—he previously refereed in [[2006 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2006]] and [[2008 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2008]].{{Cite news|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/2012/0820/334328-barry-kelly-to-referee-hurling-final/|title=Barry Kelly confirmed as referee for All-Ireland hurling final|work=RTÉ Sport|date=20 August 2012|access-date=20 August 2012}} Team GB's Olympic boxer [[Natasha Jonas]] was invited to attend the 2012 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final.{{Cite news|first=Coilin|last=Duffy|url=http://www.independent.ie/national-news/taylor-adversary-invited-to-allireland-hurling-final-3196701.html|title=Taylor adversary invited to All-Ireland hurling final|newspaper=Irish Independent|publisher=Independent News & Media|date=11 August 2012|access-date=11 August 2012}} === Match summary === This was the first All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final at the end of which the teams finished level since [[1959 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1959]].{{Cite news|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/2012/0909/336921-galway-earn-replay-against-kilkenny/|title=Kilkenny 0–19 Galway 2–13|work=RTÉ Sport|date=9 September 2012|access-date=9 September 2012}}{{Cite news|url=http://www.belfasttelegraph.co.uk/sport/gaa/kilkenny-galway-draw-sees-first-allireland-hurling-final-replay-in-53-years-16208896.html|title=Kilkenny Galway draw sees first All-Ireland hurling final replay in 53 years|newspaper=[[Belfast Telegraph]]|publisher=Independent News & Media|date=10 September 2012|access-date=10 September 2012}} Joe Canning scored a goal for Galway in the 10th minute, getting past three Kilkenny defenders and smashing an angled shot past Kilkenny goalkeeper David Herity. Kilkenny had managed just two points from the opening 18 minutes with Galway leading by 1–9 to 0–7 at half time. The sides were level in the 50th minute before Niall Burke got the second goal for Galway in the 55th minute after picking up a loose ball and shooting low into the net. Kilkenny were awarded a penalty for a foul on Eoin Larkin in the 69th minute with the sides level. Henry Shefflin decided to hit the ball over the bar and take the point. Joe Canning then hit a 73rd-minute equaliser from the 45-metre line close to the Hogan Stand side of the field to make the scores level and take the game to a replay three weeks later. == Drawn Match Details == {{Football box |date = 9 September 2012 |time = 15:30 [[Western European Summer Time|IST]] |team1 = [[Galway GAA|Galway]] |score = 2–13 – 0–19 |team2 = [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] |report = [https://www.the42.ie/live-galway-v-kilkenny-all-ireland-shc-final-589805-Sep2012/ Report] |goals1 = J Canning 1–09 (0-08f), N Burke 1-02, A Smith, N Donoghue 0-01 each. | |goals2 = H Shefflin 0–12 (10f, 1 pen), E Larkin, TJ Reid 0-02 each, A Fogarty, R Power, R Hogan. | |stadium = [[Croke Park]], Dublin |attendance = 81,932 |referee = [[Barry Kelly (referee)|B. Kelly]] ([[Westmeath GAA|Westmeath]]) }} {| width=92% | |- |{{Football kit | pattern_la = | pattern_b = | pattern_ra = | leftarm = 800000 | body = 800000 | rightarm = 800000 | shorts = FFFFFF | socks = 800000 | title = Galway }} |{{Football kit |pattern_la = _borderonblack |pattern_b = _blackstripes |pattern_ra = _borderonblack |leftarm = FFC125 |body = FFC125 |rightarm = FFC125 |shorts = FFFFFF |socks = FFC125 |title = Kilkenny }} |} == Replay == === Tickets === Tickets for the replay were reduced in price to €50 for stand tickets and €25 for terrace tickets.{{Cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/2012/0910/337044-tick-prices-cut-for-hurling-replay/ |title= GAA cuts ticket prices for All-Ireland hurling final replay between Galway and Kilkenny|date=10 September 2012|work=RTÉ Sport|access-date=30 January 2013 }} === Team news === Galway named an unchanged side for the replay, held at Croke Park on 30 September 2012. Kilkenny made two changes. However, Galway goalkeeper [[James Skehill]] dislocated his shoulder in the team's final training session, casting some doubt upon his place in the team.{{Cite news|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/2012/0928/339587-galway-goalkeeper-suffers-shoulder-injury/|title=Galway goalkeeper James Skehill suffers shoulder injury but Cunningham names unchanged side for final|work=RTÉ Sport|publisher=RTÉ|date=28 September 2012|access-date=28 September 2012}} He still played though.{{Cite news|url=http://www.irishtimes.com/sports/gaa/2012/0930/1224324632979.html|title=Skehill starts for Galway|newspaper=The Irish Times|publisher=Irish Times Trust|date=30 September 2012|access-date=30 September 2012}} === Match summary === ==== First half ==== Galway opened the scoring with a point from a 65-metre free after six minutes. Kilkenny soon moved in front with points from [[Henry Shefflin]] and debutant [[Walter Walsh (hurler)|Walter Walsh]]. Galway's [[David Burke (Galway hurler)|David Burke]] scored the first goal of the game after sixteen minutes, adding a second goal one minute later. [[Richie Power (hurler born 1985)|Richie Power]] quickly scored Kilkenny's first goal and the game's third in as many minutes. Soon Kilkenny began to dominate and Galway could not register a score. The half-time score was Galway 2-04, Kilkenny 1–11. ==== Second half ==== Kilkenny's [[Richie Hogan]] opened the second half scoring with a point. Following some pushing and shoving, David Burke gets the ball into the back of the Kilkenny net for a third time but the referee blew his whistle and awarded a free to Galway instead, which Joe Canning scored. In the 49th minute, Galway's [[Cyril Donnellan]] was shown the red card and sent off after swinging his hurley at opponent [[J. J. Delaney]] and hitting him upon the head. In the 58th minute, debutant Walter Walsh scored Kilkenny's second goal and the game's fourth, with substitute C. Fennelly adding Kilkenny's third goal in the 62nd minute. In the 66th minute, Galway's J. Glynn scored his team's third goal and the game's sixth, lashing the sliotar into the roof of the net. But it was all too little, too late. The full-time score was Kilkenny 3–22, Galway 3–11.{{Cite news|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/2012/0930/339700-live-all-ireland-hurling-finals/|title=As it Happened: All-Ireland Hurling final|work=RTÉ Sport|publisher=RTÉ|date=30 September 2012|access-date=30 September 2012}} == Replay Match Details == {{Football box |date = 30 September 2012 |time = 15:30 [[Western European Summer Kilkenny }} |} == Trophy presentation == The trophy was presented from the [[Croke Park|Hogan stand]] to Kilkenny captain [[Eoin Larkin]] by GAA president [[Liam O'Neill]].{{Cite web|url=http://www.thescore.ie/galway-kilkenny-all-ireland-final-2-615658-Sep2012/ |title=As It Happened: Kilkenny v Galway, All-Ireland SHC final replay |date=20 September 2012 |work=thescore.ie 2013 }} After the presentation the Kilkenny team and management went on a lap of honour around the Croke Park pitch. {{convert|17|°C|°F}} | previous = [[2012 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2012]] | next = [[2014 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2014]] }} The '''2013 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final''', the deciding game of the [[2013 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]], was played on 8 September 2013 at [[Croke Park]], Dublin. For the [[2012 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|second straight year]], the final ended in a draw, requiring a replay that was held on 28 September 2013 at Croke Park.{{cite news|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/2013/0909/473172-replay/ |title=All-Ireland hurling final replay to throw in a 5pm on Saturday 28 September |publisher=[[RTÉ Sport]] |date=9 September 2013 |access-date=10 September 2013}}{{cite web|url= https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2024/0717/1460471-small-fish-and-teenage-hat-tricks-2013-drama-revisited/|title=Small fish and teenage hat-tricks - Clare and Cork's double dose of drama in 2013|date=18 July 2024|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=18 July 2024}} In the replay Clare beat Cork 5–16 to 3–16 to claim their fourth All Ireland title.{{cite web|url = http://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/clare-claim-a-game-borrowed-from-the-gods-244646.html|title=Clare claim a game borrowed from the gods|date=28 September 2013|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=27 September 2013}}{{cite web|url = http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/clare-bridge-16year-gap-after-shane-odonnell-becomes-hattrick-hero-29617992.html|title=Clare bridge 16-year gap after Shane O'Donnell becomes hat-trick hero|date=28 September 2013|work=Irish Independent|access-date=30 September 2013}}{{cite web|url=http://www.thescore.ie/clare-cork-replay-match-report-1105271-Sep2013/ |title=O'Donnell's dream day fires Clare to victory |date=28 September 2013 |work=The Score |access-date=30 September 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131001200830/http://www.thescore.ie/clare-cork-replay-match-report-1105271-Sep2013/ |archive-date= 1 October 2013 }} The replay has been described by some as one of the greatest finals of all time.{{cite web|url = http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/cyril-farrell-shrewd-davy-has-all-the-materials-to-build-a-dynasty-29620498.html|title= Cyril Farrell: Shrewd Davy has all the materials to build a dynasty|date=30 September 2013|work=Irish Independent|access-date=30 September 2013}}{{cite web|url = http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/anthony-daly-clare-brought-an-uzi-with-them-and-emptied-the-clip-29620512.html|title= Clare brought an Uzi with them and emptied the clip|date=30 September 2013|work=Irish Independent|access-date=30 September 2013}}{{cite web|url = http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/hurlings-top-10-the-best-games-of-the-modern-era-29622863.html|title= Hurling's top 10 - the best games of the modern era|date=1 October 2013|work=Irish Independent|access-date=30 September 2013}}{{cite web|url = http://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/theyll-party-like-its-1995-but-clare-are-already-looking-forward-244743.html|title= They'll party like it's 1995, but Clare are already looking forward|date=30 September 2013|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=30 September 2013}}{{cite web|url = http://munster.gaa.ie/2013/09/28/all-ireland-senior-hurling-championship-final-replay-clare-v-cork/|title= Clare 5-16 Cork 3-16|date=28 September 2013|work=Munster GAA|access-date=30 September 2013}} The game between [[Cork GAA|Cork]] and [[Clare GAA|Clare]] was an all Munster All-Ireland for the second time ever, the first having been in [[1997 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1997]] between Clare and [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]].{{cite web|url= http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/barrymurphy-leads-cork-back-to-biggest-stage-29491306.html|title= Barry-Murphy leads Cork back to biggest stage|date=12 August 2013|work=Irish Independent|access-date=19 August 2013 }}{{cite web|url= http://munster.gaa.ie/2013/08/18/all-ireland-senior-hurling-championship-semi-final-limerick-v-clare/|title= Clare 1-22 Limerick 0-18|date=18 August 2013|work=Munster GAA|access-date=19 August 2013 }}{{cite web|url= http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-football/all-ireland-hurling-final-replay-to-be-held-at-5pm-on-saturday-28-september-29564099.html|title= All Ireland hurling final replay to be held at 5pm on Saturday 28 September|date=9 September 2013|work=Irish Independent|access-date=11 September 2013}} The drawn final was shown live in Ireland on [[RTÉ2]] as part of ''[[The Sunday Game]]'' live programme, presented by [[Michael Lyster]] from Croke Park, with studio analysis from [[Cyril Farrell]], [[Liam Sheedy]], and [[Eddie Brennan]] and pre-match comments from [[Tomás Mulcahy]] and [[Ger Loughnane]]. Match commentary was provided by [[Ger Canning]] with analysis by [[Michael Duignan (hurler)|Michael Duignan]]. The replay was shown live in Ireland on [[RTÉ2]] as part of ''[[The Sunday Game|The Saturday Game]]'' live programme, presented by [[Michael Lyster]] from Croke Park, with studio analysis from [[Cyril Farrell]], [[Liam Sheedy]], and [[Eddie Brennan]]. Match commentary was provided by [[Ger Canning]] with analysis by [[Michael Duignan (hurler)|Michael Duignan]]. The drawn match was preceded by the [[Galway GAA|Galway]] against [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] minor hurling [[2013 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|final]] which started at 1.15pm and was won by Waterford, their first minor title in 65 years.{{cite web|url= http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/2013/0908/472978-galway-waterford/|title= Waterford 1-21 Galway 0-16|date=8 September 2013|work=RTÉ Sport|access-date=11 September 2013}} A peak Irish television audience of 1.3 million people watched RTÉ's coverage of the drawn final with an average audience of 885,000 viewers, a 64% share of the available television audience.{{cite web|url= http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/2013/0909/473172-replay/|title=All-Ireland hurling final replay to throw in a 5pm on Saturday 28 September|date=9 September 2013|work=RTÉ Sport|access-date=12 September 2013}} ==Background== {{main|Clare–Cork hurling rivalry}} This All-Ireland final was the 50th championship meeting of [[Cork GAA|Cork]] and [[Clare GAA|Clare]]; however, it was their first meeting in an All-Ireland decider. Cork held the balance of power in all previous meetings between the two, having recorded 34 championship victories to Clare's eleven. There had been four drawn games. Both sides last met in the 2013 Munster semi-final, when Cork recorded a 0–23 to 0–15 victory.{{cite web|url=http://www.thescore.ie/cork-hurling-final-road-1065565-Sep2013/ |title=All-Ireland SHC 2013: Cork's route to the final |date=3 September 2013 |work=The Score |access-date=4 September 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131004222445/http://www.thescore.ie/cork-hurling-final-road-1065565-Sep2013/ |archive-date=4 October 2013 }} It was their seventh successive championship defeat of Clare, extending the record which stretches back to the 1998 Munster semi-final when Clare last defeated Cork. In total it was the fifth meeting between the counties in 2013, with Clare having won the first three before Cork prevailed in the Munster semi-final.{{cite web|url= http://thescore.thejournal.ie/clare-route-to-all-ireland-hurling-final-1066068-Sep2013/|title= All-Ireland SHC 2013: Clare's route to the final|date=3 September 2013|work=The Score|access-date=3 September 2013}} Cork, who last played in the final in [[2006 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2006]] when they lost by three points to Kilkenny, were bidding to win the title for the first time since [[2005 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2005]] while Clare, who last reached the final in [[2002 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2002]], had won their last All-Ireland in [[1997 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1997]].{{cite web|url=http://munster.gaa.ie/2013/09/03/all-ireland-senior-hurling-championship-final-cork-v-clare/ final.{{cite web|url= http://thescore.thejournal.ie/clare-cork-final-big-screen-ennis-1065778-Sep2013/|title= Clare fans get chance to see All-Ireland Final on big screen... in Ennis|date=3 September http://www.irishtimes.com/sport/intriguing-history-reaches-unforgettable-climax-1.1515038|title= Intriguing history reaches unforgettable climax|date=4 March 2013|work=Irish Times|access-date=4 September 2013}} ===Hurling Stars of the 1980s Team=== The GAA announced on 26 August that a special ''Hurling Stars of the 1980s'' team, a specially-chosen line-up of players who were unsuccessful in winning an All-Ireland medal would be acknowledged on finals day before the senior final.{{cite web|url=http://www.gaa.ie/gaa-news-and-videos/daily-news/3/2608131633-hurling-stars-of-the-80s-team-confirmed/ |title=Hurling Stars of the 80s team confirmed |date=26 August 2013 |work=GAA.ie of the players were put forward by a panel of All-Star and former All-Star selectors who covered Gaelic games for the print and broadcast media during the 1980s.{{cite web|url=http://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/gaa-names-hurling-stars-of-the-80s-team-604867.html|title= GAA names Hurling Stars of the 80s team|date=26 August 2013|work= Irish August 2013|work= Breaking News|access-date=27 August 2013 }} ===Referee=== [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] based referee Brian Gavin was named as the referee for the 2013 All-Ireland final on 26 August.{{cite web|url= http://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/gavin-gets-nod-to-referee-all-ireland-final-241146.html|title= Gavin gets nod to referee All-Ireland final|date=27 August 2013|work= Irish We're just delighted to have another day out and we'll look forward to it."{{cite web|url= http://www.hoganstand.com/clare/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=200676|title= Donnellan delighted to get second chance|date=10 September 2013|work=Hogan Stand|access-date=12 September 2013}} Highlights of the final were shown on ''The Sunday Game'' programme which aired at 9:30pm that night on [[RTÉ Two]] and was presented by [[Des Cahill]] with analysis from [[Donal Óg Cusack]], [[Ger Loughnane]], and [[Ollie Moran]]. Also in that programme, Cork manager [[Jimmy Barry-Murphy]] and captain [[Pa Cronin]] were interviewed by [[Michael Lyster]] from the Cork team hotel, the DT hotel in Dublin. [[Marty Morrissey]] who was at the Clare team hotel, the Clyde Court Hotel, interviewed Clare manager [[Davy Fitzgerald]] and captain Pat Donnellan. ==Pre-match - Replay== ===Build-up=== The replay match was fixed for Saturday 28th rather than a traditional Sunday because the ladies Gaelic football finals are scheduled for the following Sunday, the 29th and are not going to be moved to another date which happened in 2012.{{cite web|url= http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-football/all-ireland-hurling-final-replay-to-be-held-at-5pm-on-saturday-28-september-29564099.html|title=All Ireland hurling final replay to be held at 5pm on Saturday 28 September|date=9 September 2013|work=Irish Independent|access-date=12 September 2013}} The GAA have predicted that the replay will be a sell-out even with the 5pm throw-in time and it will be the first senior final to be played under floodlights.{{cite web|url= http://www.independent.ie/irish-news/gaa-predicts-hurling-replay-sellout-despite-late-throwin-29565764.html|title=GAA predicts hurling replay sell-out despite late throw-in|date=11 September replay|date=10 September 2013|work=Irish Times|access-date=12 September 2013}} The GAA confirmed that there will be ticket reductions for the replay similar to the 2012 replay with stand tickets priced at €50 (down from €80) and terrace tickets at €25 (down from €40).{{cite web|url=http://www.thescore.ie/all-ireland-final-replay-1078443-Sep2013/ |title=GAA to stick with 5pm time for Examiner|access-date=12 September 2013}} Cork manager Jimmy Barry-Murphy commented on the replay saying “It’s more of a game now than it is a final."{{cite web|url=http://www.thescore.ie/jimmy-barry-murphy-cork-clare-replay-1098906-Sep2013/ |title=JBM: Hurling replay feels more like a match than an occasion |date=25 September 2013 |work=The Score http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/clare-and-cork-gear-up-for-sixth-meeting-29608094.html|title=Clare and Cork gear up for sixth meeting|date=25 September 2013|work=Irish But they still have to make the breakthrough and the quicker they make that breakthrough the better."{{cite web|url = http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/new-banner-breed-yet-to-reach-their-peak-louis-mulqueen-29608086.html|title=New Banner breed yet to reach their peak – Louis Mulqueen|date=25 September 2013|work=Irish Independent|access-date=27 September 2013}} Clare manager Davy Fitzgerald is concerned about the number of games the team has played in 2013 saying ""Since the start of February we've been flat out because we played the league campaign at a championship pace, So, I'd be saying to myself: 'Will these games catch up on them?' That's the only concern, but it doesn't seem to have. They seem to be good. I think the only really flat game we had was that Tipperary league game."{{cite web|url = http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/davy-fitzgerald-fears-replay-may-be-one-game-too-many-29614494.html|title=Davy Fitzgerald fears replay may be one game too many|date=27 September 2013|work=Irish Independent|access-date=27 September 2013}} ===Referee=== James McGrath was named as the referee for the replay on 18 September. It will be McGrath's second final after he was in charge of the 2012 Replay final between Kilkenny and Galway.{{cite web|url =http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/james-mcgrath-in-charge-of-all-ireland-hurling-replay-29588528.html|title= James McGrath in charge of All Ireland hurling replay|date=18 September 2013|work=Irish Independent|access-date=24 September 2013}} ===Team news=== The Cork team for the replay was named on 25 September with [[Cian McCarthy]] being named in place of [[Jamie Coughlan]] in the half forward line.{{cite web|url = http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/barrymurphy-puts-faith-in-mccarthy-to-ruffle-banner-halfback-trio-29611760.html|title= Barry-Murphy puts faith in McCarthy to ruffle Banner half-back trio|date=26 September 2013|work=Irish Independent|access-date=26 September 2013}} Clare named an unchanged team for the replay and also for the third game in succession.{{cite web|url = http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/2013/0926/476511-fitzgerald-keeps-faith-with-same-team/|title= Davy Fitzgerald keeps faith with same Clare team for All-Ireland Hurling final replay|date=26 September 2013|work=RTÉ Sport|access-date=26 September 2013}} There had been speculation that [[Darach Honan]] could be replaced before throw-in after he failed to make an impact in the drawn game. A couple of hours before the start of the match, [[Shane O'Donnell]] was told that he would be starting the match in place of Darach Honan.{{cite web|url = http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/no-change-for-clare-but-honan-place-in-doubt-29614495.html|title=No change for Clare but Honan place in doubt|date=27 September 2013|work=Irish Independent|access-date=27 September 2013}} ==Match details - Replay== ===Summary=== [[John Conlon]] got the opening score of the game, a point in the second minute. A hat-trick of goals in the 6th, 14th and 19th minutes at the hill 16 end from late call-up [[Shane O'Donnell]] put Clare on the way to a four-point lead of 3–9 to 1–11 at half time. [[Anthony Nash (hurler)|Anthony Nash]] had blasted a 20-metre free past 12 Clare players on the line for a goal that brought Cork back to within three points in the 16th minute.{{cite web|url = http://www.breakingnews.ie/sport/gaa/clare-win-eight-goal-thriller-608436.html|title= Clare win eight-goal thriller|date=28 September 2013|work=Breaking News|access-date=30 September 2013}} Clare then led by eight points but Cork had drawn level, 1–16 to 3–10, by the 52nd minute. With 18 minutes left the scores were level at 1–16 to 3-10 and they were level again with ten minutes left when [[Séamus Harnedy]] scored with a low shot to the net to make the score 2–16 to 3–13. In the 61st minute, Clare's [[Conor McGrath]] ran at goals and fired the ball high to the left corner of the net for Clare's fourth goal. [[Darach Honan]], who came on as a second-half substitute, got Clare's fifth goal in the 71st minute after he received the ball on the right and managed to get as far as the Cork goals before pushing the ball past the goalkeeper with the ball rolling over the line. {{cite web|url =http://www.hoganstand.com/Cork/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=201822 |title= brilliant Banner prevail in classic|date=28 September 2013|work=Hogan Stand|access-date=30 September 2013}}{{cite web|url = http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/how-the-game-was-won-29620494.html|title= How the game was won|date=30 September 2013|work=Irish Independent|access-date=30 September 2013}}{{cite web|url = http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/allireland-hurling-final-replay-minute-by-minute-29618525.html|title= All-Ireland Hurling Final Replay minute by minute|date=30 September 2013|work=Irish Independent|access-date=30 September 2013}} {{football box |date = 28 September 2013 |time = 17:00 |round = Final Replay |team1 = [[Clare GAA|Clare]]

The Clare team then embarked on a lap of honor around Croke Park.{{cite web|url = https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5gWFKE2rn44|title= All Ireland final captains speech|date=2 October 2013|work=RTÉ Sport|access-date=2 October 2013}} ==Reaction== Clare manager Davy Fitzgerald felt Clare were the better team over the two games saying " In my opinion over the two days we were the better team, I think Cork are a fantastic hurling team, but I really believe that we were the better team over the two days, We’re 2013 All-Ireland champions and it feels so good. I’m so proud of them young boys. They did it and fair play to them.”{{cite web|url = http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/2013/0928/477063-fitzgerald-clare/|title= Cork were fantastic - we were better|date=28 September 2013|work=RTÉ Sport|access-date=30 September 2013}}{{cite web|url = http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-football/colm-keys-conveyor-belt-of-talent-to-keep-banner-on-toes-29622853.html|title= Conveyor belt of talent to keep Banner on toes|date=1 October 2013|work=Irish Independent|access-date=30 September 2013}} Fitzgerald speaking the morning after the game said “I suppose it still has not sunk in, but it is one of immense satisfaction. I am still the same. I am still so thrilled for the lads."{{cite web|url = http://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/nineteen-players-in-davys-living-room-with-mi-wadi-and-biscuits-244745.html|title=Nineteen players in Davy's living room with Mi Wadi and biscuits...|date=29 September 2013|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=30 September 2013}} Fitzgerald also said that it hurt that people did not trust him saying "My one objective was for Clare to win. I wasn't trying to do anything else, only to try and make sure Clare would win. It does hurt when people would cut your throat and knife you in the back. It isn't nice."{{cite web|url = http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/2013/0929/477206-fitzgerald-it-hurt-people-didnt-trust-me/|title=Davy Fitzgerald reveals anguish from earlier this year: 'It did hurt that people didn't trust me'|date=29 September 2013|work=RTÉ Sport|access-date=30 September 2013}} Seven members of Clare's All-Ireland winning side were picked in ''[[The Sunday Game]]'' hurling team of the year.{{cite web|url = http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/2013/0929/477214-sunday-game-team-of-the-year/|title=The Sunday Game Team of the Year|date=28 September 2013|work=RTÉ Sport|access-date=30 September 2013}} Man of the match [[Shane O'Donnell]] who got 3-3 said the county's win means “absolutely everything” revealing that he did not know he was starting until hours before the game.{{cite web|url = http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/2013/0928/477084-odonnell-win-means-absolutely-everything/|title=O'Donnell: All-Ireland win means 'absolutely everything'|date=28 September 2013|work=RTÉ Sport|access-date=30 September 2013}}{{cite web|url=http://www.thescore.ie/live-cork-clare-1104952-Sep2013/ |title=As it happened: Cork v Clare, All-Ireland senior hurling final replay |date=28 September 2013 |work=The Score |access-date=30 September 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131002064613/http://www.thescore.ie/live-cork-clare-1104952-Sep2013/ |archive-date=2 October 2013 }} O'Donnell was named by ''[[The Sunday Game]]'' as the man of the match for the replay on the night of the match. At the teams celebration banquet at the Clyde Court Hotel in Dublin, he received his award from [[List of Presidents of the Gaelic Athletic Association|GAA President]] [[Liam O'Neill]] and [[Michael Lyster]]. Cork manager Jimmy Barry-Murphy acknowledged Clare's win saying "There is no disgrace in getting beaten by a team like Clare, you have to acknowledge they deserved their victory".{{cite web|url = http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/its-no-disgrace-losing-to-clare-jimmy-barrymurphy-29620459.html|title= 'It's no disgrace losing to Clare' - Jimmy Barry-Murphy|date=30 September 2013|work=Irish Independent|access-date=30 September 2013}} Former [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] hurler, [[John Mullane]] writing in the ''[[Irish Independent]]'' praised Clare manager Davy Fitzgerald and said "starting with Shane O'Donnell was a masterstroke".{{cite web|url = http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/john-mullane-davy-deserves-his-day-in-the-sun-29620483.html|title= Davy deserves his day in the sun|date=30 September 2013|work=Irish Independent|access-date=30 September 2013}} [[Jamesie O'Connor]] also writing in the ''Irish Independent'' believes that Clare have reached the summit earlier than expected saying "With the way Clare finished the year I think the consensus now is that the best team in the country came out on top, it's hard to believe that the hurling year gave us what it did, especially with the old order contesting the league final back in April. They will be back in 2014 but on a far more level playing pitch. Roll on 2014."{{cite web|url = http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/jamesie-oconnor-clare-have-reached-the-summit-earlier-than-expected-29618520.html|title= Clare have reached the summit earlier than expected|date=29 September 2013|work=Irish Independent|access-date=30 September 2013}} Former [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] All Ireland winner and hurling analyst [[Daithí Regan]] thinks that the Clare system was the key as best team of the summer won out, saying "The big question now is, how many can Clare win with this crop of young lads. I was talking to Jamesie O’Connor after the game about what we can expect from this side over the next few years. He made the point that it’s a high-octane, high-energy game that Clare play. And it takes its toll and makes demands on players. But they’re at such an age profile at the moment that they’ll want more. When the celebrations die down, they’ll go back at it and you know I think because of their age profile they’ll be hungry and burnout won’t be an issue."{{cite web|url = http://thescore.thejournal.ie/daitho-regan-davy-fits-column-1107620-Sep2013/|title= System was the key as best team of the summer won out|date=1 October 2013|work=The Score|access-date=30 September 2013}} Double All Ireland winning manager [[Ger Loughnane]] is confident that this is the start of a golden era for hurling in Clare, saying "“This has been a magical year – the best year I can remember for hurling, but you know we have the prospect that next year and the year after will be even better."{{cite web|url = http://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/loughnane-hopeful-clare-wont-disappear-like-tipp-244962.html|title= Loughnane hopeful Clare won't 'disappear like Tipp'|date=2 October 2013|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=2 October 2013}} British newspaper ''[[The Guardian]]'' in its editorial section, hailed the 'ancient Irish' game of hurling as a beacon of sporting courage and commitment, Hopefully the Gaelic Athletic Association will do all sports fans everywhere a massive favour and produce DVD copies of this memorable game, where Clare emerged victorious."{{cite web|url = http://www.independent.ie/sport/the-guardian-lauds-hurling-and-lashes-premier-league-prima-donnas-29631255.html|title= The Guardian lauds hurling and lashes Premier League prima donnas|date=2 October 2013|work=Irish Independent|access-date=4 October 2013}} In 2017, after three years of under-performing, former Clare manager [[Ger Loughnane]] criticized the team that won the title saying "it was the greatest fluke of all time, they didn't beat either Tipperary or Kilkenny - the Litmus test in this era, until they show consistency and beat a big team in a big game, you'd have to say that this Clare team are over-rated.{{cite web|url= http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/winning-allireland-in-2013-was-the-greatest-fluke-of-all-time-ger-loughnane-slams-limited-clare-35789300.html|title= 'Winning All-Ireland in 2013 was the greatest fluke of all time' - Ger Loughnane slams 'limited' Clare|date=5 June 2017|work=Irish Independent|access-date=6 July 2017}}{{cite web|url= http://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/weve-underperformed-but-2013-was-no-fluke-says-colm-galvin-454188.html|title= We've underperformed, but 2013 was no fluke, says Colm Galvin|date=6 July 2017|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=6 July 2017}} ==Homecoming== The Clare team arrived back in [[Ennis]] at 9.30pm on the day after the game on an open top bus. The team traveled by train from [[Dublin Heuston railway station|Heuston Station]] in Dublin to Limerick and then by bus to Ennis. En route they stopped at [[Cratloe]], [[Sixmilebridge]], [[Newmarket on Fergus]], and [[Clarecastle]]. There was a reception held at Tim Smyth Park in Ennis which was attended by 30,000 people. Both sets of players, the senior panel and the under 21 winning panel were introduced on stage by MC's Syl O'Connor of [[Clare FM]] and RTÉ's [[Marty Morrissey]].{{cite web|url = http://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/30000-welcome-clare-hurlers-home-608519.html|title=30,000 welcome Clare hurlers home|date=29 September 2013|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=30 September 2013}}{{cite web|url = http://www.irishmirror.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/hurling-news/all-ireland-champions-clare-homecoming-2322516|title=Clare receive heroes welcome as they're roared home by 30,000 delirious fans|date=29 September 2013|work=Irish Mirror|access-date=30 September 2013}}{{cite web|url = http://www.breakingnews.ie/sport/gaa/30000-welcome-clare-hurlers-home-608519.html|title=30,000 welcome Clare hurlers home|date=29 September 2013|work=Breaking News|access-date=4 November 2013}} On 2 October, a Clare 'A' team played a Clare 'B' team in the annual GOAL challenge which was played in [[Sixmilebridge]]. The match was a 13 a side game with the 'A' team winning by 7–3 to 6–4.{{cite web|url = http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/davy-fitzgerald-back-between-sticks-as-clare-go-for-goal-29630747.html|title= Davy Fitzgerald back between sticks as Clare go for GOAL|date=3 October 2013|work=Irish Independent|access-date=3 October 2013}} A crowd of 6,000 fans attended the match where Shane O’Donnell required a Garda escort to get him to the team bus after the game.{{cite web|url = http://www.independent.ie/irish-news/shanemania-hits-fever-pitch-as-goal-hero-needs-garda-escort-29633369.html|title= Shane-mania hits fever pitch as goal hero needs garda escort|date=4 October 2013|work=Irish Independent|access-date=4 October 2013}}{{cite web|url = http://www.irishexaminer.com/ireland/garda-escort-called-as-shaneomania-runs-wild-245247.html|title= Garda escort called as Shaneomania runs wild|date=4 October 2013|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=4 October 2013}} On 4 October, Clare manager [[Davy Fitzgerald]] along with players [[Shane O'Donnell]] and [[Patrick Donnellan]] and the Liam MacCarthy Cup appeared as guests on ''[[The Late Late Show (Ireland)|The Late Late Show]]''.{{cite web|url = http://www.rte.ie/ten/news/2013/1004/478277-whitmore-is-among-late-late-guests/|title= Whitmore and Clare hurlers for Late Late|date=4 October 2013|work=RTÉ News|access-date=4 October 2013}} ==Awards== The nominations for the 2013 [[GAA All Stars Awards winners (hurling)|GAA-GPA Hurling All-Stars]] were announced on 2 October with Clare receiving thirteen nominations with Cork receiving nine.{{cite web|url = http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/clare-lead-the-way-in-gaa-gpa-hurling-allstars-29629264.html|title= Clare lead the way in GAA GPA Hurling All-Stars|date=2 October 2013|work=Irish Independent|access-date=3 October 2013}}{{cite web|url = http://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/all-star-post-mortems-begin-245063.html|title=All Star post-mortems begin|date=2 October 2013|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=3 October 2013}} Cian Dillon and Patrick O’Connor were the only Clare players not nominated.{{cite web|url = http://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/deegan-bemused-by-dillon-and-oconnor-omission-245261.html|title=Deegan bemused by Dillon and O'Connor omission|date=4 October 2013|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=4 October 2013}} The final team selection was made on 6 November before the team were presented with their awards two days later at a banquet at Croke Park. Clare's won eight places on the All-Stars team with David McInerney, Brendan Bugler, Pat Donnellan, Colm Galvin, Conor Ryan, Tony Kelly, Pádraic Collins and Conor McGrath all winning awards. Cork won three awards with Anthony Nash, Séamus Harnedy and Patrick Horgan being named on the team.{{cite web|url = http://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/eight-clare-men-claim-hurling-all-stars-612457.html|title=Eight Clare men claim hurling All-Stars|date=7 November 2013|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=7 November 2013}}{{cite web|url = http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/martin-breheny-stars-align-to-leave-big-guns-in-shadows-29733601.html|title=Martin Breheny: Stars align to leave big guns in shadows|date=7 November 2013|work=Irish Independent|access-date=7 November 2013}}{{cite web|url = http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/2013/1106/485046-clare-dominate-2013-hurling-all-stars/|title=All-Ireland champions Clare dominate 2013 hurling All-Stars|date=7 November 2013|work=RTÉ Sport|access-date=7 November 2013}}{{cite web|url = http://www.hoganstand.com/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=204162|title=Hurling All-Stars: Champions Clare dominate with eight |date=7 November 2013|work=Hogan Stand|access-date=7 November 2013}} {{cite web|url = http://www.hoganstand.com/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=202088|title=Banner dominate All Star hurling nominations|date=2 October 2013|work=Hogan Stand|access-date=3 October 2013}} The three nominations for the [[GPA Hurler of the Year]] were Tony Kelly and Pádraic Collins of Clare, and Anthony Nash of Cork. Also announced were the three nominations for the [[All Stars Young Hurler of the Year|GPA Young Hurler of the Year]] which were Tony Kelly, Pádraic Collins, and David McInerney from Clare.{{cite web|url=http://www.gaa.ie/gaa-news-and-videos/daily-news/1/0210132246-gaa-gpa-hurling-all-stars-nominations-sponsored-by-opel/ |title=2013 GAA GPA Hurling All Star Nominations |date=2 October 2013 |work=GAA.ie |access-date=3 October 2013 |url-status=dead 2013 }}{{cite web|url=http://www.thescore.ie/2013-allstar-awards-1111379-Oct2013/ |title=13 Clare players nominated for 2013 GAA/GPA hurling Allstars |date=2 October 2013 |work=The Score
