The replay was held on 27 September 2014. The final was the seventh national final, between League and Championship, out of a possible 12, that Kilkenny and Tipperary had met in since 2009.{{cite web|url = http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/time-for-tipperary-to-restore-balance-to-great-rivalry-30517657.html|title= Time for Tipperary to restore balance to great |date=19 August 2014|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=19 August 2014}}{{cite web|url = http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/hurlings-status-quo-remains-but-not-for-much-longer-30533518.html|title= Hurling's status quo remains - but not for much longer|date=25 August 2014|work=Irish Independent|access-date=26 August 2014}}{{cite web|url=http://www.thescore.ie/kilkenny-tipperary-best-ever-hurling-games-1641084-Sep2014/ |title=Five of the best: The greatest Kilkenny – Tipperary games in the modern era |date=1 September 2014 |work=The Score |access-date=2 September 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140903121357/http://www.thescore.ie/kilkenny-tipperary-best-ever-hurling-games-1641084-Sep2014/ |archive-date=3 September 2014 }}{{cite web|url = http://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/columnists/enda-mcevoy/putting-a-new-slant-on-old-kilkenny-tipp-rivalry-284520.html|title= Putting a new slant on old Kilkenny-Tipp rivalry|date=1 September 2014|work=Irish Examiner |access-date=2 September 2014}} The final was shown live in Ireland on [[RTÉ One]] as part of ''[[The Sunday Game]]'' live programme, presented by [[Michael Lyster]] from Croke Park, with studio analysis from [[Cyril Farrell]], [[Tomás Mulcahy]] and [[Ger Loughnane]]. Match commentary was provided by [[Ger Canning]] with analysis by [[Michael Duignan (hurler)|Michael Duignan]]. The game was also shown live on [[Sky Sports]], presented by [[Rachel Wyse]] and [[Brian Carney (rugby)|Brian Carney]]. The first match finished in a draw for the third year in a row after no draws since the 1959 final.{{cite web|url = http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/tipps-closing-burst-squares-epic-contest-with-kilkenny-30569107.html|title= Tipp's closing burst squares epic contest with Kilkenny |date=8 September 2014|work=Irish Independent|access-date=9 September 2014}} {{cite web|url = http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/as-it-happened-kilkenny-v-tipperary-30565848.html|title= As it happened: Kilkenny v Tipperary|date=7 September 2014|work=Irish Independent|access-date=9 September 2014}} The final has been described by many as the greatest final in history and also the greatest hurling match in history.{{cite web|url = http://thescore.thejournal.ie/all-ireland-hurling-final-1661397-Sep2014/|title= Was Sunday the greatest All-Ireland hurling final of all time?|date=8 September 2014|work=The Score|access-date=9 September 2014}}{{cite web|url = http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/was-final-the-best-game-of-hurling-ever-to-be-played-30571635.html|title= Was final the best game of hurling ever to be played? |date=9 September 2014|work=Irish Independent|access-date=9 September 2014}}{{cite web|url = http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/tipp-and-cats-serve-up-the-greatest-game-ive-ever-seen-30569085.html|title= Tipp and Cats serve up the greatest game I've ever seen |date=8 September 2014|work=Irish Independent|access-date=9 September 2014}}{{cite web|url = http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/tipp-change-the-terms-of-battle-to-end-doubts-over-character-30569038.html|title= Tipp change the terms of battle to end doubts over character |date=8 September 2014|work=Irish Independent|access-date=9 September 2014}}{{cite web|url = http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/awesome-hawkeye-final-surpasses-any-that-ive-seen-30569036.html|title= Awesome 'Hawk-Eye' final surpasses any that I've seen |date=8 September 2014|work=Irish Independent|access-date=9 September 2014}}{{cite web|url = http://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/ger-cunningham-hurling-can-get-even-better-285885.html|title= Ger Cunningham: ‘Hurling can get even better’|date=11 September 2013|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=11 September 2014}} Tipperary had a free from 97 metres out in injury time with the scores level. [[John O'Dwyer]] took the free which was hit just wide to the right and required confirmation from Hawk-eye that it was wide.{{cite web|url =http://thescore.thejournal.ie/hawkeye-all-ireland-final-tupperary-1659600-Sep2014/|title= Here’s the Hawkeye call that decided the All-Ireland hurling final|date=8 September 2014|work=The Score|access-date=9 September 2014}}{{cite web|url =http://thescore.thejournal.ie/tipperary-kilkenny-live-1659218-Sep2014/|title= As It Happened: Tipperary v Kilkenny, All-Ireland senior hurling final|date=8 September 2014|work=The Score|access-date=9 September 2014}}{{cite July 2015|title=Statistical breakdown of All-Ireland Hurling final between Kilkenny and Tipperary, |date=8 September 2014 |work=GAA.ie |access-date=9 September 2014}} The replay was held on 27 win |date=27 September 2014|work=Irish Independent|access-date=30 September 2014}} It was their 35th All-Ireland title and the 10th senior All-Ireland of [[Brian Cody]]’s managerial career along with the 10th All-Ireland of [[Henry Shefflin]]’s playing career.{{cite web|url = http://munster.gaa.ie/2014/09/27/all-ireland-senior-hurling-championship-final-replay-kilkenny-v-tipperary/|title= KILKENNY 2-17 TIPPERARY 2-14|date=27 September 2014|work=Munster GAA |access-date=30 September 2014}}{{cite web|url=http://www.thescore.ie/kilkenny-tipperary-live-2-1693736-Sep2014/ |title=As It Happened: Final: Kilkenny v Tipperary at [[Croke Park]]]] It was the sixth successive year that the counties had played each other in the championship, with Kilkenny winning 4 times. Paul Reville |} ===Reaction=== Tipperary's [[Pádraic Maher]] said that he knew the injury-time attempt from John O’Dwyer was wide before being confirmed by Hawk-Eye saying "“I was standing right behind Bubbles. I stood right behind his free and I thought it was for three-quarters of the way going over the bar, but it just curled off at the finish. I didn’t even look up at the Hawk Eye because I f***ing knew it was gone wide.Excuse my language, but that’s just the ups and downs of the game. It was fantastic. It must have been some game to watch and it was great to be a part of it. It’s a big game again in three weeks’ time and we'll just try and come out the right side of the result.”{{cite web|url = http://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/i-didnt-even-look-up-at-the-hawk-eye-i-knew-it-was-wide-285360.html|title= ‘I didn’t even look up at the Hawk Eye, I knew it was wide’|date=8 September 2014|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=9 September 2014}} Tipperary manager [[Eamon O'Shea]] was focusing on the positives after the draw saying ""I feel I was a participant in a brilliant game," "Of course you feel drained, you try to win the game right until the end, but I just felt the occasion in terms of the game was just one of those was games..."I don't know what it looked like when you're dispassionate...but I just felt it was one of those games, like in 2009 (All-Ireland Final which Kilkenny won), it was just one of those games where you felt it was just good to be there." O'Shea also thought that John O'Dwyer's late free had gone over the bar saying " "I felt he had a chance," I thought it was over but obviously HawkEye said no. He got a great strike on it and he was unlucky." "I'm looking forward to the next day," "When you're involved in a game like that, from my perspective, you just try and win the game right until the end. You don't get a chance to get too emotional about it so I'm just looking forward to the next day, "I thought they (Tipperary) did really well today. They worked really hard, they believed in what they were doing. We could have won it, we might have lost it because we were playing against a fantastic team."{{cite web|url=http://www.gaa.ie/gaa-news-and-videos/daily-news/1/0709141832-reaction-oshea-looks-to-the-positives/ |title=Eamon O'Shea reaction |date=8 September 2014 |work=GAA.ie |access-date=9 September 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140911002347/http://www.gaa.ie/gaa-news-and-videos/daily-news/1/0709141832-reaction-oshea-looks-to-the-positives/ |archive-date=11 September 2014 }} Highlights of the final were shown on ''The Sunday Game'' programme which aired at 9:30pm that night on [[RTÉ Two]] and was presented by [[Des Cahill]] with analysis from [[Dónal Óg Cusack]], [[Liam Sheedy]], and [[Eddie Brennan]]. On the man of the match award shortlist were [[Richie Hogan]], [[John O'Dwyer]] and [[Cathal Barrett]], with [[Richie Hogan]] winning the award.{{cite web|url = http://www.news.msn.ie/all-ireland-shc-man-of-the-match-2-1660011-Sep2014/|title= RICHIE HOGAN HAS been named as the man of the match |date=7 September 2014|work=News.msn|access-date=9 September 2014}} ==Pre-match - Replay== It was announced right after the drawn match that the replay would take place on Saturday, 27 September at 5pm at Croke park.{{cite web|url=http://www.thescore.ie/all-ireland-final-tickets-2-1660581-Sep2014/ |title=GAA cut ticket prices for All-Ireland hurling final replay again |date=9 September 2014 |work=The Score |access-date=10 September 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140910200511/http://www.thescore.ie/all-ireland-final-tickets-2-1660581-Sep2014/ |archive-date=10 September 2014 }} The drawn match was the highest scoring 70-minute final since being introduced in 1975, and the first time in championship history that a total of 31 points wasn't enough to win the final. It was also the first time in history that Kilkenny and Tipperary drew in a championship game.{{cite web|url =https://tipperary.gaa.ie/ireland-senior-hurling-championship-final-replay-kilkenny-v-tipperary/|title= All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final Replay – Kilkenny v Tipperary|date=3 May 2014|work=Tipperary GAA|access-date=23 September 2014}} Kilkenny were slight favorites to win the replay, priced at 10/11 with [[Paddy Power]], with Tipperary priced at 6/5 and the draw at 9/1.{{cite web|url = http://www.paddypower.com/bet/gaa-sports|title= 2014 All Ireland Hurling Final replay match betting |date=3 September 2014|work=Paddy Power|access-date=3 September 2014}} ===Tickets=== The GAA announced on 8 September that ticket prices for the replay would be reduced with stand tickets reduced to €50 from €80 and terrace tickets priced at €25.{{cite web|url = http://thescore.thejournal.ie/all-ireland-final-tickets-2-1660581-Sep2014/|title= GAA cut ticket prices for All-Ireland hurling final replay again|date=8 September 2014|work=The Score|access-date=9 September 2014}} ===Referee=== [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] official [[Brian Gavin (referee)|Brian Gavin]] was named as the referee for the replay on 10 September. It was the third time he has refereed a senior final as he did the 2011 final between the same two teams and the drawn 2013 final between Clare and Cork.{{cite web|url = http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/offalys-brian-gavin-to-ref-allireland-hurling-replay-between-kilkenny-and-tipperary-30577599.html|title= Offaly's Brian Gavin to ref All-Ireland hurling replay between Kilkenny and Tipperary |date=11 September 2014|work=Irish Independent|access-date=11 September 2014}} Wexford's James Owens was the standby referee with James McGrath as the other linesman, while the sideline official was Alan Kelly from Galway.{{cite web|url = http://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/gavin-set-to-take-charge-of-all-ireland-replay-285883.html|title= Gavin set to take charge of All-Ireland replay|date=11 September 2014|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=11 September 2014}} Unlike the 2013 All Ireland Final between Cork and Clare where Gavin played 30 seconds over the added on time in which time Clare scored an equalizing point Gavin did not allow any additional time in this game. ===Team News=== Both teams for the replay were announced on 25 September with Kilkenny making three changes to the team.{{cite web|url = http://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/three-changes-for-cats-as-tipp-sweat-on-knocks-288721.html|title= Three changes for Cats as Tipp sweat on knocks|date=26 September 2014|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=26 September 2014}} John Power came in to replace Walter Walsh, Padraig Walsh came in at wing-back in place of Joey Holden while Kieran Joyce replaced Brian Hogan. Tipperary made no changes to their team and started with the same fifteen.{{cite web|url = http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/brian-hogan-and-walter-walsh-axed-as-kilkenny-ring-changes-for-replay-30616993.html|title= Brian Hogan and Walter Walsh axed as Kilkenny ring changes for replay |date=26 September 2014|work=Irish Independent |access-date=26 September 2014}} ==Match details== ===Summary=== Tipperary scored the first goal of the game in the 28th minute when Lar Corbett passed to the left to Séamus Callanan who passed the ball past the goalkeeper and into the net.{{cite web|url = September 2014|work=Irish Independent|access-date=3 October 2014}} Tipperary were leading the game by two points at half time on a 1–7 to 0-8 scoreline.{{cite web|url web|url=http://www.thescore.ie/john-gardiner-column-2-1697189-Sep2014/|title=John Gardiner: How Kilkenny’s defensive tweak trumped Tipp – and why the GAA needs pro refs|date=2 October 2014|work=The {{Short description|none}} {{Infobox football match | title = 2015 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Final | image = Croke park hogan stand.jpg | image_size = 250 | event = [[2015 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]] | team1 = [[Kilkenny county hurling team|Kilkenny]] | team1association = [[File:Colours of Kilkenny.svg|40px]] | team1score = 1-22 | team2 = [[Galway county hurling team|Galway]] | team2association = [[File:Colours of Galway.svg|40px]] | team2score = 1-18 | details = | date = 6 September 2015 | stadium = [[Croke Park]] | city = [[Dublin]] | man_of_the_match1a = [[Michael Fennelly (hurler)|Michael Fennelly]]{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/sunday-game-hurling-final-2015-motm-2315453-Sep2015/|title=Do you agree with The Sunday Game’s man-of-the-match selection?|date=7 September 2015|work=The 42|access-date=8 September 2015}}{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/kilkenny-7-and-galway-4-dominate-the-sunday-game-hurling-team-of-the-year/31506869.html|title=Kilkenny (7) and Galway (4) dominate The Sunday Game Hurling team of the Year|work=Irish Independent|date=7 September 2015|quote=Paul Murphy, Joey Holden and Cillian Buckley were chose in the backs, man-of-the-match Michael Fennelly got the nod in midfield…}} | referee = [[James Owens (referee)|James Owens]] ([[Wexford GAA|Wexford]]) | weather = Cloudy
{{convert|14|°C|°F}}{{Cite web |url=http://www.met.ie/climate/daily-data.asp |title=Met Eireann: Daily Data 06/09/15 |access-date=4 September 2016 |archive-date=16 September 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160916044808/http://www.met.ie/climate/daily-data.asp |url-status=dead }} | previous = [[2014 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2014]] | next = [[2016 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2016]] }} The '''2015 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final''', the 128th event of its kind and the culmination of the [[2015 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]], was played at [[Croke Park]] in [[Dublin]] on 6 September 2015. Kilkenny retained their title beating Galway by 1-22 to 1-18.{{cite web|url=http://www.gaa.ie/fixtures-and-results/national-fixtures/gaa-hurling-all-ireland-senior-championship/ |title=2015 Fixtures and Results |date=1 September 2015 |work=GAA.ie |access-date=2 September 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150903021855/http://www.gaa.ie/fixtures-and-results/national-fixtures/gaa-hurling-all-ireland-senior-championship/ |archive-date=3 September 2015 }}{{cite web|url=http://www.irishmirror.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/kilkenny-v-galway-recap-relive-6392791|title=Kilkenny v Galway recap: Relive all the action from the All-Ireland hurling final|date=7 September 2015|work=Irish Mirror|access-date=8 September 2015}} The win was the 36th All-Ireland title for Kilkenny and the 11th under [[Brian Cody]].{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/all-so-very-familiar-as-codys-crew-sink-tribesmen-31506540.html|title=All so very familiar as Cody's crew sink Tribesmen|date=7 September 2015|work=Irish Independent|access-date=8 September 2015}}{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/henry-shefflin-you-just-have-to-hold-your-hands-up-and-say-kilkenny-are-the-best-31506025.html|title=Henry Shefflin: You just have to hold your hands up and say Kilkenny are the best|date=7 September 2015|work=Irish Independent|access-date=8 September 2015}}{{cite web|url=http://www.irishmirror.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/hurling-match-reports/kilkenny-1-22-galway-1-6393676|title=Kilkenny 1-22 Galway 1-18: Cats crowned All-Ireland champions after brilliant second-half performance|date=7 September 2015|work=Irish Mirror|access-date=8 September 2015}} The final was shown live in Ireland on [[RTÉ One]] as part of ''[[The Sunday Game]]'' live programme, presented by [[Michael Lyster]] from Croke Park, with studio analysis from [[Cyril Farrell]], [[Henry Shefflin]] and [[Anthony Daly (hurler)|Anthony Daly]]. Match commentary was provided by [[Ger Canning]] with analysis by [[Michael Duignan (hurler)|Michael Duignan]]. The game was also shown live on [[Sky Sports]], presented by [[Rachel Wyse]] and [[Brian Carney (rugby)|Brian Carney]] with studio analysis from [[J. J. Delaney]], [[Ollie Canning]] and [[Jamesie O'Connor]]. The match was the third most-watched event on Irish television in 2015, with an average audience of 739,600.{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/all-ireland-football-final-most-watched-irish-tv-2344282-Sep2015/|title=All-Ireland Football Final the most-watched show on Irish television so far this year|date=21 September 2015|work=The 42|access-date=22 September 2015}} For the first time since 2011, the final did not go into a replay. ==Background== {{main article|Galway–Kilkenny hurling rivalry}} This was the 41st championship meeting between the two sides, with Kilkenny dominating the series with 29 victories. Galway had beaten Kilkenny on 9 occasions while there have been two drawn games. In their most recent meeting Kilkenny defeated Galway by 1-25 to 2-15 in the [[2015 Leinster Senior Hurling Championship Final|2015 Leinster final]] on 5 July.{{cite news | url=http://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/kikenny-stay-on-course-for-familiar-destination-340926.html| title=Kikenny stay on course for familiar destination| publisher=Irish Examiner| date=6 July 2015| access-date=24 August 2015|first=Michael|last=Moynihan}} The two sides had previously played six times in All-Ireland finals, with Kilkenny once again dominating by winning four of the previous deciders ([[1975 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1975]], [[1979 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1979]], [[1993 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1993]], [[2012 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2012]]). Galway's lone All-Ireland defeat of Kilkenny came in [[1987 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1987]], while there has been one drawn decider.{{cite web|url= http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/big-3-and-high-fives-to-haunt-galway-31496194.html|title= 'Big 3' and high fives to haunt Galway?|date=2 September 2015|work=Irish Independent|access-date=2 September 2015}} Kilkenny were hoping to retain their All-Ireland crown and claim an 8th All-Ireland title in ten years. Victory would also ensure an 11th All-Ireland title under the management of [[Brian Cody]] and a 36th All-Ireland title over all. Galway were hoping to win their first All-Ireland title since [[1988 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1988]].{{cite web|url= http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/victory-would-set-us-up-for-a-number-of-years-cunningham-31492423.html|title= Victory would set us up for a number of years - Cunningham|date=1 September 2015|work=Irish Independent|access-date=2 September 2015}} Kilkenny were favorites to win the match, priced at 1/2 with [[Paddy Power]], with Galway priced at 2/1 and the draw at 9/1. If the match was a draw it would be the fourth year in a row that the match would have finished in a draw.{{cite web|url=http://www.paddypower.com/bet/gaa-sports/gaa-matches/all-ireland-hurling-matches/Kilkenny-v-Galway-9301272.html|title= Kilkenny v Galway 6 September 2015|date=25 August attendance = 58,495 }} ==Pre-match== ===Jubilee team=== The [[Cork GAA|Cork]] All-Ireland-winning team of [[1990 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1990]], who won the title following a 5-15 to 2-21 defeat of Galway, were the jubilee team that were presented to the crowd before the final. ===Ticketing=== With a stadium capacity of 82,300, the 32 individual [[Gaelic Athletic Association county|county boards]] received 60,000 tickets. Schools and third level colleges got 2,500 tickets, while season ticket holders were entitled to 5,500 tickets. 1,000 tickets were given to overseas clubs. The [[Camogie Association|Camogie]], [[Ladies' Gaelic Football Association|Ladies' Football]], Handball and Rounders Associations were each allocated about 200 tickets, as were the jubilee teams and mini-7s which played at half-time. Galway's ticket allocation was expected to be around 7,000 as the county was contesting both the senior and minor All-Ireland finals. 5,000 tickets went to Kilkenny as it is a smaller county with fewer clubs, while another 1,000 will be given to clubs in [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] due to their participation in the All-Ireland minor final. The tickets that were allocated to the participating counties were divided among the clubs. Senior hurling clubs got the biggest allocation while intermediate and junior clubs also got a smaller share. Football clubs received a lower percentage. The allocation was based on the number of members and the number of teams in each club. The match was shown live on a big screen at [[Eyre Square]] in Galway.{{cite web|url= http://www.the42.ie/eyre-square-all-ireland-hurling-final-2311076-Sep2015/|title=Galway’s Eyre Square will be hopping for Sunday’s All-Ireland hurling final|date=5 September 2015|work=The 42|access-date=8 September 2015}} ===Related events=== The [[2015 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|2015 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Final]] between Galway and Tipperary was played as a curtain-raiser to the senior final.{{cite web|url= http://www.hoganstand.com/Tipperary/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=242608|title=All-Ireland MHC semi-final: Tipp young guns shoot down Dubs|date=16 August 2015|work=Hogan Stand|access-date=27 August 2015}} Galway won the game on a 4-13 to 1-16 scoreline.{{cite web|url=http://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/galways-minors-win-all-ireland-title-with-devastating-goal-fest-in-second-half-694519.html|title=Galway's minors win All-Ireland title with devastating goal-fest in second half|date=7 September 2015|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=8 September 2015}} ==Match summary== ===Officials=== On 24 August 2015 the officials were chosen for the final by the [[Gaelic Athletic Association|GAA]], led by [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] referee [[James Owens (referee)|James Owens]]. His umpires on the day were James Dunbar, John Clarke, David Owens (Askamore) and Ian Plunkett (Marshalstown). [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]]’s Johnny Ryan was the standby referee. The other linesman was [[James McGrath (referee)|James McGrath]] ([[Westmeath GAA|Westmeath]]) and the sideline official was Owen Elliott ([[Antrim GAA|Antrim]]). Owens has also refereed the [[2007 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|2007 All-Ireland minor final]], the [[2008 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|2008 All-Ireland under-21 final]] and the [[2015 All-Ireland Senior Club Hurling Championship Final|2015 All-Ireland club final]].{{cite news | url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/james-owens-realises-lifetime-goal-to-be-named-allireland-hurling-final-referee-31473630.html| title=James Owens realises 'lifetime goal' to be named All-Ireland hurling final referee| publisher=Irish Independent| date=24 August 2015| access-date=24 August 2015|first=Michael|last=Verney}}{{cite news | url=http://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/wexford-s-james-owens-to-referee-all-ireland-hurling-final-1.2327253| title=Wexford’s James Owens to referee All-Ireland hurling final| publisher=Irish Times| date=24 August 2015| access-date=24 August 2015|first=Seán|last=Moran}} ===Team news=== Both Kilkenny and Galway named unchanged sides for final.{{cite web|url= http://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/galway-remain-unchanged-for-croker-date-with-destiny-694359.html|title=Galway remain unchanged for Croker date with destiny|date=5 September 2015|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=8 September 2015}} Jackie Tyrrell and Richie Power both returned to the Kilkenny squad after recovering from injury.{{cite web|url= http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/kilkenny-and-galway-unchanged-for-final-31504051.html|title=Kilkenny and Galway unchanged for final|date=5 September 2015|work=Irish Independent|access-date=8 September 2015}} ===Summary=== Joe Canning got the first score of the game from a close-range free after two minutes. Johnny Coen blocked a goal-bound shot from Walter Walsh after four minutes with the scores level at two points each. In the fourteenth minute with Galway leading by two points, Walter Walsh burst in from the right and hand passed to TJ Reid who shot low into the back of the net to put Kilkeeny into a one-point lead. After twenty three minutes, Joe Canning pointed another free to put Galway back in front by one.{{cite web|url= http://www.hoganstand.com/Kilkenny/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=243713|title=All-Ireland SHC final: consummate Cats roar to 36th crown|date=6 September 2015|work=Hogan Stand|access-date=8 September 2015}} Jason Flynn then pointed a free from long range to increase the lead to two points a minute later. Jason Flynn got his third point of the game in the twenty eighth minute to put four between the sides. With a minute to half time, a dangerous high foul by Johnny Coen on Colin Fennelly earned him a yellow card when most people including all members of the ''[[The Sunday Game|Sunday Game]]'' panel expected a red card. Half-time score was Kilkenny 1-8 Galway 0-14.{{cite web|url= http://www.the42.ie/live-kilkenny-galway-all-ireland-final-2314718-Sep2015/|title=All-Ireland SHC final: as it happened|date=6 September 2015|work=The 42|access-date=8 September 2015}} The first score of the second half came after four minutes with Conor Fogarty scoring from a free. TJ Reid then scored with another free and then a sixty five to level the scores. David Collins then got a point to put Galway back in front before Richie Hogan again got the equalizer. After forty nine minutes, Conor Whelan with the help of HawkEye put just one point between the sides with a shot from a very tight angle on the right. With six minutes to go Colin Fennelly pointed after Joe Canning had earlier missed from a free to put Kilkenny four points in front. Conor Whelan missed a goal chance for Galway with four minutes to go when his weak shot went low passed the left post. Colin Fennelly then got a second point to put five between them with two minutes to go. Two quick points from Michael Fennelly and Walter Walsh put seven between them before Joe Canning scored a goal with a low shot to the net from a free for the final score of the game. The final score is Kilkenny 1-22 Galway 1-18.{{cite web|url= http://www.the42.ie/kilkenny-galway-liam-maccarthy-cup-2-2315200-Sep2015/|title=5 talking points as Kilkenny celebrate again and Galway’s wait goes on|date=6 September 2015|work=The 42|access-date=8 September 2015}}{{cite web|url= http://www.gaa.ie/gaa-news-and-videos/daily-news/1/0709151845-kilkenny-galway-a-statistical-breakdown-/|title=Statistical breakdown|date=8 September 2015|work=GAA.ie|access-date=9 September 2015}} ==Match details== {{Football box | date = 6 September 2015 | round = | time = 15:30 | team1 = [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] [[File:Colours of Kilkenny.svg|20px|border]] | score = 1-22 - 1-18 | report = [http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/2015/0906/726081-kilkenny-v-galway/ Report] | goals1 = TJ Reid (1-7, 0-5 frees, 0-2 65s); We went in at half-time three points down and that’s not a bad position to be in and I thought the second-half response from our players was magnificent. I thought the relentless spirit, attitude and hurling that they showed was top class and it was a hard fought victory, there’s no doubt about that. “{{cite web|url= http://www.hoganstand.com/Kilkenny/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=243716|title=Reaction: Cody delighted by second-half display|date=6 September 2015|work=Hogan Stand|access-date=8 September 2015}}{{cite web|url= http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/kilkenny-boss-hails-response-to-injuries-31509266.html|title=Kilkenny boss hails response to injuries|date=8 September 2015|work=Irish Independent|access-date=9 September 2015}} [[Colin Fennelly]] revealed that a half-time speech from [[Jackie Tyrrell]] provided Kilkenny with the inspiration they needed in the second-half, saying "“Jackie Tyrrell at half-time, the speech he made was absolutely amazing, Jackie may have only one or two years left maybe and young lads hearing that coming on, it’s amazing. His speech at half-time was absolutely unbelievable, He spoke. Richie Power spoke and Michael Fennelly spoke and they’re probably the three senior lads of the team and whatever they said went through to us and we came out in the second-half and did the business."{{cite web|url= http://www.hoganstand.com/Kilkenny/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=243717|title=Tyrrell speech motivated us, says Fennelly|date=6 September 2015|work=Hogan Stand|access-date=8 September 2015}}{{cite web|url= http://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/jackie-tyrrell-inspirational-speech-from-the-heart-352599.html|title=Jackie Tyrrell: Inspirational speech ‘from the heart’|date=8 September 2015|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=9 September 2015}} Galway manager [[Anthony Cunningham]] speaking to ''[[RTÉ Sport]]'' after the game said "Unfortunately we came out second-best there in the second-half, having had a nice lead there at half-time, Congratulations to Kilkenny, they were the better team there in the second-half. We just had a few unforced errors there really; we only returned 1-4 in the second-half, But no fault to any of our players. They gave it some, some effort, it was some battle there. A few unforced errors there in the second-half, maybe a couple of decisions went against us at the start of the second-half. Kilkenny, with all their experience and their guile and their craft, a tremendous team, they punished us."{{cite web|url= http://www.the42.ie/anthony-cunningham-all-ireland-final-reaction-2315117-Sep2015/|title=Cunningham laments ‘unforced errors and a couple of decisions’ after second-half collapse|date=6 September 2015|work=The 42|access-date=8 September 2015}} [[Nicky English]] writing in the ''[[Irish Times]]'' was impressed by how Kilkenny performed in the second-half saying "Whatever Cody said at half- time worked because Kilkenny came out a different team. They’d reorganised themselves and they came back out and dictated the pace from the word go. They closed the gap straight away and got into the lead and were well on top in all areas. They closed down the space that Galway had been able to create in the full-forward line and Galway were reduced to scraps."{{cite web|url= http://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/galway-can-t-handle-intensity-of-kilkenny-pressure-cooker-1.2342369|title=Galway can’t handle intensity of Kilkenny pressure cooker|date=7 September 2015|work=Irish Times|access-date=9 September 2015}} [[Cyril Farrell]] writing in the ''[[Irish Independent]]'' called it a tough defeat for Galway to take especially after a great first half in which they took the game to Kilkenny saying "Unfortunately for Galway, Cody's team got the upper hand in those vital early stages of the second half and drove on to dominate the match. The problem was they were up against a team managed by the greatest hurling manager in the game's history and we knew that Kilkenny would come out with all guns blazing in the first ten to 15 minutes of the second half."{{cite web|url= http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/cyril-farrell-galway-wounded-by-defeat-but-can-build-on-positives-for-2016-31506542.html|title=Cyril Farrell: Galway wounded by defeat but can build on positives for 2016|date=7 September 2015|work=Irish Independent|access-date=9 September 2015}} Highlights of the final were shown on ''The Sunday Game'' programme which aired at 9:30pm that night on [[RTÉ Two]] and was presented by [[Des Cahill]] with analysis from [[Donal Óg Cusack]], [[Liam Sheedy]], and [[Ger Loughnane]]. On the man of the match award shortlist were [[Michael Fennelly (hurler)|Michael Fennelly]], [[T. J. Reid]] and [[David Burke (Galway hurler)|David Burke]], with [[Michael Fennelly (hurler)|Michael Fennelly]] winning the award which was presented by GAA president [[Aogán Ó Fearghail]] at the City West hotel in Dublin. ===Trophy presentation=== Kilkenny captain [[Joey Holden]] accepted the [[Liam MacCarthy Cup]] from GAA president [[Aogán Ó Fearghail]] in the Hogan Stand. ===Celebrations=== The Kilkenny team returned home on the 7 September were the homecoming event was held at [[Nowlan Park]] in Kikenny City at 5:45pm where up to 12,000 people attended.{{cite web|url= http://www.irishexaminer.com/ireland/kilkenny-homecoming-cody-sows-seeds-for-next-years-season-352592.html|title=Kilkenny homecoming: Cody sows seeds for next year’s season|date=8 September 2015|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=10 September 2015}} The team arrived at Kilkenny Castle before boarding an open-top bus for the journey to Nowlan Park.{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/31-counties-were-against-us-says-brian-cody-as-cats-celebrate-31509219.html|title='31 counties were against us' says Brian Cody as Cats celebrate|date=8 September 2015|work=Irish Independent|access-date=8 September 2015}} ==References== {{Reflist}} {{All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship}} {{GAA 2015}} {{Use dmy dates|date=June 2017}} [[Category:2015 in hurling|All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final]] [[Category:2010s in Dublin (city)|All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final, 2015]] [[Category:September 2015 sports events in Ireland]] [[Category:All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship finals]] [[Category:GAA finals at Croke Park]] [[Category:Kilkenny county hurling team matches]] [[Category:Galway county hurling team matches]]

{{convert|19|°C|°F}}{{Cite web |url=http://www.met.ie/climate/daily-data.asp |title=Met Eireann: Daily Data 04/09/16 |access-date=6 September 2016 |archive-date=16 September 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160916044808/http://www.met.ie/climate/daily-data.asp |url-status=dead }} | previous = [[2015 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2015]] | next = [[2017 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2017]] }} The '''2016 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final''' was the 129th event of its kind and the culmination of the [[2016 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]]. It was played at [[Croke Park]] in [[Dublin]] on 4 September 2016. This was the 18th All-Ireland season that ended with a Kilkenny–Tipperary final. Of the previous 17, Tipperary won 10 and Kilkenny 7. It was also the fifth final between Tipperary and Kilkenny since 2009, with Kilkenny leading the series 3–1.{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/kilkenny-tipperary-final-details-2927940-Aug2016/|title=Here's the details for the All-Ireland senior hurling final between Kilkenny and Tipperary|date=14 August 2016|work=The 42|access-date=15 August 2016}} Kilkenny were chasing three in a row with Tipperary looking for a first All-Ireland since 2010.{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2016/0814/809150-galway-v-tipperary/|title=Tipp edge Galway to set up Kilkenny showdown|date=14 August 2016|work=RTE Sport|access-date=17 August 2016}}{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2016/0813/809020-kilkenny-waterford/|title=Kilkenny deny Déise in thriller to book final spot|date=13 August 2016|work=RTE Sport|access-date=17 August 2016}} The final was shown live in Ireland on [[RTÉ One]] as part of ''[[The Sunday Game]]'' live programme, presented by [[Michael Lyster]] from Croke Park, with studio analysis from [[Liam Sheedy]], [[Henry Shefflin]] and [[Ger Loughnane]]. Match commentary was provided by [[Ger Canning]] with analysis by [[Michael Duignan (hurler)|Michael Duignan]]. The game was also shown live on [[Sky Sports]], presented by [[Rachel Wyse]] and [[Brian Carney (rugby)|Brian Carney]].{{cite web|url=http://www.irishmirror.ie/sport/gaa/what-time-kilkenny-v-tipperary-8742662|title=What time is Kilkenny v Tipperary? All you need to know about the All-Ireland hurling final|date=1 September 2016|work=Irish Mirror|access-date=2 September 2016}} Tipperary clinched their 27th All-Ireland title winning on a 2-29 to 2-20 scoreline.{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/vincent-hogan-tipps-master-at-peak-of-his-powers-35021053.html|title=Vincent Hogan: Tipp's master at peak of his powers|date=5 September 2016|work=Irish Independent|access-date=6 September 2016}} Their victory also marked the first time since the 1960s that Tipperary had won multiple All-Ireland titles in a single decade, having only won one title each in the 1970s, 1980s, 1990s and 2000s. ==Background== {{main article|Kilkenny–Tipperary hurling rivalry}} This was the seventh time in eight years that the counties have played each other in the championship, with Kilkenny winning 5 times. Kilkenny went into the final having won 36 All Ireland titles, 11 titles in the last 15 years (2000, 2002, 2003, 2006, 2007, 2008, 2009, 2011, 2012, 2014, and 2015), with Tipperary on 26 titles, 2 titles over the same period (2001 and 2010). The teams had played each other 26 times in the championship, the first time being in 1887, with Kilkenny winning 12 times and Tipperary winning on 13 occasions with one draw in 2014. Since the [[2010 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2010 All-Ireland Final]], Kilkenny have 10 wins and a draw in 13 league and championship games against Tipperary.{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/i-would-never-think-we-have-an-indian-sign-over-tipp-cody-35005681.html|title= I would never think we have an Indian sign over Tipp - Cody|date=30 August 2016|work=Irish Independent|access-date=30 August 2016}} Kilkenny had played in 65 All-Ireland finals, winning 36, losing 25 and drawing 4, with Tipperary having appeared in 40 All-Ireland finals, winning 26, losing 12 and drawing 2. The final was Kilkenny manager [[Brian Cody]]'s 84th championship match as manager since taking over at the start of [[1999 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1999]] season. Kilkenny had won 68, drawn six and lost nine of the previous matches, the defeats being against Galway in [[2001 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2001]], [[2005 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2005]] and [[2012 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2012]], Cork in [[1999 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1999]], [[2004 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2004]] and [[2013 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2013]], Wexford in [[2004 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2004]], Tipperary in [[2010 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2010]] and Dublin in [[2013 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2013]]. Tipperary were bidding to become the first Munster champions to win the All-Ireland title since Cork in [[2005 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2005]].{{cite web|url=http://tipperary.gaa.ie/ireland-senior-hurling-championship-final-kilkenny-v-tipperary-2/|title=All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final – Kilkenny v Tipperary|date=1 September 2016|work=Tipperary GAA|access-date=2 September 2016}} ==Route to the final== ===Kilkenny=== {{football box | date = 11 June 2016 | round = Leinster Semi-final | time = 19:00 | team1 = [[File:Colours of Dublin.svg|20px|border]] [[Dublin GAA|Dublin]] | score = 0-16 - 1-25 | report = [http://www.gaa.ie/hurling/news/leinster-shc-kilkenny-too-good-for-dublin/ Report] | team2 = [[File:Colours of Kilkenny.svg|20px|border]] [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] | goals1 = D Treacy (0-11, 0-10 frees); D O’Callaghan (0-2); É Dillon, D Plunkett, P Ryan (0-1). | goals2 = TJ Reid (0-10, 0-7 frees, 0-1 ’65); JJ Farrell (1-5); C Buckley, W Walsh, M Fennelly (0-2); P Walsh, C Fogarty, L Ryan, C Fennelly (0-1). | referee = B Gavin (Offaly) | attendance = 10,419 | stadium = [[O'Moore Park]], [[Portlaoise]] | stack = no }} {{football box|date = 3 July 2016|team1 = [[File:Colours of Kilkenny.svg|20px|border]] [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]]|team2 = [[File:Colours of Galway.svg|20px|border]] [[Galway GAA|Galway]]|time = 16:00|round = Leinster Final|score =1-26 - 0-22|goals1 = TJ Reid 0-10 (0-7f, 1 65), J Farrell 1-4, R Hogan 0-5, C Fogarty 0-3, W Walsh 0-2, J Power 0-1, M Fennelly 0-1.|report =[http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/galway-challenge-peters-out-as-kilkenny-claim-71st-leinster-crown-in-familiar-style-34853403.html Report]|goals2 =J Canning 0-6 (0-6f), C Mannion 0-5, C Cooney 0-3, C Whelan 0-3, J Cooney 0-2, D Glennon 0-1, C Donnellan 0-1, A Smith 0-1. |stadium = [[Croke Park]], [[Dublin]]|attendance =29,377|referee =F. Schools and third level colleges will get 2,500 tickets, while season ticket holders will be entitled to 5,500 tickets. 1,000 tickets will be given to overseas clubs. The [[Camogie Association|Camogie]], [[Ladies' Gaelic Football Association|Ladies' Football]], Handball and Rounders Associations are each allocated about 200 tickets, as are the jubilee teams and mini-7s which play at half-time. The match was a sell-out. ===Related events=== The [[2016 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|2016 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Final]] was played between Tipperary and [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] as a curtain-raiser to the senior final.{{cite web|url=http://tipperary.gaa.ie/electric-ireland-ireland-minor-hurling-championship-final-limerick-v-tipperary/|title=Electric Ireland All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship Final – Limerick v Tipperary|date=1 September 2016|work=Tipperary GAA|access-date=2 September 2016}} Tipperary went on to win the final on a 1–21 to 0-17 scoreline.{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2016/0904/814079-tipperary-limerick-mhc-final/|title=Tipperary see off Limerick to claim minor title|date=4 September 2016|work=RTE Sport|access-date=6 September 2016}} The Tipperary minor team were captained by Brian McGrath, brother of Noel and John McGrath who went to win the senior final with Tipperary.{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/three-allireland-medals-in-one-day-photo-captures-heartwarming-moment-the-mcgraths-came-together-at-croker-35022610.html|title=Three All-Ireland medals in one day! Photo captures heartwarming moment the McGraths came together at Croker|date=4 September 2016|work=Irish Independent|access-date=6 September 2016}} ==Match summary== ===Officials=== On 22 August 2016 the officials were chosen for the final by the [[Gaelic Athletic Association|GAA]], with [[Brian Gavin (referee)|Brian Gavin]] being named as the referee.{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/brian-gavin-kilkenny-tipperary-2942366-Aug2016/|title= A familiar face will referee the All-Ireland hurling final between Kilkenny and Tipperary|date=23 August 2016|work=The 42|access-date=23 August 2016}} [[Barry Kelly (referee)|Barry Kelly]] was the standby referee with Colm Lyons of Cork the other linesman and John Keane of Galway the sideline official. The umpires were Michael Gavin, David Gavin, William Flynn, all from Clara and PJ Lawlor from Ferbane/Belmont. The match was his fourth All-Ireland final having been the referee in [[2011 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2011]], [[2013 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2013]], and the replay in [[2014 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2014]].{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2016/0822/811112-offalyman-brian-gavin-to-ref-all-ireland-shc-final/|title= Offalyman Brian Gavin to ref All-Ireland SHC final|date=23 August 2016|work=RTE Sport|access-date=23 August 2016}} ===Team news=== It was confirmed on 15 August that Kilkenny's [[Michael Fennelly (hurler)|Michael Fennelly]] would miss the final after he ruptured his achilles tendon in the semi-final replay victory over Waterford.{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/huge-blow-for-brian-cody-as-kilkenny-confirm-that-michael-fennelly-has-achilles-injury-34968445.html|title=Huge blow for Brian Cody as Kilkenny confirm that Michael Fennelly has achilles injury|date=15 August 2016|work=Irish Independent|access-date=17 August 2016}} Kilkenny named their starting fifteen on Friday 2 September and it showed two changes to the one which defeated Waterford in the semi-final replay with [[Kevin Kelly (hurler)|Kevin Kelly]] included at corner-forward. The other change saw [[Kieran Joyce (hurler)|Kieran Joyce]] replacing Michael Fennelly.{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/kilkenny-all-ireland-final-team-2962310-Sep2016/|title=Cody springs selection surprise for All-Ireland final as 22-year-old Kevin Kelly included|date=2 September 2016|work=The 42|access-date=6 September 2016}} Michael Ryan made one change to the Tipperary team for the final with John O’Dwyer coming in at top of the right instead of Nial O Meara with John McGrath moving to top of the left. There were five All-Ireland Final debutants in Tipperary's starting line-up.{{cite web|url=http://www.nationalist.ie/news/home/214904/bubbles-to-start-as-tipperary-make-one-change-for-final.html|title=Bubbles' to start as Tipperary make one change for final|date=3 September 2016|work=The Nationalist|access-date=6 September 2016}} ===Summary=== Seamus Callanan opened the scoring after two minutes with a point from out on the left which he hit over his left shoulder. Kevin Kelly equalized for Kilkenny in the fifth minute before TJ Reid scored from a free to put Kilkenny into a one-point lead.{{cite web|url= http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2016/0904/814073-live-build-up-all-ireland-shc-final/|title=As it happened: Tipperary claim Liam MacCarthy glory|date=5 September 2016|work=RTE Sport|access-date=6 September 2016}} After ten minutes, [[Séamus Kennedy (hurler)|Séamus Kennedy]] scored his first ever championship point to make it four points all, after fifteen minutes it was six all. John O’Dwyer scored a point after twenty five minutes to level the scores at nine all. The half-time score was Tipperary 0-14 Kilkenny 0–12 with every single Tipperary forward scoring from play. The sides were level 10 times in the first half.{{cite web|url=http://www.irishmirror.ie/sport/gaa/tipperary-crowned-ireland-champions-after-8766942 |title=Tipperary crowned All Ireland Champions after super nine point victory over Kilkenny|date=5 September 2016|work=Irish Mirror|access-date=6 September 2016}}{{cite web|url= http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-football/majestic-tipperary-are-all-ireland-champions-after-victory-over-kilkenny-in-croke-park-35020342.html|title=Majestic Tipperary are All Ireland champions after victory over Kilkenny in Croke Park|date=6 September 2016|work=Irish Independent|access-date=6 September 2016}} Seamus Callinan had five points in the first half and scored the first point of the second half from a free to open the lead to three points. After forty-one minutes, Kevin Kelly scored a goal for Kilkenny when he scoped and flicked the ball into the empty net in front of the hill 16 end.{{cite web|url= http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2016/0904/814136-10-minutes-that-mattered/|title=10 minutes that mattered, from a final to remember|date=6 September 2016|work=RTE Sport|access-date=6 September 2016}} Seamus Callinan got the next score from a free to put one point between them. Jason Forde who had come on as a substitute a minute earlier for Michael Breen scored a point to level the game in the forty fifth minute.{{cite web|url= http://www.hoganstand.com/Hurling/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=260420|title=SHC Final: Super Tipp claim 27th title|date=6 September 2016|work=Hogan Stand|access-date=6 September 2016}} Two minutes later John O’Dwyer picked up the ball and cut in from the left and hit a low shot from distance that flew into the back of the net to put Tipperary into a four-point lead.{{cite web|url= http://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/all-ireland-final-tipping-point-reached-as-kilkenny-succumb-1.2779483|title=All-Ireland final: Tipping point reached as Kilkenny succumb|date=6 September 2016|work=Irish Times|access-date=6 September 2016}}{{cite web|url= http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/colm-keys-10-small-battles-that-tilted-the-croker-war-in-tipps-direction-35024610.html|title=Colm Keys: 10 small battles that tilted the Croker war in Tipp's direction|date=5 September 2016|work=Irish Independent|access-date=6 September 2016}} Pauric Maher scored a point from out on the left touchline in the fifty-first minute to increase the lead to five.{{cite web|url= http://www.the42.ie/tipperary-kilkenny-talking-points-3-2963994-Sep2016/|title=5 talking points as breathtaking Tipperary take down Cody's empire|date=4 September 2016|work=The 42|access-date=6 September 2016}} Tipperary were six ahead in the fifty-sixth minute after another Seamus Callinan point.{{cite web|url= http://www.nationalist.ie/news/home/214942/magnificent-tipperary-dethrone-kilkenny-to-win-all-ireland-final-in-superb-style.html|title=Magnificent Tipperary dethrone Kilkenny to win All-Ireland final in superb style|date=5 September 2016|work=Nationalist|access-date=6 September 2016}} With ten minutes left John McGrath scored a second goal for Tipperary when he cut in from the right and hit a high shot to the left after a pass from Noel McGrath, this put Tipperary nine points clear. Two minutes later Richie Hogan scored with a ground shot to the net to reduce the lead to six. Tipperary then scored a further four points to go into stoppage time with a nine-point lead which they held to the end to claim the title.{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/kilkenny-tipperary-live-3-2963653-Sep2016/ |title=As it happened: 2016 All Ireland Final|date=4 September 2016|work=The 42|access-date=6 September 2016}}{{cite web|url= http://www.the42.ie/kilkenny-tipperary-all-ireland-hurling-final-2964224-Sep2016/|title=John Gardiner: Relentless Tipp left Kilkenny searching for answers they simply didn't have|date=4 September 2016|work=The 42|access-date=6 September 2016}} ==Match details== {{football box |date = 4 September 2016 |time = 15:30 |team1 = [[File:Colours of Kilkenny.svg|20px|border]] [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] | score = 2-20 - The Tipperary team then did a victory lap around Croke Park with the trophy. ===Reaction=== Tipperary manager [[Michael Ryan (hurler, born 1970)|Michel Ryan]] speaking after the match said "This is a fantastic day for Tipperary hurling. I think we might have awoken other giants that may have been sleeping though, in that every other county is going to take huge encouragement from what we’ve achieved this year, because we’re all in the pot; every one of us hurling counties are chasing Kilkenny and those are the facts. And for one of us to come through and break that mould for once... don’t get me wrong, that’s not a foregone conclusion that that will ever happen again, such is the quality of Kilkenny, but I think we’re after sending home a lot of teams that I think will set 2017 alight.”{{cite web|url= http://www.the42.ie/michael-ryan-reaction-2964024-Sep2016/|title=Tipp win 'might have awoken sleeping giants' says Ryan|date=4 September 2016|work=The 42|access-date=6 September 2016}}{{cite web|url= http://www.the42.ie/michael-ryan-tipperary-3-2964133-Sep2016/|title='He remains a great friend to our group' - Ryan tribute to ex Tipp manager O'Shea|date=4 September 2016|work=The 42|access-date=6 September 2016}} [[File:Seamus Kennedy shirt from 2016 All-Ireland SHC final.jpg|thumb|170px|Shirt worn by [[Séamus Kennedy (hurler)|Séamus Kennedy]] in the 2016 All-Ireland final ([[Tipperary Museum of Hidden History]])]] Kilkenny manager [[Brian Cody]] speaking after the match said "The better team won, the better team always wins as far as I’m concerned but it was comprehensive, We went in after the first half two points down, well in the game. We got a good start to the second half, got the goal but you know they didn’t blink, they came back at us and they got some terrific scores, We were out-played through the second half and there’s no argument that the better team won the match."{{cite web|url= http://www.the42.ie/brian-cody-reaction-3-2964066-Sep2016/|title='They didn't blink' - no excuses from Brian Cody as three-in-a-row bid ends|date=4 September 2016|work=The 42|access-date=6 September 2016}}{{cite web|url= http://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/no-complaints-no-excuses-no-if-onlys-from-brian-cody-419380.html|title=No complaints, no excuses, no ‘if onlys’ from Brian Cody|date=4 September 2016|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=6 September 2016}} [[Noel McGrath (hurler)|Noel McGrath]] said it was the stuff of dreams to come back from cancer and win the All-Ireland title saying "Fifteen months ago I never thought I'd be playing in Croke Park, let alone going up the steps at Croke Park, or watching Brendan (Maher) lift up the cup. It was tough for me for a few months in 2015, but look I'm just delighted to be back playing and delighted to be on the pitch and doing what I can for Tipperary and I'm just absolutely thrilled to be part of an All-Ireland-winning team. I was just delighted to be able to get back playing to whatever level I could get back to - I wasn't sure what that would be."{{cite web|url= http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/beating-cancer-to-win-the-allireland-the-stuff-of-dreams-for-noel-mcgrath-35024762.html|title=Beating cancer to win the All-Ireland the 'stuff of dreams' for Noel McGrath|date=5 September 2016|work=Irish Independent|access-date=6 September 2016}} Former Tipperary hurler and manager [[Nicky English]] writing in the ''[[Irish Times]]'' taught that Tipperary out-Kilkennyed Kilkenny this time to emerge as very deserving and worthy winners of this All-Ireland final saying "This was a huge win for Tipperary – there’s no other way to put it. Huge! Tipperary’s strength in the first tackle, their aerial ability throughout, their skill in the forwards and their intensity was reminiscent of Kilkenny at their level best, which should be taken as a serious compliment. From Mick Ryan and his management team’s perspective, they couldn’t have asked for any more from the players. In terms of power, aggression, skill and intelligent hurling, Tipperary were fantastic."{{cite web|url= http://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/nicky-english-tipp-beat-kilkenny-by-playing-like-kilkenny-1.2779322|title=Nicky English: Tipp beat Kilkenny by playing like Kilkenny|date=5 September 2016|work=Irish Times|access-date=6 September 2016}} Highlights of the final were shown on ''The Sunday Game'' programme which aired at 9:30pm that night on [[RTÉ Two]] and was presented by [[Des Cahill]] with match analysis from [[Brendan Cummins (GAA player)|Brendan Cummins]], [[Eddie Brennan]], and [[Cyril Farrell]]. On the man of the match award shortlist were John O'Dwyer, Ronan Maher, and Seamus Callanan, with Seamus Callanan winning the award which was presented by GAA president [[Aogán Ó Fearghail]] at the [[Burlington Hotel (Dublin)|Double tree by Hilton hotel]] in Dublin where the post match Tipperary function was being held. Tipperary manager [[Michael Ryan (hurler, born 1970)|Michael Ryan]] opened the envelope that contained the winning players name.{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/seamus-callanan-man-of-the-match-2-2964243-Sep2016/|title=Seamus Callanan named All-Ireland final man of the match - and who'd argue?|date=5 September 2016|work=The 42|access-date=6 September 2016}} ===Celebrations=== The Tipperary team returned home on the 5 September were the homecoming event was held at [[Semple Stadium]] in [[Thurles]]. The gates of the Stadium were opened at 4.00pm with the Tipperary senior team were introduced to the crowd at 8.00pm, preceded by the minor squad, who helped the county to their first minor-senior double since 1949.{{cite web|url=http://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/massive-turnout-for-tipperary-hurling-champs-homecoming-1.2780637|title=Massive turnout for Tipperary hurling champs’ homecoming|date=5 September 2016|work=Irish Times|access-date=6 September 2016}}{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2016/0905/814415-tipperary/|title=Tipperary fans throng Thurles for homecoming|date=5 September 2016|work=RTE Sport|access-date=6 September 2016}}{{cite web|url=http://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/michael-ryan-keeping-tipperarys-great-expectations-in-check-419551.html|title=Michael Ryan keeping Tipperary’s great expectations in check|date=6 September 2016|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=6 September 2016}} ==Miscellaneous== * Sides were level 11 times (equalling the all-time record from 2009 and the 2014 drawn match). * Kilkenny were in the lead on seven occasions, equal to Tipperary's record in 2009. ==References== {{Reflist}} {{All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship}} {{GAA 2016}} {{Use dmy dates|date=June 2017}} [[Category:2016 in hurling|All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final]] [[Category:2010s in Dublin (city)|All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final, 2016]] [[Category:September 2016 sports events in Ireland]] [[Category:All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship finals]] [[Category:GAA finals at Croke Park]] [[Category:Kilkenny county hurling team matches]] [[Category:Tipperary county hurling team matches]]

[[Dublin]] on 3 September 2017{{cite web|url=http://www.gaa.ie/mm/Document/GaaIe/GAANews/13/47/27/FinalVersion-GAAMasterFixtureScheduleBooklet2017-15112016_Neutral.pdf|title=GAA MASTER FIXTURES between [[Galway county hurling team|Galway]] and [[Waterford county hurling team|Waterford]], the culmination of the [[2017 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]]. It was the [[List of All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship finals|130th final]] of that sport's primary competition, the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]]. Galway won their fifth All-Ireland All-Ireland SHC title, winning by three points, it was their first title since [[1988 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|1988]].{{cite web|url= http://www.the42.ie/galway-all-ireland-hurling-champions-waterford-3579472-Sep2017/|title=Galway end 29 years of hurt as they lift All-Ireland crown with win over Waterford|date=3 September 2017|work=The 42|access-date=5 September 2017}}{{cite web|url= http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/five-things-we-learned-from-galways-all-ireland-win-over-waterford-36095769.html|title=Five things we learned from Galway's All ireland win over Waterford|date=3 September 2017|work=Irish Independent|access-date=5 September 2017}}{{cite web|url= http://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/emotions-run-high-as-tribe-end-agonising-29-year-wait-458279.html|title=Emotions run high as Tribe end agonising 29-year wait|date=4 September 2017|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=5 September 2017}}{{cite web|url= http://www.the42.ie/tommy-dunne-all-ireland-hurling-final-analysis-galway-waterford-2017-3580343-Sep2017/|title=Analysis: Galway deserving All-Ireland winners as Waterford system buckles under intense heat|date=3 September 2017|work=The 42|access-date=5 September 2017}} The final was shown live in Ireland on [[RTÉ2]] as part of ''[[The Sunday Game]]'' live programme, presented by [[Michael Lyster]] from Croke Park, with studio analysis from [[Liam Sheedy]], [[Henry Shefflin]] and [[Ger Loughnane]]. Match commentary was provided by [[Marty Morrissey]] with analysis by [[Michael Duignan (hurler)|Michael Duignan]]. The game was also shown live on [[Sky Sports]], presented by [[Rachel Wyse]] and [[Brian Carney (rugby)|Brian Carney]].{{cite web|url= https://www.balls.ie/gaa/ger-canning-hurling-finals-commentary-372693|title=An Amazing Broadcasting Streak Will End During The All-Ireland Hurling Final|date=1 September 2017|work=Ball.ie|access-date=5 September 2017}} The match drew a peak audience of 1.1 million which made it the most watched RTÉ broadcast of 2017 up to then before being overtaken by the [[2017 All-Ireland Senior Football Championship final|football final]], it had an average audience of 901,500.{{cite web|url= https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2017/0904/902225-huge-numbers-tune-in-to-watch-galway-triumph/|title=Record numbers tune in to watch Galway triumph in hurling final|date=4 September 2017|work=RTE Sport|access-date=5 September 2017}} ==Background== The match-up was unusual for several reasons: *The first meeting of [[Galway GAA|Galway]] and [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] in the [[All-Ireland Hurling Final]].{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/columnists/vincent-hogan/vincent-hogan-rampant-dise-explode-myth-that-use-of-sweeper-is-ultradefensive-36028655.html|title=Vincent Hogan: Rampant Déise explode myth that use of sweeper is ultra-defensive|date=14 August 2017|work=Irish Independent|access-date=14 August 2017}}{{cite web|url= http://www.the42.ie/tommy-dunne-galway-waterford-all-ireland-final-preview-3573207-Aug2017/|title= Analysis: Waterford's 'Brick' Wall, Galway's physical edge, style wars - All-Ireland final preview|date=31 August 2017|work=The 42|access-date=31 August 2017}} *The first final since [[1996 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1996]] not to involve one of the [[Big Three (hurling)|"Big Three" counties]] ([[Cork GAA|Cork]], [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] and [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]]).{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/galway-waterford-all-ireland-3544342-Aug2017/|title= History Makers! First ever Galway Waterford All-Ireland senior hurling final in store|date=13 August 2017|work=The 42|access-date=14 August 2017}} *Galway had not won the All-Ireland since [[1988 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1988]] (29 years) and had lost six finals in the interim, [[1990 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1990]], [[1993 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1993]], [[2001 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2001]], [[2005 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2005]], [[2012 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2012]], and [[2015 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2015]].{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/gaelic-games/40917401|title=All-Ireland Hurling semi-final: Waterford hurlers set up decider with Galway|date=14 August 2017|work=BBC Sport|access-date=14 August 2017}} *Waterford had not won the All-Ireland since [[1959 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1959]] (58 years) and had only appeared in two finals in the interim ([[1963 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1963]] and [[2008 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2008]]).{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/cyril-farrell-triedandtrusted-waterford-gameplan-will-rattle-galway-36028648.html|title=Cyril Farrell: Tried-and-trusted Waterford game-plan will rattle Galway|date=14 August 2017|work=Irish Independent|access-date=14 August 2017}} The match was the 11th championship meeting between Galway and Waterford, the first in 1938 with the most recent in [[2011 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2011]]. Galway had never beaten Waterford in the championship.{{cite web|url= http://www.the42.ie/waterford-unbeaten-record-galway-hurling-3545070-Aug2017/|title= Waterford aiming to protect incredible record against Galway when they meet in All-Ireland final|date=14 August 2017|work=The 42|access-date=14 August 2017}} Galway were looking to win their fifth [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland title]] after winning in [[1923 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1923]], [[1980 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1980]], [[1987 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1987]], and [[1988 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1988]]. Waterford were looking for a third title after winning in [[1948 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1948]] and [[1959 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1959]].{{cite web|url= http://munster.gaa.ie/2017/07/21/all-ireland-senior-hurling-championship-final-6/|title=2017 All Ireland Senior Final|date=1 September 2016|work=Munster GAA|access-date=1 September 2017}} ==Paths to A Cadogan, C Lehane 0-2; S Kingston, D Fitzgibbon (sideline), S Harnedy, L O’Farrell 0-1 | penaltyscore = | penalties1 = | penalties2 = | stadium = [[Croke Park]], [[Dublin]] | attendance = 72,022 | referee = J Owens (Wexford) | aet = }} ==Pre-match== ===Jubilee team=== The [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] team that won the [[1992 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1992 All-Ireland Final]] were presented to the crowd before the match to mark 25 years. ===Ticketing=== With a stadium capacity of 82,300, the 32 individual [[Gaelic Athletic Association county|county boards]] received 60,000 tickets. Schools and third level colleges got 2,500 tickets, while season ticket holders were entitled to 5,500 tickets. 1,000 tickets were given to overseas clubs. The [[Camogie Association|Camogie]], [[Ladies' Gaelic Football Association|Ladies' Football]], Handball and Rounders Associations were each allocated about 200 tickets, as were the jubilee teams and mini-7s which play at half-time. Demand for tickets was very high in both counties with Galway and Waterford having receiving around 32,000 tickets between. Stand tickets were priced at [[€]]80 with terrace at €40.{{cite web|url= http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/ticket-frenzy-for-hurling-final-36086450.html|title= Ticket frenzy for hurling final|date=31 August 2017|work=Irish Independent|access-date=31 August 2017}} ===Related events=== The [[2017 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|2017 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Final]] was played between Galway and [[Cork GAA|Cork]] as a curtain-raiser to the senior final, with Galway winning by 2-17 to 2-15.{{cite web|url= http://www.the42.ie/galway-minor-hurling-cork-jack-canning-3579315-Sep2017/|title=Canning man-of-the-match as Galway lift All-Ireland minor title with win over Cork|date=3 September 2017|work=The 42|access-date=5 September 2017}} ==Match summary== ===Officials=== On 17 August 2017 the officials were chosen for the final by the [[Gaelic Athletic Association|GAA]], with Tipperary's [[Fergal Horgan]] being named as the referee in what will be his first senior final.{{cite web|url= http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/tipperarys-fergal-horgan-to-referee-allireland-senior-hurling-final-36042373.html|title=Tipperary's Fergal Horgan to referee All-Ireland senior hurling final|date=17 August 2017|work=Irish Independent|access-date=22 August 2017}} Cork’s Colm Lyons was named as linesman and standby referee with Paud O’Dwyer of Carlow on the other line. The sideline official were Johnny Murphy from Limerick. The umpires were John Ryan, Paul Ryan, Mick Butler, and Sean Bradshaw.{{cite web|url= http://www.the42.ie/fergal-horgan-all-ireland-final-referee-3551022-Aug2017/|title=Tipperary native Fergal Horgan appointed as All-Ireland hurling final referee|date=17 August 2017|work=The 42|access-date=22 August 2017}} ===Team news=== During Galway's win in the semi-final, [[Adrian Tuohy]] was involved in an incident where the helmet of Tipperary player [[Patrick Maher (hurler)|Bonner Maher]] was pulled off. It was confirmed a few days later that he would face no sanction arising from the incident and would be free to play in the final.{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/allireland-shc-semifinal-cannings-class-the-tiebreaker-in-epic-showdown-36005770.html|title= All-Ireland SHC Semi-Final: Canning's class the tie-breaker in epic showdown|date=7 August 2017|work=Irish Independent|access-date=9 August 2017}}{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/galways-adrian-tuohy-gets-green-light-for-all-ireland-final-as-he-is-cleared-on-bonner-helmet-incident-36017779.html|title= Galway's Adrian Tuohy gets green light for All Ireland final as he is cleared on Bonner helmet incident|date=10 August 2017|work=Irish Independent|access-date=10 August 2017}} During the semi-final win against [[Cork GAA|Cork]], Waterford's [[Austin Gleeson]] in a similar incident to Adrian Tuohy's pulled [[Luke Meade]]’s helmet off his head in the first half. It was confirmed on 15 August that he would also escape punishment from the CCCC for the incident and would be free to play in the final.{{cite web|url= http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/why-austin-gleeson-case-shows-the-need-to-follow-rugby-example-36036924.html|title= Why Austin Gleeson case shows the need to follow rugby example|date=16 August 2017|work=Irish Independent|access-date=16 August 2017}}{{cite web|url= http://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/waterford-rejoice-as-austin-gleeson-gets-final-all-clear-457144.html|title= Waterford rejoice as Austin Gleeson gets final all-clear|date=16 August hurler)|Conor Gleeson]] would miss the final after being handed a one-match ban after receiving a straight red card in the semi-final win against Cork.{{cite web|url= uses but big-day players make difference|date=26 August 2017|work=Irish Independent|access-date=28 August 2017}} [[Jonathan Glynn]] was named in the starting line-up for Galway for the first time in two years, replacing [[Niall Burke]] in the half-forward line. [[Tadhg de Búrca]] returned to the Waterford line-up after being suspended for the semi-final, replacing the banned Conor Gleeson.{{cite web|url= http://www.the42.ie/galway-hurling-waterford-johnny-glynn-3577717-Sep2017/|title=Glynn to start for Galway for first time in two years as Waterford bring back de Búrca|date=2 September 2017|work=The 42|access-date=5 September 2017}} ===Summary=== Galway thundered into Waterford from the beginning, giving na Déise very little room to breathe. Playing into the Davin end, [[Joe Canning]] opened the scoring for Galway after 18 seconds with a point from out on the left which he hit over his left shoulder. Further points from Johnny Coen, Joseph Cooney, and Cathal Mannion gave Galway a four points to no score lead after four minutes. In the fifth minute, Kevin Moran scored Waterford's first score, a goal when he ran in on goal after collecting a pass from Michael Walsh to finish low to the left of the net. Kevin Moran got a point in the 11th minute to make the score 0-6 to 1-2. David Burke got his second point in the 21st minute to make it 0-10 to 1-4. In the 22nd minute, a high ball in from Kieran Bennett went all the way into the net after a mistake by Galway goalkeeper [[Colm Callanan]] when he tried to catch the ball after it bounced, this made the score 0-10 to 2-4. Galway had a one-point lead at half-time on a 0-14 to 2-7 scoreline.{{cite web|url= http://www.the42.ie/galway-waterford-live-3579427-Sep2017/|title=2017 All Ireland Final: as it happened|date=3 September 2017|work=The 42|access-date=5 September 2017}} In the second-half [[Pauric Mahony]] got the first point from a free to level the match after three minutes. Waterford had a one-point lead in the 43rd minute after another free from Mahony. Joe Canning leveled the match a minute later from a free. After fifty minutes, Galway had a two point lead on a 0-20 to 2-12 scoreline, and with ten minutes to play the Galway lead was one point. With five minutes to go, the lead was four for Galway after a point from Jason Flynn. Canning got Galway's last point in the last minute from another free to make it 0-26 to 2-16, with the final score of the match coming from another Mahony free in the first minute of the four minutes which were added on. Despite attempts by Waterford to score a goal and level the match, Galway held on to win by three points, 0-26 to 2-17.{{cite web|url= http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/galway-026-waterford-217-as-it-happened-tribesmen-are-the-champions-for-the-first-time-since-1988-36095318.html|title=Galway 0-26 Waterford 2-17 as it happened: Tribesmen are the champions for the first time since 1988|date=3 September 2017|work=Irish Independent|access-date=6 September 2017}} ==Match details== {{football box | round = Final | date = 3 September 2017 | time = 15:30 | team1 = [[Galway GAA|Galway]] [[File:Colours of Galway.svg|20px|border]] | score = 0-26 – 2-17 | report =[https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2017/0903/901916-galway-v-waterford/ Report] | team2 = [[File:Colours of Waterford.svg|border|20px]] [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] | goals1 = J Canning 0-9 (6f, 1 sideline); During his speech Burke paid tribute to the late [[Tony Keady]] and [[Niall Donoghue]].{{cite web|url= http://www.the42.ie/galway-captain-remembers-absent-heroes-in-passionate-acceptance-speech-3579651-Sep2017/|title=Galway captain remembers absent heroes in passionate acceptance speech|date=3 September 2017|work=The 42|access-date=5 September 2017}} The Galway team then did a victory lap around Croke Park with the trophy.{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2017/0903/902042-david-burke-never-stopped-believing/|title= David Burke never stopped believing|date=4 September 2017|work=RTE Sport|access-date=5 September 2017}}{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/galway-hurling-david-burke-all-ireland-3607803-Sep2017/|title=Pen to paper for Galway's All-Ireland winning hurling speech with the help of his mother|date=20 September 2017|work=The 42|access-date=21 September 2017}} ===Reaction=== Highlights of the final were shown on ''The Sunday Game'' programme which aired at 9:30pm that night on [[RTÉ2]] and was presented by [[Des Cahill]] with match analysis from [[Brendan Cummins (GAA player)|Brendan Cummins]], [[Eddie Brennan]], and [[Anthony Daly (hurler)|Anthony Daly]]. On the man of the match award shortlist were [[David Burke (Galway hurler)|David Burke]], [[Gearóid McInerney]] and [[Jamie Barron]], with David Burke winning the award which was presented by GAA president [[Aogán Ó Fearghail]] at the City West hotel in Dublin where the post match Galway function was being held.{{cite web|url= http://www.hoganstand.com/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=275317|title=TV viewers knew man of the match winner before it was revealed|date=4 September 2017|work=Hogan Stand|access-date=6 September 2017}} ===Celebrations=== The Galway teams returned home on the 4 September were the homecoming event was held at [[Pearse Stadium]], with the team arriving around 7:30pm, a crowd of around 20,000 turned put to greet the team.
