The '''2018 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final''' was a [[hurling]] match played at [[Croke Park]] in [[Dublin]] on 19 August 2018<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2017/1001/908864-gaa-season-2018/ |title=How the GAA season might look in 2018 following Special Congress vote|date=2 October 2017|work=RTE Sport|access-date=20 October 2017}}</ref> between [[Galway county hurling team|Galway]] and [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick]], the culmination of the [[2018 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]]. It was the [[List of All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship finals|131st final]] of that sport's primary competition, the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]].

Limerick won the match, ending a 45-year wait for a title.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/how-the-game-was-won-37231542.html |title =How the game was won|date=20 August 2018|work=Irish Independent|access-date=21 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/there-were-more-shots-than-hooks-blocks-and-tackles-five-talking-points-from-limericks-dramatic-allireland-triumph-37230764.html|title =There were more shots than hooks, blocks and tackles - Five talking points from Limerick's dramatic All-Ireland triumph|date=20 August 2018|work=Irish Independent|access-date=21 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/martin-breheny-allireland-final-match-report-limericks-new-wave-swamp-sloppy-tribe-37231548.html |title =Martin Breheny All-Ireland final match report: Limerick's new wave swamp sloppy Tribe|date=20 August 2018|work=Irish Independent|access-date=21 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/gaa/limerick-win-first-all-ireland-hurling-title-in-45-years-863141.html |title =Limerick win first All Ireland hurling title in 45 years|date=20 August 2018|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=21 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2018/0819/986137-is-limericks-road-to-glory-the-most-impressive-ever/ |title =Is Limerick's road to All-Ireland glory the most impressive ever?|date=20 August 2018|work=RTE News|access-date=21 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/gaa/limericks-dreams-becomes-one-of-the-gaas-greatest-sporting-moments-863795.html|title =Limerick's 'Dreams' becomes one of the GAA's greatest sporting moments|date=22 August 2018|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=22 August 2018}}</ref>	

The final was shown live in Ireland on [[RTÉ2]] as part of ''[[The Sunday Game]]'' live programme, presented by [[Michael Lyster]] from Croke Park, with studio analysis from [[Liam Sheedy]], [[Henry Shefflin]] and [[Ger Loughnane]]. Match commentary was provided by [[Marty Morrissey]] with analysis by [[Michael Duignan (hurler)|Michael Duignan]]. The game was also shown live on [[Sky Sports]], presented by [[Rachel Wyse]] and [[Brian Carney (rugby)|Brian Carney]].
		
The match drew a peak audience of more than 1 million on RTÉ. The TV audience for ''The Sunday Game'' coverage peaked at 1,007,500 by the end of the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/330764/1-000-000-tv-viewers-for-limerick-s-all-ireland-final-win.html |title =More than a million TV viewers for Limericks All Ireland Win|date=20 August 2018|work=Limerick Leader|access-date=21 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2018/0820/986301-huge-numbers-tune-in-to-watch-limerick-end-45-year-wait/ |title =Huge numbers tune in to watch Limerick end 45-year wait for Liam MacCarthy success|date=20 August 2018|work=RTE News|access-date=21 August 2018}}</ref>

==Background==
Galway were the defending champions and were looking to win their sixth [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland title]] after winning in [[1923 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1923]], [[1980 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1980]], [[1987 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1987]], [[1988 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1988]], and [[2017 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2017]].
Limerick were appearing in their first final since [[2007 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2007]] and were looking for an eighth title after winning in [[1897 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1897]], [[1918 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1918]], [[1921 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1921]], [[1934 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1934]], [[1936 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1936]], [[1940 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1940]], and [[1973 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1973]].
The two counties had played each other in the final twice prior to this: in [[1923 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1923]] and [[1980 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1980]] with Galway winning both.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/gaa/sean-silke-4am-wake-up-gearbag-missing-and-happy-limerick-fans-at-the-door-862259.html |title = Sean Silke: 4am wake-up, gearbag missing, and happy Limerick fans at the door|date=15 August 2018|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=15 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/2018-hurling-final/galway-probable-line-up-for-the-all-ireland-hurling-final-1.3594891 |title =Galway: probable line-up for the All-Ireland hurling final|date=15 August 2018|work=Irish Times|access-date=16 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2018/0815/985359-from-1973-to-now-limericks-long-wait-for-glory/ |title =From 1973 to now: Limerick's long wait for glory|date=18 August 2018|work=RTE Sport|access-date=21 August 2018}}</ref>

==Pre-match==
===Build-up===
The final was shown on a giant screen at the [[Gaelic Grounds]] in Limerick where an all ticket crowd of 20,000 watched the match. A big screen was also in place in [[Eyre Square]] in Galway for the match.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/gaelic-grounds-limerick-bog-screen-hurling-final-galway-4171195-Aug2018/ |title =Gaelic Grounds to show Limerick-Galway All-Ireland hurling final on giant screen|date=9 August 2018|work=The 42|access-date=9 August 2018}}</ref>

===Hurling stars of the 1990s===
The [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] team that won the [[1992 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1992 All-Ireland Final]] were honoured in [[2017 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2017]] and as Kilkenny also won the [[1993 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1993 All-Ireland Final]] the GAA decided instead to honour the star hurlers of the 1990s. A group of senior GAA correspondents under the chairmanship of GAA President [[John Horan (GAA President)|John Horan]] selected the team. The team was presented to the crowd after the completion of the minor final.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/gaa-hurling-stars-1990s-4182781-Aug2018/ |title =8 counties included as GAA to honour hurling stars of the 90s on All-Ireland final day|date=15 August 2018|work=The 42|access-date=16 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/gaa-to-honour-hurling-team-of-the-1990s-at-allireland-final-and-some-big-names-have-been-left-out-37219723.html |title =GAA to honour 'Hurling Team of the 1990s' at All-Ireland final - and some big names have been left out|date=15 August 2018|work=Irish Independent|access-date=16 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://gaa.ie/hurling/news/gaa-confirms-ceremonies-and-events-around-the-all-ireland-hurling-finals/ |title = GAA has confirmed a list of events and ceremonies which will take place around this Sunday's All-Ireland hurling finals|date=17 August 2018|work=GAA.ie|access-date=17 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://gaa.ie/news-archive/news/hurling-heroes-of-the-1990s-to-be-honoured-on-all-ireland-final-sunday/ |title = GAA to salute the star hurlers of the 1990s |date=15 August 2018|work=GAA.ie|access-date=17 August 2018}}</ref>

===Ticketing===
With a stadium capacity of 82,300, the 32 individual [[Gaelic Athletic Association county|county boards]] received 60,000 tickets. Schools and third level colleges got 2,500 tickets, while season ticket holders were entitled to 5,500 tickets. 1,000 tickets were given to overseas clubs. The [[Camogie Association|Camogie]], [[Ladies' Gaelic Football Association|Ladies' Football]], Handball and Rounders Associations were each allocated about 200 tickets, as were the jubilee teams and mini-7s which play at half-time. Demand for tickets was very high in both counties with Galway and Limerick having receiving around 32,000 tickets between. Stand tickets were priced at €80 with terrace at €40.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/brendan-cummins-hype-and-ticket-demands-are-part-of-the-final-buildup-but-opposition-should-be-first-concern-37198660.html |title = Brendan Cummins: Hype and ticket demands are part of the final build-up but opposition should be first concern|date=10 August 2018|work=Irish Independent|access-date=10 August 2018}}</ref>

===Related events===
The [[2018 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|2018 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Final]] was played between Galway and [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] as a curtain-raiser to the senior final with Galway retaining their title by winning 0–21 to 0–14.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2018/0819/986108-galway-minors-complete-back-to-back-all-ireland-success/ |title =Galway minors complete back-to-back All-Ireland success|date=19 August 2018|work=RTE Sport|access-date=21 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/snow-joke-as-lynskeys-galway-minors-go-backtoback-37231533.html |title =Snow joke as Lynskey's Galway minors go back-to-back|date=19 August 2018|work=Irish Independent|access-date=21 August 2018}}</ref>

==Match summary==
===Officials===
On 7 August 2018 the officials were chosen for the final by the [[Gaelic Athletic Association|GAA]], with Wexford's [[James Owens (referee)|James Owens]] being named as the referee in what was his second senior final after being the referee in [[2015 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2015]]. Tipperary's [[Fergal Horgan]] was the standby referee with Kilkenny's Sean Cleere the linesman and Carlow's Patrick Murphy the sideline official.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/james-owens-wexford-referee-hurling-final-4168542-Aug2018/ |title = Wexford's Owens to take charge of Limerick-Galway All-Ireland hurling final|date=7 August 2018|work=The 42|access-date=8 August 2018}}</ref>

===Team news===
The Limerick team announced for the final was unchanged from the semi-final win over [[Cork GAA|Cork]]. Galway made one change to the starting team with [[Gearóid McInerney]] recovering from a calf injury he picked up in the drawn game against [[Clare GAA|Clare]] and coming in to replace [[Niall Burke]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2018/0817/985854-galway-limerick-teams/ |title = GAA teams: One switch for Galway, Limerick unchanged|date=18 August 2018|work=RTE Sport|access-date=21 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-3-16-galway-2-18-how-the-limerick-players-rated-1.3601266|title =Limerick 3-16 Galway 2-18: How the Limerick players rated|date=19 August 2018|work=Irish Times|access-date=22 August 2018}}</ref>

===Summary===
Playing into the Davin end, [[Aaron Gillane]] opened the scoring for Limerick after 2 minutes. [[Joe Canning]] opened Galway's account with a 65 after 7 minutes to make the score 3 points to 1. Canning got another point in the 15th minute to level the score at 5 points each. In the 16th minute [[Graeme Mulcahy]] scrambled the ball over the line on the ground from close range after dropping it for the opening goal to put Limerick into a 2-point lead. A [[Séamus Flanagan]] point in the last minute of the first half made the score 1–10 to 0–9 at half-time.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-316-galway-218-as-it-happened-the-45year-wait-for-the-treaty-men-is-over-37230279.html |title =2018 All Ireland Final: as it happened|date=19 August 2018|work=Irish Independent|access-date=22 August 2018}}</ref>	

Four minutes into the second-half Kyle Hayes got the opening score to increase the lead to 4 points. Kyle Hayes got the decision from Hawk-Eye with another point a minute later to increase the lead to 6 points. After 54 minutes, Limerick got their second goal when [[Tom Morrissey (hurler)|Tom Morrissey]] pounced on a mistake from [[Gearoid McInerney]] to run in on goal and finish low and powerful to the net off the Hurley from the middle of the goal to put 9 points between the sides.<ref>{{cite web|url= http://www.gaa.ie/hurling/news/all-ireland-shc-final/|title =Limerick win first All-Ireland SHC since 1973|date=19 August 2018|work=GAA.ie|access-date=22 August 2018}}</ref>	
In the 68th minute, substitute [[Shane Dowling (hurler)|Shane Dowling]] got another goal for Limerick when he picked the ball up and finished with a low shot to the right of the net from the left to increase the lead to 8 points.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-3-16-galway-2-18-five-match-defining-moments-1.3601209|title =Limerick 3-16 Galway 2-18: Five match defining moments|date=19 August 2018|work=Irish Times|access-date=22 August 2018}}</ref>	
 
In the first of the 8 minutes of added time Galway scored a goal when [[Conor Whelan]] shot powerfully to the right of the net, four minutes later [[Joe Canning]] got another goal with a powerful shot to the top left corner of the net from a free to put 2 points between the sides.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/limerick-galway-hurling-final-analysis-4193041-Aug2018/ |title =Analysis: Limerick dominate puck-outs, their ferocious work-rate and Galway's attacking woes|date=21 August 2018|work=The 42|access-date=22 August 2018}}</ref>	
A minute later [[Niall Burke]] scored a point to put only one point between the sides. [[Graeme Mulcahy]] then scored a point for Limerick with a shot from the right to put 2 between them again before Joe Canning scored with a 65 to again make it a one-point game.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-hold-on-to-dethrone-galway-and-end-45-years-of-hurt-1.3601179|title =Limerick hold on to dethrone Galway and end 45 years of hurt|date=19 August 2018|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=22 August 2018}}</ref>	
In the last minute of time added on, Galway were awarded a free form inside their own half on the right, Joe Canning took the free which dropped short and was eventually cleared before the final sounded with Limerick the winners by one point.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/galway-limerick-all-ireland-final-4189637-Aug2018/ |title =2018 All Ireland Final: as it happened|date=19 August 2018|work=The 42|access-date=22 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/gaa/joe-cannings-all-ireland-final-free-wasnt-outside-his-range-it-was-just-probably-outside-his-comfort-zone-says-brother-ollie-882159.html |title =Joe Canning's All-Ireland final free 'wasn't outside his range, it was just probably outside his comfort zone', says brother Ollie|date=31 October 2018|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=2 November 2018}}</ref>

===Trophy presentation===
Limerick captain [[Declan Hannon]] accepted the [[Liam MacCarthy Cup]] from GAA president [[John Horan (GAA President)|John Horan]] in the Hogan Stand.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/limerick-all-ireland-hurling-champions-4189777-Aug2018/ |title =Champs at last! Limerick end 45-year wait for All-Ireland hurling glory|date=19 August 2018|work=The 42|access-date=21 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/billy-keane-hannon-raises-liam-to-lift-the-weight-of-45-years-off-a-countys-shoulders-37231486.html |title =Billy Keane: Hannon raises Liam to lift the weight of 45 years off a county's shoulders|date=19 August 2018|work=Irish Independent|access-date=21 August 2018}}</ref>

===Reaction===
Speaking after the final whistle, Limerick manager [[John Kiely (Limerick hurler)|John Kiely]] was happy that Limerick had held on in the final few minutes saying "It's huge, huge, huge relief, this group has phenomenal belief in its own abilities, its own resolve, that never-say-die attitude. We have worked so, so hard. Galway pushed us so hard in the last 10, 15 minutes. It was really difficult on the lads to hold their nerve to try and find those last few vital scores, but they did."<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2018/0819/986120-kiely-limerick-no-longer-second-class-hurling-citizens/|title =Kiely: Limerick no longer second-class hurling citizens|date=19 August 2018|work=RTE Sport|access-date=23 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/gaa/while-some-urge-limerick-fans-to-go-mental-john-kiely-yearns-for-somewhere-nice-and-quiet-863222.html |title =While some urge Limerick fans to 'go mental', John Kiely yearns for 'somewhere nice and quiet'|date=20 August 2018|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=23 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/330636/bridesmaid-no-more-declares-victorious-limerick-hurling-manager-john-kiely.html |title ='Bridesmaid no more' declares victorious Limerick hurling manager John Kiely|date=20 August 2018|work=Limerick Leader|access-date=23 August 2018}}</ref>

Galway manager [[Micheál Donoghue]] accepted that his side were 'a tad off' in the final but vowed that they will be back again next year saying "We're bitterly disappointed. I just felt we probably didn't get into the game but you have to give huge credit to Limerick. They started really well and were dominant for long periods."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2018/0819/986129-we-were-a-tad-off-but-these-boys-will-be-back/ |title =Donoghue: We were a tad off but these boys will be back|date=19 August 2018|work=RTE Sport|access-date=23 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/these-boys-have-shown-massive-resilience-theyll-be-back-micheal-donoghue-37236021.html |title =These boys have shown massive resilience, they'll be back - Micheal Donoghue|date=21 August 2018|work=Irish Independent|access-date=23 August 2018}}</ref>		
		
Highlights of the final were shown on ''The Sunday Game'' programme which aired at 9:30pm that night on [[RTÉ2]] and was presented by [[Des Cahill]] with match analysis from [[Brendan Cummins (GAA player)|Brendan Cummins]], [[Eddie Brennan]], and [[Anthony Daly (hurler)|Anthony Daly]]. On the man of the match award shortlist were [[Kyle Hayes]], [[Declan Hannon]] and [[Joe Canning]] with Kyle Hayes winning the award which was presented by GAA president [[John Horan (GAA President)|John Horan]] at the City West hotel in Dublin where the post match Limerick function was being held.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/kyle-hayes-man-of-the-match-4190424-Aug2018/ |title =Limerick's Kyle Hayes named All-Ireland final man of the match|date=19 August 2018|work=The 42|access-date=21 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/kyle-hayes-wins-man-of-the-match-limerick-dominate-sunday-game-best-xv-but-galway-star-was-their-hurler-of-the-year-37231272.html |title =Kyle Hayes wins Man of the Match, Limerick dominate Sunday Game best XV but Galway star was their hurler of the year|date=20 August 2018|work=Irish Independent|access-date=21 August 2018}}</ref>

===Celebrations===
The Limerick team returned home the day after the final where the homecoming event was held at [[Gaelic Grounds]], with the team arriving around 7:00pm, the MC was [[Marty Morrissey]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/gaa/limerick-homecoming-it-has-been-an-amazing-24-hours-and-there-are-many-more-to-come-863471.html |title =Limerick homecoming: 'It has been an amazing 24 hours and there are many more to come'|date=20 August 2018|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=21 August 2018}}</ref>	
An estimated 90,000 people turned out to see the team and fans lined a route from Colbert Rail Station where the team arrived at 5.40pm through Mallow Street, O'Connell Street, Sarsfield Bridge and out to the Ennis Road to the Gaelic Grounds which was packed by 45,000.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.thejournal.ie/limerick-homecoming-party-all-ireland-senior-hurling-champions-gaelic-grounds-monday-2-4190491-Aug2018/ |title =Gaelic Grounds to host homecoming for All-Ireland hurling champions in Limerick today|date=20 August 2018|work=The 42|access-date=21 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/newly-crowned-all-ireland-champions-limerick-receive-heroes-welcome-home-4191908-Aug2018/ |title = Newly crowned All-Ireland champions Limerick receive heroes' welcome home|date=20 August 2018|work=The 42|access-date=21 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/john-kiely-limerick-hurling-2-4192220-Aug2018/ |title = You were heading out into the back yard to look up at the stars and figure out the solution|date=20 August 2018|work=The 42|access-date=21 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/watch-the-tears-were-coming-out-of-my-eyes-lifting-liam-i-am-so-happy-80k-welcome-limerick-home-37233848.html |title =WATCH: 'The tears were coming out of my eyes, lifting Liam... I am so happy' - 80k welcome Limerick home|date=20 August 2018|work=Irish Independent|access-date=21 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/gaa/80000-plus-fans-pay-tribute-as-limericks-all-ireland-winning-team-return-home-863448.html |title =80,000 plus fans pay tribute as Limerick's All Ireland-winning team return home|date=20 August 2018|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=21 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2018/0820/986296-limerick-prepare-for-homecoming-after-hospital-visits/ |title =Almost 90,000 turn out to welcome home Limerick hurlers|date=20 August 2018|work=RTE Sport|access-date=21 August 2018}}</ref>

Tipperary are All Ireland Senior Hurling champions|website=The Nenagh Guardian}} | previous = [[2018 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2018]] | next = [[2020 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2020]] }} The '''2019 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final''' was a [[hurling]] match played at [[Croke Park]] in [[Dublin]] on 18 August 2019{{cite web|url=https://www.gaa.ie/hurling/gaa-hurling-all-ireland-senior-championship/fixtures|title=GAA Hurling All-Ireland Senior Championship|website=gaa.ie|access-date=2 April 2023}} between [[Kilkenny county hurling team|Kilkenny]] and [[Tipperary county hurling team|Tipperary]], the culmination of the [[2019 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]]. It was the [[List of All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship finals|132nd final]] of that sport's primary competition, the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]]. Tipperary defeated Kilkenny to claim their [[Tipperary GAA honours|28th All-Ireland title]].{{cite web|url=https://www.hoganstand.com/Tipperary/Article/Index/302982|title =All-Ireland SHC final: Tipp power past 14-man Cats to regain Liam|date=18 August 2019|work=Hogan Stand|access-date=21 August 2019}} The match was televised live on RTÉ2 as part of ''[[The Sunday Game]]'' presented by [[Joanne Cantwell]] from the Croke Park studio with analysis by [[Anthony Daly (hurler)|Anthony Daly]], [[Donal Óg Cusack]] and [[Henry Shefflin]]. Commentary on the game was provided by [[Marty Morrissey]] alongside [[Michael Duignan (hurler)|Michael Duignan]]. The match was also live on [[Sky Sports]] presented by [[Rachel Wyse]] and [[Brian Carney (rugby)|Brian Carney]] with analysis from [[Ollie Canning]], [[Jamesie O'Connor]] and [[J. J. Delaney]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2019/0814/1068748-how-to-watch-the-all-ireland-final-worldwide/|title = How to watch the All-Ireland final worldwide|website = [[RTÉ.ie]]|date = 15 August 2019}} An average of 804,500 viewers tuned in to watch the final on RTÉ with a peak audience of 901,900 just after 5pm.{{cite web|url= https://www.the42.ie/tv-figures-all-ireland-hurling-final-4772816-Aug2019/|title =Over 800,000 people tuned in to Tipperary's emphatic All-Ireland final victory|date=19 August 2019|work=The 42|access-date=21 August 2019}} ==Background== {{main article|Kilkenny–Tipperary hurling rivalry}} This was the ninth time since 2009 that the counties have played each other in the championship, with Kilkenny winning 5 times. Kilkenny went into the final having won 36 All Ireland titles, 11 titles in the last 18 years (2000, 2002, 2003, 2006, 2007, 2008, 2009, 2011, 2012, 2014, and 2015), with Tipperary on 27 titles, 3 titles over the same period (2001, 2010, and 2016). The teams had played each other 27 times in the championship, the first time being in 1887, with Kilkenny winning 12 times and Tipperary winning on 14 occasions with one draw in the final in 2014. Kilkenny had played in 66 All-Ireland finals, winning 36, losing 26 and drawing 4, with Tipperary having appeared in 41 All-Ireland finals, winning 27, losing 12 and drawing 2.{{cite web|url= https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/the-final-countdown-cork-s-patrick-horgan-gives-tipp-the-nod-1.3985942|title =The final countdown: Cork's Patrick Horgan gives Tipp the nod|date=14 August 2019|work=Irish Times|access-date=14 August 2019}} This was only the third occasion, since the introduction of the "back door" in [[1997 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1997]], that neither the [[Leinster Senior Hurling Championship]] winners (2019: Wexford) nor the [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship]] winners (2019: Limerick) have reached the final. This previously occurred in: *[[2004 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2004]] (Wexford and Waterford were provincial champions, final was Cork v Kilkenny) *[[2013 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Sky Sports }} ==Pre-match== ===Ticketing=== With a stadium capacity of 82,300, the 32 individual [[Gaelic Athletic Association county|county boards]] received 60,000 tickets. Schools and third level colleges got 2,500 tickets, while season ticket holders were entitled to 5,500 tickets. 1,000 tickets were given to overseas clubs. The [[Camogie Association|Camogie]], [[Ladies' Gaelic Football Association|Ladies' Football]], Handball and Rounders Associations were each allocated about 200 tickets, as were the jubilee teams and mini-7s which play at half-time. Demand for tickets was very high in both counties with Tipperary and Kilkenny having received around 32,000 tickets between. Stand tickets were priced at [[€]]90 with terrace at €45.{{cite web|url= https://www.hoganstand.com/Kilkenny/Article/Index/302735|title =Brennan blasts All-Ireland final ticket prices|date=12 August 2019|work=Hogan Stand|access-date=13 August 2019}}{{cite web|url= https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/gaa-defends-shocking-90-cost-of-stand-tickets-for-the-all-ireland-final-38398580.html|title =GAA defends 'shocking' €90 cost of stand tickets for the All Ireland final|date=13 August 2019|work=Irish Independent|access-date=13 August 2019}} ===Related events=== The [[2019 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|2019 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Final]] was played between Galway and [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] as a curtain-raiser to the senior final with Galway winning their third title in a row and 13th overall on a 3–14 to 0–12 scoreline.{{cite web|url= https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2019/0818/1069469-galway-make-it-three-minor-titles-on-the-spin/|title = Galway make it three minor titles on the spin as McDonagh stars|date=18 August 2019|work=RTE Sport|access-date=21 August 2019}} ===Jubilee team=== The [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] team that won the [[1994 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1994 All-Ireland Final]] was presented to the crowd before the match to mark 25 years. RTÉ commentator [[Michael Duignan (hurler)|Michael Duignan]] was part of the Offaly team.{{cite web|url= https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2019/0818/1069449-all-ireland-final-build-up-kilkenny-v-tipperary/|title = Tipperary 3-25 Kilkenny 0-20: Recap |date=18 August 2019|work=RTE Sport|access-date=21 August 2019}} ==Match summary== ===Officials=== On 6 August 2019 the officials were chosen for the final by the [[Gaelic Athletic Association|GAA]], with Wexford's [[James Owens (referee)|James Owens]] being named as the referee in what was his third senior final after being the referee in [[2015 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2015]] and [[2018 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2018]]. Paud O’Dwyer from Carlow was the standby referee with the other linesman being Johnny Murphy from Limerick and the sideline official was Liam Gordon from Galway.{{cite web|url= https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/james-owens-to-referee-hurling-final-for-second-year-running-1.3978805|title =James Owens to referee hurling final for second year running|date=10 August 2019|work=Irish Times|access-date=13 August 2019}} ===Team news=== The Tipperary team named for the match on the Friday night was the same that lined out in the semi-final against [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]]. Kilkenny brought [[Cillian Buckley]] into the team instead of [[Richie Leahy]] from the team that defeated [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] in the semi-final.{{cite news|url=https://www.the42.ie/kilkenny-tipperary-all-ireland-hurling-final-team-news-4769942-Aug2019/ |title =Kilkenny and Tipperary reveal their hands for All-Ireland hurling final|date=16 August 2019|work=The 42|access-date=21 August 2019|last1 =Team|first1 =The42}}{{cite web|url= https://www.hoganstand.com/Tipperary/Article/Index/302949|title =Team news: Tipp keep the faith for Kilkenny showdown|date=16 August 2019|work=Hogan Stand|access-date=21 August 2019}} ===Summary=== In wet and showery conditions, Kilkenny opened the scoring in the first minute with a free from [[TJ Reid]].{{cite web|url= https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/all-ireland-shc-final-kilkenny-0-20-tipperary-3-25-ft-1.3989863|title =All-Ireland SHC Final: Kilkenny 0-20 Tipperary 3-25 (FT)|date=19 August 2019|work=Irish Times|access-date=21 August 2019}} [[Michael Breen (hurler)|Michael Breen]] got Tipperary's first point after 3 minutes to make the score 2–1. A torrential downpour came after around 5 minutes of the game with many heading for cover under the stands.{{cite web|url= https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/tipperary-emerge-from-the-deluge-to-wash-away-kilkenny-1.3990243|title =Tipperary emerge from the deluge to wash away Kilkenny|date=19 August 2019|work=Irish Times|access-date=21 August 2019}} Tipperary playing into the Davin end in the first half might have had a penalty after 9 minutes when Seamus Callanan was pulled down inside the square with the referee awarding a free instead.{{cite web|url= https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2019/0818/1069449-all-ireland-final-build-up-kilkenny-v-tipperary/|title = Tipperary 3-25 Kilkenny 0-20: Recap |date=18 August 2019|work=RTE Sport|access-date=21 August 2019}} After 16 minutes [[Cathal Barrett]] caught [[Richie Hogan]] high across the faceguard with his hurley with Kilkenny being awarded a free which they scored to make it 6–3.{{cite web|url= https://www.the42.ie/live-what-score-is-kilkenny-v-tipperary-all-ireland-hurling-final-4771385-Aug2019/|title =2019 All Ireland Final: as it happened|date=18 August 2019|work=The 42|access-date=21 August 2019}} Three minutes later Tipperary goalkeeper [[Brian Hogan (Tipperary hurler)|Brian Hogan]] caught [[John Donnelly (hurler)|John Donnelly]]’s shot from over his crossbar with HawkEye awarding the point.{{cite web|url= https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2019/0820/1069917-hawk-eye-say-that-controversial-final-call-was-correct/|title = Hawk-Eye say that controversial All-Ireland final call was correct|date=20 August 2019|work=RTE.ie|access-date=21 August 2019}}{{cite web|url=https://www.hoganstand.com/Tipperary/Article/Index/302980 |title =Watch: Hawkeye awards Donnelly point|date=18 August 2019|work=Hogan Stand|access-date=21 August 2019}} Tipperary scored their first goal of the match after 25 minutes when [[Niall O'Meara]] turned past Conor Fogarty before shooting low to the right corner of the net to make the score 0-8 to 1-5.{{cite web|url= https://www.irishmirror.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/hurling-match-reports/tipperary-3-25-kilkenny-0-18958886|title =Tipperary 3-25 Kilkenny 0-20: Premier County are crowned All-Ireland hurling champions|date=19 August 2019|work=Irish Mirror|access-date=21 August 2019}} After 33 minutes Cathal Barrett was caught high with a raised elbow by Richie Hogan with the referee showing a straight red card to Hogan. Tipperary had a one point lead at half-time with the score 1-9 to 0-11.{{cite web|url= https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2019/0818/1069488-all-ireland-hurling-final-2019-kilkenny-0-20-tipperary-3-25/|title = Ruthless Tipperary dismantle 14-man Cats for 28th title|date=19 August 2019|work=RTE.ie|access-date=21 August 2019}}{{cite web|url= https://www.the42.ie/tipperary-kilkenny-all-ireland-hurling-final-talking-points-4771909-Aug2019/|title =Sheedy returns to the promised land, where it went wrong for Kilkenny and Callanan's goal rush|date=19 August 2019|work=The 42|access-date=21 August 2019}}{{cite web|url= https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/turning-point-something-had-to-give-in-fiery-battle-between-hogan-and-barrett-1.3990137|title = Turning point: Something had to give in fiery battle between Hogan and Barrett|date=18 August 2019|work=Irish Times|access-date=21 August 2019}} Kilkenny leveled the match with the first point of the second half.{{cite web|url= https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/gaa/premier-power-their-way-to-28th-all-ireland-title-944676.html|title = Tipperary 3-25 Kilkenny 0-20|date=18 August 2019|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=21 August 2019}} After 38 minutes Tipperary got a second goal, with Seamus Callanan getting his eighth goal of the championship when he followed up after John McGrath’s effort was half blocked to scramble the ball low to the left of the net.{{cite web|url= https://www.hoganstand.com/Tipperary/Article/Index/302984|title =Callanan downplays goal-scoring heroics|date=18 August 2019|work=Hogan Stand|access-date=21 August 2019}} {{cite web|url= https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/tipperary-punish-14-man-kilkenny-with-devastating-second-half-showing-1.3990049|title = Tipperary punish 14-man Kilkenny with devastating second-half showing|date=18 August 2019|work=Irish Times|access-date=21 August 2019}}{{cite web|url= https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/tipperary-are-allireland-champions-as-liam-sheedys-men-see-off-14man-kilkenny-in-croke-park-38413769.html|title = Tipperary are All-Ireland champions as Liam Sheedy's men see off 14-man Kilkenny in Croke Park|date=18 August 2019|work=Irish Times|access-date=21 August 2019}} Five minutes later they got their third goal when Seamus Callanan found [[John O'Dwyer]] with a cross-field pass from the right to the left edge of the box with O'Dwyer firing powerfully to the net to put Tipperary into an eight point lead on 3-12 to 0-13.{{cite web|url= https://www.the42.ie/callanan-bubbles-goal-4771637-Aug2019/|title =Tipp deadly duo Callanan and Bubbles combine for magical All-Ireland final goal|date=18 August 2019|work=The 42|access-date=21 August 2019}} Tipperary eased to victory after that and the full time score was 3-25 to 0-20 to win their 28th All-Ireland title.{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2019/0819/1069719-tipperary-did-a-kilkenny-on-kilkenny/ |title = Tipperary did a Kilkenny on Kilkenny|date=19 August 2019|work=RTE.ie|access-date=21 August 2019}}{{cite web|url= https://www.tippsupportersclub.com/westside-column-23-august-2019/|title =Westside Column 23 August 2019 |date=21 August 2019|work=Tipperary Supporters Club|access-date=21 August 2019}} ==Match details== {{GAAmatchbox |date = 18 August 2019 |time = 15:30 [[Time in Ireland|IST]] ([[UTC+01:00]]) |round = All-Ireland Final |report = A different perspective|date=16 August 2019|work=GAA.ie|access-date=21 August 2019}} The Tipperary team then did a victory lap around Croke Park with the trophy.{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2019/0818/1069490-callanan-this-is-everything-we-dreamed-of/ |title = Callanan: This is everything we dreamed of|date=18 August 2019|work=RTE.ie|access-date=21 August 2019}}{{cite web|url= https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2019/0818/1069485-gallery-the-story-of-tipperarys-all-ireland-victory/|title = Gallery: The story of Tipperary's All-Ireland victory|date=18 August 2019|work=RTE Sport|access-date=21 August 2019}}{{cite web|url= https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/all-ireland-hurling-final-1.3989848|title = All-Ireland Hurling Final|date=21 August 2019|work=Irish Times|access-date=21 August 2019}} ===Reaction=== Tipperary captain [[Séamus Callanan]] speaking to RTÉ after the match said "It’s everything we f...ing dreamed of, we put in so much work and to finally get there in the end of it is such an unbelievable feeling, I’m so proud of that group there."{{cite web|url= https://www.the42.ie/tipperary-all-ireland-kilkenny-4771595-Aug2019/|title ='Everything we dreamed of': Callanan overjoyed as Tipp triumph|date=18 August 2019|work=The 42|access-date=21 August 2019}}{{cite web|url= https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/watch-its-everything-we-fking-dreamed-of-seamus-callanan-cant-contain-his-joy-as-he-leads-tipp-to-promised-land-38413833.html|title =WATCH: 'It's everything we f**king dreamed of' - Seamus Callanan can't contain his joy as he leads Tipp to promised land|date=18 August 2019|work=Irish Independent|access-date=21 August 2019}} Tipperary manager [[Liam Sheedy]] speaking to RTÉ Radio singled out his family for special praise on the day of the match.{{cite web|url= https://www.the42.ie/liam-sheedy-tipperary-all-ireland-2019-4771705-Aug2019/|title =I have two very special girls. They gave me a card this morning that said, ''Dad, go and do it''|date=18 August 2019|work=The 42|access-date=21 August 2019}}{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/dunne-has-taken-hard-road-to-good-times-with-premier-county-38418749.html |title =Dunne has taken hard road to good times with Premier County|date=20 August 2019|work=Irish Independent|access-date=21 August 2019}}{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/tipperary-win-pics-agony-and-ecstasy-4771857-Aug2019/ |title =14 great photos that capture the agony and ecstasy of Tipperary's All-Ireland win|date=19 August 2019|work=The 42|access-date=21 August 2019}}{{cite web|url= https://www.the42.ie/tipperary-hurling-liam-sheedy-all-ireland-4771751-Aug2019/|title =Liam Sheedy: 'We have some of the best players ever to wear that blue and gold jersey'|date=19 August 2019|work=The 42|access-date=21 August 2019}}{{cite web|url= https://www.the42.ie/liam-sheedy-tipperary-hurling-8-4773274-Aug2019/|title =Liam Sheedy: 'To do it again with Eamon by my side is a very special moment'|date=20 August 2019|work=The 42|access-date=21 August 2019}}{{cite web|url= https://www.gaa.ie/news-archive/news/liam-sheedy-thrilled-with-tipperary-s-response/|title =Liam Sheedy thrilled with Tipperary's response|date=18 August 2019|work=GAA.ie|access-date=21 August 2019}} Kilkenny manager [[Brian Cody]] was amazed that a red card was shown to Richie Hogan, saying "We were beaten well in the final score but it is a huge decision to make, to issue a red card".{{cite web|url= https://www.the42.ie/brian-cody-richie-hogan-red-card-4771849-Aug2019/|title ='It took the referee a long, long time to make up his mind': Cody 'amazed' at Hogan's red card|date=18 August 2019|work=The 42|access-date=21 August 2019}}{{cite web|url= https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2019/0818/1069502-cody-gives-a-post-match-defensive-masterclass/|title = Cody gives a post-match defensive masterclass that his team would have been proud of|date=18 August 2019|work=RTE Sport|access-date=21 August 2019}} Former Kilkenny hurler [[Henry Shefflin]] speaking on ''[[The Sunday Game]]'' argued that the red card issued to Richie Hogan for the high tackle on Cathal Barrett should not have been red.{{cite web|url= https://www.the42.ie/henry-shefflin-on-hogan-red-card-all-ireland-final-the-sunday-game-4771675-Aug2019/|title =Shefflin: 'Where is the common sense to this? I'm not saying it because it's Kilkenny'|date=18 August 2019|work=The 42|access-date=21 August 2019}} Also former Kilkenny hyrler [[Jackie Tyrrell]] speaking on the Sunday Game on the night of the final also thought that a red card should not have been shown.{{cite web|url= https://www.hoganstand.com/Article/Index/303072?county=National|title = What they said … the weekend in quotes|date=19 August 2019|work=Hogan Stand|access-date=21 August 2019}}{{cite web|url= https://www.hoganstand.com/Tipperary/Article/Index/303084|title = Sure I'll meet him and we'll have it out|date=19 August 2019|work=Hogan Stand|access-date=21 August 2019}} [[Richie Hogan]] speaking two days after the final insisted that it should never have been a red card.{{cite web|url= https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/its-not-irish-dancing-kilkennys-richie-hogan-defends-red-card-tackle-in-allireland-final-38422088.html|title ='It's not Irish dancing' - Kilkenny's Richie Hogan defends red card tackle in All-Ireland Final|date=21 August 2019|work=Irish Independent|access-date=21 August 2019}}{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/richie-hogan-red-card-2-4775464-Aug2019/ |title =Richie Hogan: 'In my opinion, there was absolutely no way it was a sending-off'|date=20 August 2019|work=The 42|access-date=21 August 2019}}{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2019/0819/1069572-barrett-airs-hogan-sympathy-on-biggest-day-of-year/ |title = Barrett airs Hogan sympathy on 'biggest day of year'|date=20 August 2019|work=RTE Sport|access-date=21 August 2019}} Kilkenny appealed the one match suspension given to Hogan but on 6 November the suspension was upheld.{{cite web|url= https://www.the42.ie/kilkenny-hurling-richie-hogan-red-card-4881486-Nov2019/|title =Suspension upheld for Kilkenny's Hogan after All-Ireland final red card|date=6 November 2019|work=The 42|access-date=7 November 2019}} Highlights of the final were shown on ''The Sunday Game'' programme which aired at 9:30pm that night on RTÉ2 and was presented by [[Des Cahill]] with match analysis from [[Brendan Cummins (GAA player)|Brendan Cummins]], [[Cyril Farrell]], [[Jackie Tyrell]], [[Ursula Jacob]], [[Graeme Mulcahy]], [[Derek McGrath (hurler)|Derek McGrath]] and [[Enda Rowland]]. On the man of the match award shortlist were [[Ronan Maher (hurler)|Ronan Maher]], [[Noel McGrath (hurler)|Noel McGrath]] and [[Barry Heffernan]] with Noel McGrath winning the award which was presented by GAA president John Horan at the post match Tipperary function at the Clayton Burlington Hotel in Dublin.{{cite web|url= https://www.the42.ie/noel-mcgrath-man-of-the-match-tipperary-4771939-Aug2019/|title =Tipperary star Noel McGrath named All-Ireland final man-of-the-match|date=19 August 2019|work=The 42|access-date=21 August 2019}}{{cite news|url= https://www.the42.ie/all-ireland-shc-final-player-ratings-4771410-Aug2019/|title =Tipperary player ratings: Maher and Heffernan lead the way in heroic team performance|date=18 August 2019|work=The 42|access-date=21 August 2019|last1 =O'Brien|first1 =Kevin}}{{cite web|url= https://www.the42.ie/ronna-maher-barry-heffernan-tipperary-player-watch-4772102-Aug2019/|title =The dynamic duo in the Tipp defence that lorded the skies against Kilkenny|date=20 August 2019|work=The 42|access-date=21 August 2019}} ===Celebrations=== The Tipperary team made the traditional visits to Our Lady's Children's Hospital in Crumlin and Temple Street hospital on 19 August before returning home by train where the homecoming event was held at [[Semple Stadium]] in [[Thurles]]. A temporary stage was set up along the side-line of the new stand for the event with the crowd on the pitch.{{cite web|url= https://www.the42.ie/tipperary-all-ireland-champions-hospitals-liam-mccarthy-4772726-Aug2019/|title =Tipperary's All-Ireland champions visit children's hospitals with Liam MacCarthy|date=19 August 2019|work=The 42|access-date=21 August 2019}}{{cite web|url= https://www.hoganstand.com/Article/Index/303049?county=National|title = Pics: Smiles all round as All-Ireland champions visit Children's Hospital|date=19 August 2019|work=Hogan Stand|access-date=21 August 2019}} The Tipperary senior back-room team and players were introduced to a crowd of over 30,000 at 8.00 pm, with all the players and manager introduced and captain Seamus Callanan addressing the crowd after carrying the cup on stage with manager Liam Sheedy. [[The 2 Johnnies]] entertained the crowd during the celebrations.{{cite web|url= https://www.the42.ie/tipperary-homecoming-semple-stadium-pics-4774344-Aug2019/|title =In pics: Fans turn out in huge numbers for Tipperary's victorious homecoming celebrations|date=20 August 2019|work=The 42|access-date=21 August 2019}}{{cite web|url= https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2019/0819/1069639-tipperary-prepare-for-homecoming-in-semple-stadium/|title = Tipperary prepare for homecoming in Semple Stadium|date=20 August 2019|work=RTE Sport|access-date=21 August 2019}}{{cite web|url= https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/chorus-of-tipperary-emotion-greets-all-ireland-stars-1.3991238|title =Chorus of Tipperary emotion greets All-Ireland stars|date=20 August 2019|work=Irish Times|access-date=21 August 2019}}{{cite web|url= https://www.gaa.ie/news-archive/news/in-pictures-tipperary-s-homecoming-celebrations/|title =In pictures: Tipperary's homecoming celebrations|date=20 August 2019|work=GAA.ie|access-date=21 August 2019}} ==References== {{Reflist}} {{All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship}} {{GAA 2019}} [[Category:2019 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|Final]] [[Category:2019 in hurling|All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final]] [[Category:2010s in Dublin (city)|All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final, 2019]] [[Category:August 2019 sports events in Ireland|All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final]] [[Category:All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship finals]] [[Category:GAA finals at Croke Park]] [[Category:Kilkenny county hurling team matches]] [[Category:Tipperary county hurling team matches]]

The '''2020 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final''' was a [[hurling]] match played at [[Croke Park]] in [[Dublin]] on 13 December 2020<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.irishcentral.com/sports/gaa-all-ireland-2020|title=GAA confirms plans for this year's Inter-County Football and Hurling Championships|date=June 26, 2020|website=IrishCentral.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/gaa-december-all-ireland-5133792-Jun2020/|title=December All-Ireland final dates confirmed as GAA unveil 2020 championship plan|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole|website=The42}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/all-ireland-finals-set-for-december-13th-and-19th-as-gaa-confirm-2020-schedule-1.4289406|title=All-Ireland finals set for December 13th and 19th as GAA confirm 2020 schedule|first=Ian|last=O'Riordan|newspaper=The Irish Times}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/2020-all-ireland-senior-hurling-championship-key-dates-1.4289497|title=2020 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship key dates|first=Seán|last=Moran|newspaper=The Irish Times}}</ref> between [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick]] and [[Waterford county hurling team|Waterford]], the culmination of the [[2020 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]]. It was the [[List of All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship finals|133rd final]] of that sport's primary competition, the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]].

Limerick won the game by 0–30 to 0–19 to claim their second All-Ireland title in three years.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gaa.ie/hurling/gaa-hurling-all-ireland-senior-championship/limerick-waterford/1739657/|title=LIMERICK 0-30 WATERFORD 0-19|date=13 December 2020|work=GAA.ie|accessdate= 11 May 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2020/1213/1184174-all-ireland-shc-final-limerick-v-waterford-build-up/|title=All-Ireland SHC final recap: Limerick 0-30 Waterford 0-19|date=13 December 2020|work=RTE Sport|accessdate= 11 May 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/live-all-ireland-hurling-final-limerick-0-30-waterford-0-19-ft-1.4435608|title=LIVE All-Ireland hurling final: Limerick 0-30 Waterford 0-19 (FT)|date=13 December 2020|work=Irish Times|accessdate= 11 May 2021}}</ref>

The match was televised live on RTÉ2 as part of ''[[The Sunday Game]]'', presented by [[Joanne Cantwell]] from the outside studio at Croke Park, with analysis by [[Anthony Daly (hurler)|Anthony Daly]], [[Donal Óg Cusack]] and [[Henry Shefflin]]. Commentary on the game was provided by [[Marty Morrissey]] alongside [[Michael Duignan (hurler)|Michael Duignan]]. The match was also live on [[Sky Sports]], with analysis from [[Jamesie O'Connor]] and [[Ollie Canning]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-waterford-all-ireland-hurling-final-live-score-updates-5298330-Dec2020/|title=Limerick 0-30 Waterford 0-19: As it happened|date=13 December 2020|work=The 42|accessdate= 11 May 2021}}</ref>

==Background==
*The championship was delayed due to the [[impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on Gaelic games]]. This was the latest the final had taken place in a year since [[1924 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|1924]], when the All-Ireland hurling final took place on 14 December.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-31008354.html|title=Own points and unfinished matches: The story of hurling championship games in December|first=Leo|last=McGough|date=June 30, 2020|website=Irish Examiner}}</ref>
*Waterford had not won the All-Ireland since [[1959 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1959]] (61 years) and had only appeared in three finals in the interim ([[1963 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|1963]], [[2008 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2008]] and [[2017 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2017]]).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/cyril-farrell-triedandtrusted-waterford-gameplan-will-rattle-galway-36028648.html|title=Cyril Farrell: Tried-and-trusted Waterford game-plan will rattle Galway|date=14 August 2017|work=Irish Independent|access-date=14 August 2017}}</ref>
*This was the third final in the previous four years not to involve one of the [[Big Three (hurling)|Big Three]] (Cork, Kilkenny, Tipperary) — the [[2017 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2017]] (Galway—Waterford) and [[2018 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2018]] (Limerick—Galway) finals also did not involve them.
*This was the third final in which both the teams were from the province of Munster, with the first two being in [[1997 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|1997]] (Clare—Tipperary) and [[2013 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2013]] (Clare—Cork).
*This was only the third All-Ireland final in history in which neither team scored a goal, the first two being in 1999 and 2004.

==Pre-match==
The [[2020 Joe McDonagh Cup final]] between [[Kerry county hurling team|Kerry]] and [[Antrim county hurling team|Antrim]] took place prior to the All-Ireland senior final.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40186725.html|title= Antrim and Kerry hurlers may not watch All-Ireland final at Croke Park |date=8 December 2020|work=Irish Examiner|access-date= 9 December 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40189899.html|title=Antrim see off Kerry to secure McDonagh Cup success at Croke Park |date=13 December 2020|work=Irish Examiner|access-date= 16 December 2020}}</ref>

On 4 December 2020, the officials were chosen for the final by the [[Gaelic Athletic Association|GAA]], with Tipperary's [[Fergal Horgan]] being named as the referee in what would be his second senior final after being the referee in [[2017 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2017]]. Colm Lyons from Cork was named as standby referee, with the other linesman being Paud O'Dwyer from Carlow and the sideline official Seán Cleere from Kilkenny.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40148969.html|title= Fergal Horgan confirmed as All-Ireland Hurling final referee|date=4 December 2020|work=Irish Examiner|access-date= 9 December 2020}}</ref>

===Jubilee team===
The [[Clare county hurling team|Clare]] team that won the [[1995 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|1995 All-Ireland Final]] were remembered before the match to mark 25 years. There was no traditional walk out and parade due to [[COVID-19]] restrictions but the Clare captain of 1995 [[Anthony Daly (hurler)|Anthony Daly]] was present to place the Liam MacCarthy Cup in front of the Hogan Stand before the match.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.gaa.ie/hurling/news/anthony-daly-to-represent-clare-jubilee-team-on-all-ireland-day/|title=Anthony Daly to represent Clare jubilee team on All-Ireland day|date=6 January 2021|work=GAA.iel|access-date= 6 January 2021}}</ref>

{{Short description|none}} {{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}} {{Infobox football match | title = 2021 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final | image = | image_size = 250 | event = [[2021 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]] | team1 = [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick]] | team1association = [[File:Colours of Limerick.svg|40px]] | team1score = 3–32 | team2 = [[Cork county hurling team|Cork]] | team2association = [[File:Colours of Cork.svg|40px]] | team2score = 1–22 | date = 22 August 2021 | stadium = [[Croke Park]] | city = [[Dublin]] | man_of_the_match1a = [[Cian Lynch]]{{cite news|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40364450.html|title=Limerick Messi Cian Lynch named final man of the match|work=[[Irish Examiner]]|first=Larry|last=Ryan|date=22 August 2021}}{{cite news|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2021/0822/1242237-lynch-treasuring-special-limerick-moments/|title=Lynch treasuring 'special' Limerick moments|publisher=[[RTÉ News]]|date=22 August 2021|accessdate=22 August 2021}} | referee = [[Fergal Horgan]] ([[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]]) | weather = Dry with sunny spells
{{convert|20|°C|°F|abbr=on}}{{Cite journal|url=https://hoganstand.com/Article/Index/319524|title=Met Eireann forecasts dry weather for All-Ireland hurling final|first=|last=|date=22 August 2021|accessdate=22 August 2021|journal=Hogan Stand}} | attendance = 82,000 | previous = [[2020 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2020]] | next = [[2022 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2022]] }} The '''2021 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final''' was a [[hurling]] match played at [[Croke Park]] in [[Dublin]] on 22 August 2021{{cite web|url=https://www.gaa.ie/hurling/gaa-hurling-all-ireland-senior-championship/fixtures|title=GAA Hurling All-Ireland Senior Championship|access-date=20 March 2023|website=GAA}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/gaa-2021-roadmap-5403856-Apr2021/|title=GAA unveils 2021 roadmap with leagues starting in May and All-Ireland finals in August|first=Kevin|last=O'Brien|website=The42}} between [[Cork county hurling team|Cork]] and [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick]], the culmination of the [[2021 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]]. It was the [[List of All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship finals|134th final]] of that sport's primary competition, the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]]. Limerick won the game by 3–32 to 1–22 to claim their third All-Ireland title in four years. This final marked the highest winning score ever achieved in an All-Ireland Senior Hurling final, surpassing Kilkenny's previous record set in the [[2008 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2008]] final.{{cite news|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2021/0822/1242236-limerick-crush-cork-to-claim-back-to-back-all-irelands/|title=Limerick crush Cork to claim back-to-back All-Irelands|publisher=[[RTÉ News and Current Affairs]]|first=Eoin|last=Ryan|date=22 August 2021|accessdate=22 August 2021}}{{cite news|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40364432.html|title=Record-breaking Limerick retain All-Ireland title after powerful win over Cork|publisher=[[Irish Examiner]]|first=John|last=Fogarty|date=22 August 2021|accessdate=22 August 2021}}{{cite news|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-cork-all-ireland-hurling-final-5529019-Aug2021/|title=Awesome Limerick storm past Cork to retain All-Ireland senior hurling crown|publisher=[[TheJournal.ie#The42.ie|The42.ie]]|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole|date=22 August 2021|accessdate=22 August 2021}} The match was also the highest scoring final in the 134-year history of the fixture.{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2021/0822/1242223-all-ireland-shc-finalcork-v-limerick-updates/|title=Recap: Limerick 3-32 Cork 1-22|date=22 August 2021|work=RTE Sport|accessdate= 25 August 2021}} Due to [[COVID-19]] restrictions, attendance was at 50% (40,000 people).{{Cite web |url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2021/0730/1238276-attendance-boost-for-all-ireland-finals-wc-qualifiers/|title=Attendance to increase to 40,000 for All-Ireland finals|first=Damian|last=Lawlor|date=July 30, 2021|via=www.rte.ie}} The match was televised live on [[RTÉ2]] as part of ''[[The Sunday Game]]'', presented by [[Joanne Cantwell]] from the outside studio at Croke Park with analysis by [[Anthony Daly (hurler)|Anthony Daly]], [[Donal Óg Cusack]] and [[Henry Shefflin]]. Commentary on the game was provided by [[Marty Morrissey]] alongside [[Michael Duignan (hurler)|Michael Duignan]]. The match was also live on [[Sky Sports]], with analysis from [[Jamesie O'Connor]] and [[Ollie Canning]]. ==Background== The two finalists share a [[Cork–Limerick hurling rivalry|Munster rivalry]], with the sides having faced one another more than 100 times in the [[National Hurling League|league]] and championship since their inaugural match in November 1893. The game was the 66th championship meeting between the sides and was their first time meeting in an All-Ireland final. [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] made their 19th All-Ireland final appearance and their third in the last four championship seasons, having missed out in [[2019 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2019]].{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-kilkenny-all-ireland-semi-final-report-4742990-Jul2019/|title=Brilliant Kilkenny slay champions Limerick to book first All-Ireland final since 2016|publisher=The 42|date=27 July 2019|accessdate=11 August 2021|first=|last=}} However, they were undefeated in those recent finals appearances, beating [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in [[2018 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2018]] and [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] in [[2020 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2020]].{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickpost.ie/2020/12/20/talking-points-as-limerick-claim-a-ninth-ever-all-ireland-hurling-title/|title=Talking Points as Limerick claim a ninth ever All-Ireland Hurling Title|publisher=Limerick Post|date=20 December 2020|accessdate=11 August 2021|first=|last=}} Limerick's seven previous All-Ireland titles were secured at various intervals between [[1897 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1897]] and [[1973 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1973]]. They were seeking their 10th All-Ireland title overall and their first ever consecutive titles. [[Cork GAA|Cork]] made their 50th All-Ireland final appearance overall and their first since defeat by [[Clare GAA|Clare]] in [[2013 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2013]]. They last won the title against Galway in [[2005 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2005]], meaning that the 16-year title drought equals their previous record of no titles between [[1903 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1903]] and [[1919 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1919]].{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/not-since-1903-1919-have-cork-gone-so-long-without-a-hurling-all-ireland-has-their-time-come-again-37162583.html|title=Not since 1903-1919 have Cork gone so long without a hurling All-Ireland, has their time come again?|publisher=Irish Independent|date=18 July 2018|accessdate=11 August 2021|first=|last=}}{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/cork-s-near-record-dry-spell-casts-minds-back-to-2004-05-glory-days-1.4351958|title=Cork's near-record dry spell casts minds back to 2004-05 glory days|publisher=Irish Times|date=11 September 2020|accessdate=11 August 2021|first=Seán|last=Moran}} Cork currently lie second only to Kilkenny on the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship records and statistics#General performances|all-time roll of honour]] and were seeking their 31st All-Ireland title, having won all their previous titles at various intervals between [[1890 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1890]] and 2005. For the first time since [[1999 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1999]], not one single member of the Cork team was a holder of an All-Ireland winners' medal. This final was the fourth all-[[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] final in the history of the championship, after [[1997 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1997]] between Clare and [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]], 2013 between Clare and Cork and 2020 between Limerick and Waterford. It was the eighth time when teams from the same province met.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/the-best-and-worst-hurling-finals-when-teams-from-the-same-province-meet-1.4643227|title=The best and worst: Hurling finals when teams from the same province meet|publisher=Irish Times|date=10 August 2021|accessdate=11 August 2021|first=Seán|last=Moran}} This final marked the third meeting between the teams in the All-Ireland Championship proper. The series currently stood at one apiece, with Cork winning the [[2006 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2006 All-Ireland quarter-final]] and Limerick winning the [[2018 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2018 All-Ireland semi-final]]. Both sides had already played each other in the 2021 championship, with Limerick beating Cork by 2-22 to 1-17 in the Munster semi-final.{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-cork-hurling-2-5483927-Jul2021/|title=First-half goal blast clinches win for Limerick against Cork to book Munster final spot|publisher=The 42|date=3 July [[Sky Sports]] }} ==Pre-match== ===Officials=== On 10 August 2021, the GAA named [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]]'s [[Fergal Horgan]] as the referee for the final.{{cite news|url=https://www.gaa.ie/hurling/news/gaa-confirms-fergal-horgan-to-referee-the-2021-gaa-hurling-all-ireland-senior-fi/|title=GAA confirms Fergal Horgan to referee the 2021 GAA Hurling All-Ireland Senior Final|publisher=GAA website|date=10 August 2021|accessdate=11 August 2021|first=|last=|newspaper=www.gaa.ie }} Horgan has been an inter-county referee since joining the [[Munster GAA|Munster]] panel of referees in 2011, before joining the national panel in 2012. He officiated three prior matches in the 2021 championship; the Leinster semi-final between [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] and [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]], the round 1 qualifier between Wexford and [[Clare GAA|Clare]] and the All-Ireland semi-final between [[Cork GAA|Cork]] and Kilkenny. Horgan also served as referee for the All-Ireland finals in [[2017 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2017]] and [[2020 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2020]].{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/fergal-horganselected-to-take-charge-of-his-third-all-ireland-hurling-final-for-cork-and-limerick-showpiece-40736742.html|title=Fergal Horgan selected to take charge of his third All-Ireland hurling final for Cork and Limerick showpiece|publisher=Irish Independent|date=10 August 2021|accessdate=11 August 2021|first=|last=}} His umpire team was John Ryan ([[Cashel King Cormacs GAA|Cashel King Cormacs]]), Alan Horgan, Mick Butler, and Sean Bradshaw (all [[Knockavilla-Donaskeigh Kickhams GAA|Knockavilla-Donaskeigh Kickhams]]). Wexford's [[James Owens (referee)|James Owens]] was named as the standby referee.{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/all-ireland-hurling-final-2021-referee-fergal-horgan-5519517-Aug2021/|title=Tipperary's Fergal Horgan to referee All-Ireland senior hurling final|publisher=The 42|date=10 August 2021|accessdate=11 August 2021|first=|last=}} The other linesman were Seán Stack ([[Dublin GAA|Dublin]]) and the sideline official, Liam Gordon ([[Galway GAA|Galway]]).{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2021/0810/1240062-horgan-appointed-to-referee-all-ireland-hurling-final/|title=Horgan appointed to referee All-Ireland hurling final|publisher=RTÉ Sport|date=10 August 2021|accessdate=11 August 2021|first=|last=}} ===Pageantry=== A number of traditional All-Ireland final elements returned for the first time since the [[2019 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2019 All-Ireland final]], however, a number of these were scaled back due to [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports in the Republic of Ireland|COVID-19 protocols]]. [[President of Ireland|President]] [[Michael D. Higgins]]’ arrival was announced to the crowd but the custom of him meeting the players along with the [[GAA President]] did not take place. The pre-match parade featuring the [[Artane Band]] made a return.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40362566.html|title=Two cheers for the Rebels: Cork allowed to make second entry onto pitch on Sunday|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=19 August 2021|accessdate=22 August 2021|first=John|last=Fogarty}} [[1996 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1996 All-Ireland Championship]] winners [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] were not honoured in the traditional fashion as this year's [[silver jubilee]] team. Instead, [[List of Wexford senior hurling team captains|captain]] [[Martin Storey]] represented the team when he brought out the [[Liam MacCarthy Cup]] to the plinth on the pitch before the game.{{cite web|url=https://hoganstand.com/Article/Index/319511|title=Martin Storey to represent Wexford's heroes of 1996 as jubilee team at All-Ireland SHC final|publisher=Hogan Stand|date=21 August 2021|accessdate=22 August 2021|first=|last=}} ==Match== ===Summary=== [[Cian Lynch]] opened the scoring with a point for Limerick in the first minute. [[Gearóid Hegarty]] got the opening goal of the game after two minutes with a low shot after cutting in from the left to make it 1-1 to 0-1. Two minutes later Cork replied with a goal from [[Shane Kingston]] when he cut in from the left and shot high to the net. In the fifteenth minute, [[Aaron Gillane]] scored a second goal for Limerick with a low shot to the right corner of the net after a pass from Seamus Flanagan to make it 2-5 to 1-5.{{cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/live-blog/30554/12387954/all-ireland-hurling-championship-final-2021-cork-vs-limerick-live|title=All-Ireland Hurling Championship Final 2021: Cork vs Limerick as it happened...|date=22 August 2021|work=SKY Sports|accessdate= 25 August 2021}} Limerick were ahead by 2-8 to 1-6 at the first water break. In the thirty-fifth minute, Gearóid Hegarty got a third goal for Limerick and his second when he ran in on goal and shot low to the left corner of the net. Limerick were ahead by thirteen points at half-time on a 3-18 to 1-11 scoreline. They kept Cork at bay in the second half and scored another fourteen points to eleven for Cork to win the game 3-32 to 1-22 and retain the title.{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/live/northern-ireland/58297943|title=As it happened: Limerick storm to All-Ireland glory|date=22 August 2021|work=BBC Sport|accessdate= 25 August 2021}} ===Details=== {{GAAmatchbox |bg = |date = 22 August 2021 |time= 15:30 |round = All-Ireland Final |report = [https://www.the42.ie/limerick-cork-all-ireland-hurling-final-5529019-Aug2021/ Report] |team1 = [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick]] |score1 = 3-32 {{small|(41)}} |score2 = {{small|(25)}} 1-22 |team2 = [[Cork county hurling team|Cork]] |HT = 3-18 {{small|(27)}} - {{small|(14)}} 1-11 |goals1 = G Hegarty 2, A Gillane 1. |points1 = A Gillane 6 (3f), C Lynch 6, P Casey 5, T Morrissey 3, G Hegarty 2, D Byrnes 2 (1f), D Hannon 2, B Nash 1, D O'Donovan 1, S Flanagan 1, G Mulcahy 1, D Reidy 1, P Ryan 1. |goals2 = S Kingston 1. |points2 = P Horgan 12 (10f), S Harnedy 4, N O'Leary 1, M Coleman 1 (f), L Meade 1, J O'Connor 1, S Barrett 1, A Cadogan 1. |location = [[Dublin]] |venue = [[Croke Park]] |attendance = 40,000 |referee = [[Fergal Horgan]] ([[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]]) |TV = [[RTÉ]], [[Sky Sports]] }} {{col-begin}} {{col-2}} {{Football kit | pattern_la = _oneillswhite | pattern_b = _vneck | pattern_ra = _oneillswhite | pattern_sh = _oneills20onwhite | pattern_so = _hoops_white | leftarm = 009900 | body = 009900 | rightarm = 009900 | shorts = 009900 | socks = 009900 | title = Limerick }} {{col-2}} {{Football kit | pattern_la = _whitelines | pattern_b = | pattern_ra = _whitelines | pattern_sh = _red_stripes_adidas | pattern_so = | leftarm = ff0000 | body = ff0000 | rightarm = ff0000 | shorts = ffffff | socks = ff0000 |title = Cork }} {{col-end}} {{col-begin}} {{col-2}} {| style="font-size:90%; {{convert|29|°C|°F|abbr=on}}{{cite web|url=https://hoganstand.com/Article/Index/324275|title=Soaring temperatures for All-Ireland hurling final day|website=[[HoganStand.com]]|date=17 July 2022|accessdate=17 July 2022}} | attendance = | previous = [[2021 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2021]] | next = [[2023 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2023]] }} The '''2022 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final''' was a [[hurling]] match played at [[Croke Park]] in [[Dublin]] on 17 July 2022 between [[Kilkenny county hurling team|Kilkenny]] and [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick]], the culmination of the [[2022 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]]. It was the [[List of All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship finals|135th final]] of that sport's primary competition, the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]]. This was the earliest in the year that the final had ever taken place. Some past finals had taken place at dates earlier in the year, but these were finals rescheduled from the years in which they were originally supposed to occur.{{Cite web|url=https://www.gaa.ie/news/gaa-publish-master-fixtures-schedule-for-2022/|title=GAA publish Master Fixtures Schedule for 2022|website=www.gaa.ie}}{{Cite news|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2021/1122/1262358-only-championship-finals-will-have-replays-next-year/|title=25-week inter-county season to conclude by late July|first=Damian|last=Lawlor|date=November 22, 2021|via=www.rte.ie}} Reigning title holder Limerick won the game by 1–31 to 2–26 to claim their fourth title in five years and their first ever three-in-a-row.{{cite news|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2022/0717/1310723-resilient-limerick-see-off-cats-to-claim-three-in-a-row/|title=Resilient Limerick see off Kilkenny to claim three-in-a-row|publisher=[[RTÉ News and Current Affairs]]|first=Eoin|last=Ryan|date=17 July 2022|accessdate=17 July 2022}}{{cite web|url= https://www.the42.ie/limerick-kilkenny-all-ireland-hurling-5819034-Jul2022/|title=Limerick complete All-Ireland three-in-a-row after epic contest against Kilkenny|date=17 July 2022|work=The 42|accessdate=19 July 2022}} The game was the joint highest scoring final in history, equalling the total of 66 points scored in the 2021 final between Limerick and Cork,{{cite news|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2021/0822/1242223-all-ireland-shc-finalcork-v-limerick-updates/|title=Recap: Limerick 3-32 Cork 1-22|publisher=[[RTÉ Sport]]|date=22 August 2021|accessdate=21 July 2022}} and had the most scores (60) in a final, surpassing the 58 scores of the 2021 final. Kilkenny's score of 2–26 was the highest total for a losing team in a final. There were 25 different scorers in the game, 10 for Limerick and 15 for Kilkenny. The match was televised live on [[RTÉ One]] as part of ''[[The Sunday Game]]'', presented by [[Joanne Cantwell]] from the Croke Park studio with analysis by [[Anthony Daly (hurler)|Anthony Daly]], [[Dónal Óg Cusack]] and [[Liam Sheedy]]. Commentary on the game was provided by [[Marty Morrissey]] alongside [[Michael Duignan (hurler)|Michael Duignan]].{{cite web|url=https://presspack.rte.ie/2022/07/16/sport-on-rte-one-rte2-week-29-4/|title=SPORT ON RTÉ ONE & RTÉ2 Week 29|website=[[RTÉ.ie]]|publisher=RTÉ Press Centre|date=15 July 2022|accessdate=17 July 2022}} The match was also live on [[Sky Sports]], with analysis from [[Jamesie O'Connor]], [[Ollie Canning]] and [[J. J. Delaney]]. [[Audience share]] for television coverage of the game in Ireland was 72%.{{cite news|url=https://www.kilkennypeople.ie/news/gaa/863368/revealed-how-many-viewers-tuned-into-the-all-ireland-hurling-final.html|title=REVEALED: How many viewers tuned into the All-Ireland hurling final?|work=[[Kilkenny People]]|date=18 July 2022}} ==Background== {{main|Kilkenny–Limerick hurling rivalry}} *This was the first meeting of Kilkenny and Limerick in the final since [[2007 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2007]]. The [[Liam MacCarthy Cup]] was brought out onto the pitch by two Ukrainian children who had fled their country due to the ongoing [[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine|Russian invasion of Ukraine]]. ===Build-up=== The final was shown on a giant screen at the [[Gaelic Grounds]] in Limerick where an all ticket crowd watched the match.{{cite news|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40918889.html|title=All-Ireland final: TUS Gaelic Grounds to run fan zone for supporters|publisher=[[Irish Examiner]]|first=Eoghan|last=Cormican|date=16 July 2022|accessdate=17 July 2022}} ===Jubilee teams=== The [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] team that won the [[1996 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1996 All-Ireland Final]] along with the [[Clare GAA|Clare]] teams that won the [[1995 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1995]] and [[1997 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1997]] All-Ireland Final's were presented to the crowd before the match. The first time teams were presented on the pitch since the [[2019 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2019 All-Ireland Final]].{{cite web|url= https://hoganstand.com/Wexford/article/index/324280|title=1990's Clare and Wexford All-Ireland winning teams honoured on All-Ireland final day|date=17 July 2022|work=[[HoganStand.com]]|accessdate=19 July 2022}} ==Match== ===Summary=== In dry and very warm conditions of {{convert|29|°C|°F|abbr=on}} due to a [[July 2022 European heat wave|heat wave]], [[Diarmaid Byrnes]] opened the scoring in the first minute. In front of a crowd of over 80,000 for the first time since the [[2019 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2019 All-Ireland final]] due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the Republic of Ireland|COVID-19 pandemic]], [[Gearóid Hegarty]] got the opening goal of the game after four minutes with a strike to the left corner of the net from out on the right to make it 1-1 to no score.{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-kilkenny-all-ireland-hurling-final-live-score-updates-5819458-Jul2022/ |title=AS IT HAPPENED: LIMERICK V KILKENNY, ALL-IRELAND HURLING FINAL|date=17 July 2022|work=The 42|accessdate=19 July 2022}} Limerick were ahead by four points at half-time on a 1-17 to 0-16 scoreline. In the second half, goals from [[Billy Ryan (hurler)|Billy Ryan]] with a low shot to the corner of the net and [[Martin Keoghan]] with a shot into the left corner form the right twice helped to briefly drag Kilkenny back on level terms, and every one of their subs scored – [[Richie Hogan]] hitting an equaliser in his first appearance of the season. In the end, Limerick won the game 1-31 to 2-26 to claim their fourth title in five years and their first ever three-in-a-row. Captain [[Declan Hannon]] lifted the [[Liam MacCarthy Cup]] alongside the injured [[Cian Lynch]], whose absence with an ankle injury made the achievement all the more impressive.{{cite news|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2022/0717/1310699-all-ireland-hurling-final-build-up-kilkenny-v-limerick/|title=All-Ireland hurling final recap: Limerick 1-31 Kilkenny 2-26|publisher=[[RTÉ Sport]]|first=Peter|last=Branigan|date=17 July 2022|accessdate=17 July 2022}} ===Details=== {{GAAmatchbox |bg = |date = 17 July 2022 |time= 15:30 |round = All-Ireland Final |report = [https://www.the42.ie/limerick-kilkenny-all-ireland-hurling-5819034-Jul2022/ Report] |team1 = [[File:Colours of Kilkenny.svg|border|20px]] [[Kilkenny county hurling team|Kilkenny]] |score1 = 2-26 {{small|(32)}} |score2 = {{small|(34)}} 1-31 |team2 = [[File:Colours of Limerick.svg|border|20px]] [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick]] |HT = 0-16 {{small|(16)}} – {{small|(20)}} 1-17 |goals1 = Martin Keoghan 1, Billy Ryan 1 |points1 = TJ Reid 9 (9f), Martin Keoghan 1, Adrian Mullen 3, Paddy Deegan 2, Padraig Walsh 2, Eoin Cody 1, Tommy Walsh 1, Mikey Carey 1, Richie Reid 1, David Blanchfield 1, Alan Murphy 1, Walter Walsh 1, John Donnelly 1, Richie Hogan 1 |goals2 = Gearoid Hegarty 1 |points2 = Gearoid Hegarty 5, Aaron Gillane 6 (4f), Diarmaid Byrnes 5 (3f, 1 '65), Kyle Hayes 4, Tom Morrissey 4, Séamus Flanagan 2, Declan Hannon 1, Dan Morrissey 1, Conor Boylan 1, Cathal O'Neill 1 |location = [[Dublin]] |venue = [[Croke Park]] |attendance = |referee = Colm Lyons ([[Cork GAA|Cork]]) |TV =[[RTÉ]]
