[[John Kiely (Limerick hurler)|John Kiely]] |} {{col-end}} ===Trophy presentation=== Limerick captain [[Declan Hannon]], alongside [[Cian Lynch]] (who did not play in the final due to an injury),{{cite news|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2022/0715/1310506-cian-lynch-not-included-in-limerick-all-ireland-panel/|title=Cian Lynch not included in Limerick's All-Ireland final panel, Kilkenny unchanged|publisher=[[RTÉ News and Current Affairs]]|date=16 July 2022|accessdate=17 July 2022}} accepted the [[Liam MacCarthy Cup]] from GAA president [[Larry McCarthy (sports administrator)|Larry McCarthy]] in the Hogan Stand.{{cite news|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40920101.html|title=Limerick v Kilkenny liveblog - All-Ireland final play by play|publisher=[[Irish Examiner]]|first=John|last=Fogarty|date=17 July 2022|accessdate=17 July 2022|quote=Declan Hannon has become the first captain to receive the Liam MacCarthy Cup four times. He lifts it with the injured Cian Lynch. }} In doing so, Hannon became the first captain to lift the Liam MacCarthy Cup four times.{{cite web|url=https://hoganstand.com/Article/Index/324283|title=Limerick complete All-Ireland three-in-a-row after sensational final win against Cats|website=[[HoganStand.com]]|date=17 July 2022|accessdate=17 July 2022}} Lynch later revealed that he was not anticipating Hannon asking him to lift the trophy with him.{{cite news|url=https://www.the42.ie/cian-lynch-ankle-injury-2-5820402-Jul2022/|title='You're dealing with grief really, you have to accept it' — Cian Lynch facing three months out with injury|publisher=[[The42.ie]]|first=Kevin|last=O'Brien|date=19 July 2022|accessdate=19 July 2022}} ===Reaction=== Limerick captain [[Declan Hannon]] speaking to RTÉ after the match said "It means everything to us".{{cite tweet|author=RTÉ GAA|user=RTEgaa|title='It means everything to us'. Limerick captain Declan Hannon savours another All-Ireland title following today's victory at Croke Park #RTEGAA. Highlights on @TheSundayGame @RTE2/@RTEplayer from 9.30pm|number=1548722215482531840|date=17 July 2022|accessdate=17 July 2022}} Limerick manager [[John Kiely (Limerick hurler)|John Kiely]] spoke to RTÉ after the match about how much it meant to make history with Limerick and how the panel almost governed itself in setting standards.{{cite tweet|author=The Sunday Game|user=TheSundayGame|number=1548710370658893831|title=John Kiely talks about how much it means to make history with Limerick and how the panel almost governs itself in setting standards. #sundaygame|date=17 July 2022|accessdate=17 July 2022}} [[Kyle Hayes]] dedicated Limerick's third All-Ireland SHC title in a row to [[Cian Lynch]], "the heart and soul of our team". Speaking to RTÉ Sport, Hayes said: "Anyone who knows Ciano personally, he's an absolute gentleman."{{cite news|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2022/0717/1310725-hayes-dedicates-glory-to-limericks-heart-soul/|title=Hayes dedicates glory to Limerick's 'heart and soul'|publisher=[[RTÉ Sport]]|date=17 July 2022|accessdate=17 July 2022}} Kilkenny manager [[Brian Cody]] speaking to RTÉ after the match said "It was close for sure at the end. I think every Kilkenny person should be very, very proud of how the Kilkenny team performed."{{cite news|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2022/0717/1310735-cody-every-kilkenny-person-should-be-proud/|title=Brian Cody: Every Kilkenny person should be proud of how the team performed|publisher=[[RTÉ Sport]]|first=Eoin|last=Ryan|date=17 July 2022|accessdate=17 July 2022}} Highlights of the final were shown on ''The Sunday Game'' programme which aired at 9:30pm that night on [[RTÉ2]] and was presented by [[Des Cahill]] with match analysis from [[Jackie Tyrrell]], [[Brendan Cummins (GAA player)|Brendan Cummins]], [[Donal Óg Cusack]], [[Davy Fitzgerald]], [[Shane Dowling (hurler)|Shane Dowling]] and [[Ursula Jacob]]. On the man of the match award shortlist were [[Gearóid Hegarty]], [[Kyle Hayes]] and [[Diarmaid Byrnes]] with Gearóid Hegarty winning the award which was presented by GAA president Larry McCarthy at the post match Limerick function at the [[Burlington Hotel (Dublin)|Clayton Burlington Hotel]] in Dublin. ===Celebrations=== The Limerick team returned home the day after the final where the homecoming event was held at [[Gaelic Grounds]], with the team arriving around 7pm. Shortly after 5pm, an estimated 40,000 people turned out to see the team and fans lined a route on an open-top bus from Colbert Rail Station where the team arrived through Mallow Street, O'Connell Street, Sarsfield Bridge and out to the Ennis Road to the Gaelic Grounds which was packed by 45,000.{{cite web|url= https://www.the42.ie/limerick-homecoming-5820563-Jul2022/|title=All-Ireland three-in-a-row winners Limerick receive heroes' welcome home|date=19 July 2022|work=The 42|accessdate=19 July 2022}} Entertainment and a concert celebration commenced at 5pm at the Gaelic Grounds in which [[Denise Chaila]], along with MuRli and [[Rusangano Family|God Knows]], performing together as [[Narolane]], led a stellar line-up of music acts including [[Emma Langford]] and Moncrieff.{{cite news|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/video/whats-on/863681/watch-limerick-supporters-gather-at-tus-gaelic-grounds-as-homecoming-celebrations-begin.html|title=WATCH: Limerick supporters gather at TUS Gaelic Grounds as homecoming celebrations begin|publisher=[[Limerick Leader]]|date=18 July 2022|accessdate=18 July 2022}}{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.ie/news/limerick-hails-conquering-heroes-at-homecoming-for-three-in-a-row-all-ireland-hurling-champs-41849179.html|title=Limerick hails conquering heroes at homecoming for three-in-a-row All-Ireland hurling champs|publisher=[[Irish Independent]]|first1=David|last1=Raleigh|first2=Paul|last2=Hyland|date=18 July 2022|accessdate=18 July 2022}}{{cite news|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/ireland/2022/07/18/an-unforgettable-evening-all-ireland-hurling-champions-limerick-arrive-home-to-warmest-of-receptions/|title='An unforgettable evening': All-Ireland hurling champions Limerick arrive home to warmest of receptions|publisher=[[The Irish Times]]|first=David|last=Raleigh|date=18 July 2022|accessdate=18 July 2022}}{{cite news|url=https://www.rte.ie/news/munster/2022/0718/1310977-limerick-team-homecoming/|title=Limerick fans turn out in force to welcome home All-Ireland champions|publisher=[[RTÉ News and Current Affairs]]|first=Cathy|last=Halloran|date=18 July 2022|accessdate=19 July 2022}} Limerick manager Kiely revealed that [[Kyle Hayes]] and [[David Reidy (Limerick hurler)|David Reidy]] were fitness doubts until one hour before the game.{{cite news|url=https://www.hoganstand.com/Article/Index/324313|title=Kiely reveals Limerick had two significant injury concerns days before All-Ireland final|work=[[HoganStand.com]]|date=19 July 2022|accessdate=19 July 2022}} [[Aaron Gillane]] later revealed that rumours circulating about his fitness were partially true after injuring his knee while clearing a soccer ball out of the way of a [[frisbee]].{{cite news|url=https://www.the42.ie/aaron-gillane-frisbee-5832934-Aug2022/|title=Limerick's star forward suffered a minor knee injury before the Kilkenny but his fitness for the game was never in doubt|publisher=[[The42.ie]]|date=4 August 2022}}{{cite news|url=https://hoganstand.com/Article/Index/324511|title=Gillane suffered frisbee injury scare before All-Ireland final|work=Hogan Stand|date=5 August 2022}} ==Matchday programme controversy== The GAA issued an apology after forgetting to include [[Clare county hurling team|Clare]] in the [[matchday programme]]'s "[[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship records and statistics|roll of honour]] section".{{cite news|url=https://www.hoganstand.com/Article/Index/324316|title=GAA issue 2023.text:
{{Short description|none}} {{Use dmy dates|date=November 2022}} {{Use Hiberno-English|date=November 2022}} {{Infobox football match | title = 2023 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final | image = Croke park hogan stand.jpg | image_size = 200 | event = [[2023 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]] | team1 = [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick]] | team1association = [[File:Colours of Limerick.svg|40px]] | team1score = 0–30 | team2 = [[Kilkenny county hurling team|Kilkenny]] | team2association = [[File:Colours of Kilkenny.svg|40px]] | team2score = 2–15 | date = 23 July 2023 | stadium = [[Croke Park]] | city = [[Dublin]] | man_of_the_match1a = [[Peter Casey (hurler)|Peter Casey]]{{cite news|url=https://hoganstand.com/article/index/328610|title=Casey scoops 'Man of the Match' award|work=Hogan Stand|date=24 July 2023}} | referee = John Keenan ([[Wicklow GAA|Wicklow]]) | weather = Cloudy with a moderate to fresh northerly breeze
{{convert|17|°C|°F|abbr=on}}{{cite news|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2023/0720/1395643-all-ireland-hurling-final-all-you-need-to-know/|title=All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final: All you need to know|publisher=[[RTÉ News]]|first=Declan|last=Whooley|date=23 July 2023|accessdate=23 July 2023}} | attendance = 82,300 | previous = [[2022 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2022]] | next = [[2024 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2024]] }} The '''2023 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final''' was a [[hurling]] match played at [[Croke Park]] in [[Dublin]] on 23 July 2023{{Cite news|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/football/2022/0924/1325285-league-finals-retained-as-2023-calendar-takes-shape/|title=League finals retained as 2023 calendar takes shape|date=24 September 2022|via=www.rte.ie}}{{Cite web|url=https://hoganstand.com/Meath/Article/Index/325123|title=Allianz League finals retained while All-Ireland SFC extended by one week - HoganStand|website=hoganstand.com}} between [[Kilkenny county hurling team|Kilkenny]] and [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick]], the culmination of the [[2023 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]]. It was the [[List of All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship finals|136th final]] of that sport's primary competition, the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]]. Reigning title holder Limerick won the game by 0–30 to 2–15 to claim their four-in-a-row and their fifth title in six years.{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/four-in-a-row-glory-for-limerick-as-treaty-take-down-kilkenny-with-devastating-all-ireland-final-blitz/a484829423.html|title=Four in-a-row glory for Limerick as Treaty take down Kilkenny with devastating All-Ireland final blitz|publisher=[[Irish Independent]]|first=Sean|last=McGoldrick|date=23 July 2023|accessdate=23 July 2023}}{{cite news|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2023/0723/1396051-limericks-leaders-rally-to-roar-past-cats/|title=Leaders drive Limerick past Kilkenny to four in a row|publisher=[[RTÉ News]]|first=Eoin|last=Ryan|date=23 July 2023|accessdate=23 July 2023}} The match was televised live on [[RTÉ2]] as part of ''[[The Sunday Game]]'', presented by [[Joanne Cantwell]] from the Croke Park studio with analysis by [[Anthony Daly (hurler)|Anthony Daly]], [[Dónal Óg Cusack]] and [[Liam Sheedy]]. Commentary on the game was provided by [[Marty Morrissey]] alongside [[Michael Duignan (hurler)|Michael Duignan]].{{cite news|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2023/0723/1396005-all-ireland-hurling-final-limerick-v-kilkenny-updates/|title=All-Ireland hurling final recap: Limerick beat Kilkenny to seal four-in-a-row|publisher=[[RTÉ News]]|first=Raf|last=Diallo|date=23 July 2023|accessdate=23 July 2023}} BBC Northern Ireland covered the final for the first time as part of the Championship, previously BBC just covered football and not Hurling. Their coverage was presented by Thomas Niblock with commentary is by Oisin Langan, with pitch-side updates from Sarah Mulkerrins.{{Cite web | title=BBC Two - The Championship, 2023: All-Ireland Hurling Championship, Final: Limerick v Kilkenny | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/m001p4lq | access-date=2026-08-14 | website=www.bbc.co.uk}} The match drew a peak audience of more than 1 million on RTÉ. The TV audience for ''The Sunday Game'' coverage peaked at 1,125,000 by the end of the final, the highest since 2019.{{cite news|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2023/0724/1396233-over-1-million-watch-limericks-four-in-a-row-success/|title=Over 1 million watch Limerick's four-in-a-row success|publisher=[[RTÉ News]]|date=24 July 2023|accessdate=24 July 2023}} ==Background== {{main|Kilkenny–Limerick hurling rivalry}} *[[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick]] were aiming to complete a four-in-a-row, having won the All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championships of [[2020 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2020]], [[2021 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2021]] and [[2022 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2022]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-keep-all-ireland-four-in-a-row-dream-alive-after-semi-final-surge-blows-galway-away/a269872893.html|title=Limerick keep All-Ireland four in-a-row dream alive after semi-final surge blows Galway away|date=8 July 2023|website=Independent.ie}} This had only been done twice before in the championship's history, by [[Cork county hurling team|Cork]] in [[1941 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1941]]–[[1944 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|44]] and [[Kilkenny county hurling team|Kilkenny]] in [[2006 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2006]]–[[2009 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|09]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20275116.html|title=Ring's 1944 goal He previously refereed the [[2016 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|2016 All-Ireland minor final]], the [[2018 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship final|2018 All-Ireland Under-21 final]], the [[2019 Leinster Senior Hurling Championship final|2019 Leinster hurling final]] and the [[2022 Munster Senior Hurling Championship final|2022 Munster hurling final]]. His umpires were Tommy Redmond (Tinahely), Eddie Leonard (St Patrick's), Paul Reville (Turin) and David Clune (Delvin). His linemen were Galway's Liam Gordon and Wexford's James Owens, with Gordon also the standby referee. The sideline official was Shane Hynes from Galway.{{cite web|url= https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/john-keenan-appointed-as-referee-for-all-ireland-hurling-final/a1451886422.html|title= John Keenan appointed as referee for All-Ireland hurling final|date=13 July 2023|work=Irish Independent|accessdate=18 July 2023}} ===Build-up=== Both teams confirmed that they would return home to their respective counties straight after the match and not remain in Dublin overnight. Limerick would return to Fitzgerald's Woodlands House Hotel and Spa in [[Adare]] while Kilkenny would go to the River Court Hotel in Kilkenny. {{cite web|url= https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2023/0718/1395171-no-capital-stay-for-kilkenny-limerick-on-night-of-final/|title= No post-game banquet for Kilkenny or Limerick in the capital after All-Ireland hurling final|date=19 July 2023|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=19 July 2023}} The final was shown on a big screen on [[Pery Square]] in Limerick where an all ticket crowd watched the match.{{cite web|url=https://www.limerick.ie/council/newsroom/news/all-ireland-big-screen-event-in-limerick-city-centre|title=All Ireland Big Screen event in Limerick City Centre|website=[[Limerick.ie]]|date=18 July 2023|accessdate=23 July 2023}} ===Jubilee teams=== The [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] team that won the [[1998 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1998 All-Ireland Final]] was presented to the crowd before the match.{{cite web|url= https://www.gaa.ie/hurling/news/advice-for-supporters-attending-the-all-ireland-shc-final/|title= Advice for supporters attending the All-Ireland SHC Final|date=23 July 2023|work=GAA.ie|accessdate=24 July 2023}} ==Match== ===Summary=== [[Paddy Deegan]] opened the scoring for Kilkenny in the opening minute of the game, a lead which was held for a further five minutes before Limerick could equalise through [[Cian Lynch]], this would be the only time the sides were level until deep into the second half. Limerick would for a brief moment, take the lead of the game when [[Diarmaid Byrnes]] knocked over Limerick's second point of the afternoon. However, Limerick's bright start was negated when, in the 10th minute, [[Eoin Cody]] picked up a loose ball in the Limerick box, and tucked it low into the bottom-right of the Limerick net, giving Kilkenny a two point advantage. By the 14th minute, two of Limerick's half-back line, [[William O'Donoghue]] and [[Diarmaid Byrnes]] received yellow cards for foul play. Kilkenny would go on to dominate much of the first half proceedings, leading by as much as six points by the 27th minute. At the end of the first half, Kilkenny led by three points on a 1-09 to 0-09 scoreline. Limerick started the second half intensely, rejuvenating their hopes of a fourth successive championship, bringing the scores to within a point by the 40th minute. Yet the afternoon was about to take another turn when a piece of individual brilliance saw Deegan scored a goal for Kilkenny, breaking the right side-netting of the Limerick goal. This saw Kilkenny extend their lead to five points in the 42nd minute. Limerick would bravely respond to this turn of events, aggressively seeking possession and scoring five successive points to bring the scores level for only the second time in the contest with 13 minutes remaining in normal time. From this point onwards, Limerick took control of proceedings, taking the lead for the first time since the sixth minute, when [[Darragh O'Donovan]] made it 0-18 to 2-11 in the 58th minute. In total, Limerick outscored Kilkenny 0-21 to 1-06 in the second half, completing a stellar comeback and running out comfortable winners. The game finished Kilkenny 2-15 (21 points), Limerick 0-30 (30 points). This fourth consecutive championship meant Limerick became only the third county, since the competition began in 1887, to win four All-Ireland hurling titles in a row.{{cite news|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41189653.html|title=Magnificent Limerick ignite in second half to make history|publisher=[[Irish Examiner]]|first=John|last=Fogarty|date=23 July 2023|accessdate=23 July 2023}}{{cite news|url=https://www.breakingnews.ie/sport/all-ireland-hurling-final-kilkenny-lead-limerick-by-three-points-at-half-time-1506011.html|title=Limerick come back to beat Kilkenny and win fourth All-Ireland in a row|publisher=[[BreakingNews.ie]]|first=James|last=Cox|date=23 July 2023|accessdate=23 July 2023}}{{cite web|url=https://www.gaa.ie/hurling/news/all-ireland-shc-final-limerick-produce-stunning-second-half-display-to-retain-ti/|title=All-Ireland SHC Final: Limerick produce stunning second half display to retain title|website=[[GAA.ie]]|first=Cian|last=O'Connell|date=23 July 2023|accessdate=23 July 2023}} While David Blanchfield was named on the Kilkenny squad to start at right wing back, he was unable to due to injury. Walter Walsh started in the position instead wearing the number 24 jersey. While starting in the half back line, Walsh operated across the half forward line, with Conor Fogarty dropping back to cover the number 5 position, and John Donnelly occupying the midfield area. [[Dublin]] on 21 July 2024{{Cite web|url=https://www.kilkennypeople.ie/news/kilkenny-sport/1387138/gaa-fixtures-for-2024-as-season-gets-underway.html|title=GAA fixtures for 2024 as season gets underway|first=Kilkenny People|last=Reporter|date=4 January 2024|website=www.kilkennypeople.ie}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.finalwhistle.ie/hurling/gaa-launch-2024-fixture-masterplan/|title=GAA Launch 2024 Fixture Masterplan – Hurling|date=7 December 2023}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/gaa/1365876/when-do-the-2024-all-ireland-hurling-and-hurling-finals-take-place.html|title=When do the 2024 All-Ireland Hurling and Football Finals take place?|date=6 December 2023|website=www.limerickleader.ie}} between [[Clare county hurling team|Clare]] and [[Cork county hurling team|Cork]], the culmination of the [[2024 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]]. It was the [[List of All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship finals|137th final]] of that sport's primary competition, the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]]. Clare won the game after extra-time by 3–29 to 1–34, to claim their fifth All-Ireland title.{{cite news|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2024/0721/1461045-clare-find-extra-gear-to-edge-cork-in-epic-final/|title=Clare find extra gear to edge Cork in historic hurling final epic|publisher=[[RTÉ Sport]]|first=Eoin|last=Ryan|date=21 July 2024|accessdate=21 July 2024}}{{cite web|url= https://www.gaa.ie/article/all-ireland-shc-final-clare-win-epic-encounter|title=All-Ireland SHC Final: Clare win epic encounter|date=21 July 2024|work=GAA.ie|accessdate=22 July 2024}}{{cite web|url= https://munster.gaa.ie/event/2024-all-ireland-senior-hurling-championship-final-clare-v-cork/|title=Clare 3–29 Cork 1–34|date=19 July 2024|work=Munster GAA|accessdate=22 July 2024}} The match was televised nationally on [[RTÉ2]] as part of ''[[The Sunday Game]]'' live programme, presented by [[Joanne Cantwell]] from the Croke Park studio with analysis by [[Anthony Daly (hurler)|Anthony Daly]], [[Dónal Óg Cusack]] and [[Liam Sheedy]]. Commentary on the game was provided by [[Marty Morrissey]] alongside [[Michael Duignan (hurler)|Michael Duignan]].{{cite web|url= https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2024/0721/1461025-all-ireland-shc-final-cork-v-clare-updates/|title=All-Ireland SHC final recap: Clare 3–29 Cork 1–34 (AET)|date=21 July 2024|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=22 July 2024}} The game was also televised on [[BBC Two]] for the first time and internationally on [[GAAGO]].{{cite news|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2024/0718/1460640-all-ireland-shc-final-all-you-need-to-know/|title=All-Ireland SHC final: All You Need to Know|publisher=[[RTÉ Sport]]|first=Niall|last=McCoy|date=19 July 2024|accessdate=21 July 2024}}{{cite web|url= https://www.bbc.com/mediacentre/2024/all-ireland-senior-hurling-final-live-bbc-iplayer-bbc-two|title=All-Ireland Senior Hurling Final live on BBC iPlayer and BBC Two|date=19 July 2024|work=BBC TV|accessdate=22 July 2024}} The BBC covered the final for the 2nd year in a row as part of The Championship presented this year for the first time by Sarah Mulkerrins alongside hurlers Neill McManus and Paul Murphy. Mark Sidebottom provides pitchside updates, with commentary by Thomas Niblock and Jamesie O’Connor. https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/m0021dwc The match was watched by over a million viewers in Ireland, an average of 1,037,000 watched live on RTÉ2, with another 9,000 watching on RTÉ2+1.{{cite web|url= https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2024/0722/1461240-over-1m-viewers-tune-in-for-classic-all-ireland-final/|title=Over 1 million viewers tune in for classic All-Ireland SHC final|date=23 July 2024|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=23 July 2024}} ==Background== {{main|Clare–Cork hurling rivalry}} *{{GG|Clare|hurling}} made their eighth final appearance, and their first since winning in [[2013 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2013]]. They also won in the finals of [[1914 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|1914]], [[1995 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|1995]] and [[1997 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|1997]], and were beaten finalists in [[1889 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|1889]], [[1932 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|1932]] and [[2002 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2002]]. *{{GG|Cork|hurling}} were aiming to win their first title since [[2005 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2005]]; they are the second most successful county in the championship's history, with 30 wins; their current streak of 18 consecutive seasons without an All-Ireland was the longest in their history.{{cite web|url= https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2024/0715/1460017-we-had-enough-steely-rebels-ready-for-final-push/|title='We just had enough' – Steely Rebels ready for final push|date=17 July 2024|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=17 July 2024}} *The two teams had met in the final once before, in [[2013 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2013]], with Clare winning after a [[replay (sport)|replay]].{{cite web|url = http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/clare-bridge-16year-gap-after-shane-odonnell-becomes-hattrick-hero-29617992.html|title=Clare bridge 16-year gap after Shane O'Donnell becomes hat-trick hero|date=28 September 2013|work=Irish Independent|access-date=30 September 2013}} *The fifth final to involve two [[Munster GAA|Munster]] teams, after [[1997 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|1997]] (Clare beat Tipperary), 2013 (Clare beat Cork), [[2020 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2020]] (Limerick beat Waterford) and [[2021 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2021]] (Limerick beat Cork). *This was the fourth final to involve neither the Munster nor the Leinster champions (in 2024, {{GG|Limerick|hurling}} and {{GG|Kilkenny|hurling}}). The previous occasions were: **[[2004 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2004]] (Cork beat Kilkenny; {{GG|Waterford|hurling}} and {{GG|Wexford|hurling}} were provincial champions) **[[2013 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2013]] (Clare beat Cork; {{GG|Dublin|hurling}} and Limerick were provincial champions) **[[2019 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2019]] ({{GG|Tipperary|hurling}} beat Kilkenny; Wexford and Limerick were provincial champions) ==Paths to the final== {{col-begin}} {{col-2}} {| class="wikitable" |+ Clare |- !Round!! He previously refereed the [[2018 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|2018 All-Ireland minor final]], the [[2021 All-Ireland Under-20 Hurling Championship final|2021 All-Ireland Under-20 final]], the [[2021 Leinster Senior Hurling Championship final|2021 Leinster hurling final]] and the All-Ireland senior club final in [[2023 All-Ireland Senior Club Hurling Championship final|2023]]. Galway's Liam Gordon and Tipperary's Michael Kennedy served as linesmen for the final.{{cite web|url= https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2024/0711/1459379-murphy-named-as-referee-for-all-ireland-hurling-final/|title=Limerick's Johnny Murphy confirmed as referee for All-Ireland SHC final|date=11 July 2024|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=17 July 2024}} ===Jubilee teams=== The [[Cork county hurling team|Cork]] team that won the [[1999 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|1999 All-Ireland final]] was presented to the crowd before the match, on the silver jubilee.{{cite web|url= https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41436766.html|title=Silver to gold: the teams who won All-Irelands as county's jubilee teams watched on|date=15 July 2024|work=Irish Examiner|accessdate=17 July 2024}} {{cite web|url= https://www.echolive.ie/corksport/arid-41436238.html|title=Cork manager Pat Ryan at peace with missing jubilee festivities|date=15 July 2024|work=EchoLive|accessdate=17 July 2024}} ===Build-up=== Tickets for the final were sold out with no general sales, over 32,000 tickets had been issued to Cork and Clare for distribution between the clubs. Cork had a total of 219 active GAA clubs, most of any county in Ireland, with 84 clubs in Clare.{{cite web|url= https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41438047.html|title=Online scammers target fans seeking All-Ireland hurling final tickets|date=16 July 2024|work=Irish Examiner|accessdate=17 July 2024}} Stand tickets for the final cost €100 with terrace tickets at €55.{{cite web|url= https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/clare-v-cork-all-ireland-shc-final-what-time-what-channel-and-all-you-need-to-know/a1667855410.html|title=Clare v Cork, All-Ireland SHC final: What time, what channel and all you need to know|date=19 July 2024|work=Irish Independent|accessdate=18 July 2024}} In Cork the match was shown at the Rebels' Fanzone free event at SuperValu [[Páirc Uí Chaoimh]] with 15,000 tickets sold out within 45 minutes.{{cite web|url= https://www.irishexaminer.com/news/munster/arid-41437138.html|title=Tickets for All-Ireland final fanzone at Páirc Uí Chaoimh sell out in 45 minutes|date=16 July 2024|work=Irish Examiner|accessdate=17 July 2024}} [[Clare County Council]] also screened the final on a big screen at a free event in Tim Smythe Park in [[Ennis]].{{cite web|url= https://www.independent.ie/regionals/clare/news/clare-county-council-confirms-free-screening-of-all-ireland-hurling-final-in-ennis/a392468369.html|title=Clare County Council confirms free screening of All-Ireland Hurling Final in Ennis|date=18 July 2024|work=Irish Independent|accessdate=18 July 2024}} ===Team news=== On 18 July, Cork announced the same team for the final that started the semi-final against Limerick. Three players remained from the side that lost the [[2013 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2013]] replay to Clare, with [[Séamus Harnedy]] and [[Patrick Horgan]] starting and [[Conor Lehane]] on the bench.{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2024/0718/1460709-shc-final-teams-cork-stick-with-same-15/ |title=Cork stick with same 15 for Clare showdown|date=18 July 2024|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=18 July 2024}} A day later, Clare also announced the same starting team as against Kilkenny in the semi-final. Four players, [[John Conlon]], [[David McInerney]], [[Tony Kelly (hurler)|Tony Kelly]] and [[Shane O'Donnell]] remained from the side that won the final in 2013. {{cite web|url= https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2024/0719/1460769-clare-unchanged-for-all-ireland-final-with-cork/|title=Clare name unchanged side for All-Ireland final with Cork|date=19 July 2024|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=18 July 2024}} ==Match== ===Summary=== Cork had two points scored in the first minute and added another before Mark Rodgers scored for Clare in the fifth minute. In the 12th minute [[Robert Downey (hurler)|Rob Downey]] won the ball on his own 65 and got away from [[Peter Duggan]] on the left before firing the ball high to the net straight off his hurl to put Cork into a seven point lead. In the 18th minute Shane O’Donnell won the ball out on the left before passing to Peter Duggan and retaining the ball again before passing to Aidan McCarthy who scored with a finish to the right corner of the net past the advancing goalkeeper. The scores were level at half-time on 1–12 each.{{cite web|url= https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/clare-3-29-cork-1-34-as-it-happened-banner-claim-all-ireland-shc-title-after-epic-battle-at-croke-park/a1019013067.html|title=Clare 3–29 Cork 1–34 as it happened: Banner claim All-Ireland SHC title after epic battle at Croke Park|date=21 July 2024|work=Irish Independent|accessdate=1 August 2024}} Clare got a second goal in the 40th minute when [[Mark Rodgers]] picked up a breaking ball before stepping inside Mark Coleman from the right and scoring with a low finish to the net. In the 52nd minute, Tony Kelly ran in on goal from the left before flicking the ball over [[Seán O'Donoghue]]’s head, touched it on the Hurley before flicking it past Patrick Collins into the right corner of the net to put Clare into a 3–15 to 1–18 lead. Clare were still leading by three with two minutes to go before Cork came back with [[Patrick Horgan]] sending the match to extra-time by scoring a free in the 76th minute.{{cite web|url= https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/2024/07/21/cork-v-clare-live-updates-all-ireland-hurling-final/|title=FT Clare 3–29 Cork 1–34 at it happened: Clare win All-Ireland hurling final|date=21 '''Manager:''' |- |colspan="4"|[[Pat Ryan (Cork hurler)|Pat Ryan]] |} {{col-end}} ===Trophy presentation=== Clare captain [[Tony Kelly (hurler)|Tony Kelly]] accepted the [[Liam MacCarthy Cup]] from GAA president [[Jarlath Burns]] in the Hogan Stand and the team then did a victory lap around Croke Park with the trophy.{{cite web|url= https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2024/0721/1461050-clares-all-ireland-winners-bask-in-greatest-day/|title=Clare's All-Ireland winners bask in 'greatest day' at Croke Park|date=21 July 2024|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=22 July 2024}}{{cite web|url= https://www.irishmirror.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/full-tony-kelly-speech-clare-33292167|title=Full Tony Kelly speech as Clare win All-Ireland Hurling Championship|date=21 July 2024|work=Irish Mirror|accessdate=22 July 2024}}{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/in-clare-hurling-is-like-a-religion-and-brian-lohan-is-like-our-god-the-gospel-according-to-tony-kelly/a1596983355.html |title=‘In Clare, hurling is like a religion and Brian Lohan is like our God’ – the gospel according to Tony Kelly|date=21 July 2024|work=Irish Independent|accessdate=22 July 2024}} ===Reaction=== Highlights of the final were shown on ''The Sunday Game'' programme which aired at 9:30pm that night on RTÉ2 and was presented by [[Jacqui Hurley]] with match analysis from [[Brendan Cummins (GAA player)|Brendan Cummins]], [[Jackie Tyrell]], [[Ursula Jacob]], [[Joe Canning]], [[Shane Dowling (hurler)|Shane Dowling]], and [[Anthony Daly (hurler)|Anthony Daly]]. On the man of the match award shortlist were [[Tony Kelly (hurler)|Tony Kelly]], [[Conor Leen]] and [[Robert Downey (hurler)|Rob Downey]] with Tony Kelly winning the award which was presented by GAA president Jarlath Burns at the post match Clare function at the Inter-Continental Hotel in Dublin.{{cite web|url= https://hoganstand.com/Article/Index/332864|title=Tony Kelly named All-Ireland SHC final Man of the Match|date=21 July 2024|work=Hogan Stand|accessdate=22 July 2024}} ''[[The Observer]]'''s architecture critic [[Rowan Moore]] wrote in praise of hurling, though also suggested it was "unexportable" and, were this not so, then it would be "a global sport".{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/article/2024/aug/10/hurling-could-be-a-global-phenomenon-if-it-werent-such-an-unexportable-sport|title=Hurling could be a global phenomenon if it weren't such an unexportable sport|date=10 August 2024|work=The Observer|first=Rowan|last=Moore|authorlink=Rowan Moore|access-date=10 August 2024}} ===Homecoming=== The Clare team arrived back in [[Ennis]] at 9pm on the day after the game on an open top bus. There was a reception held at Tim Smyth Park in Ennis with an attendance of over 35,000 people. They had previously visited [[Wolfe Tones na Sionna GAA|Wolfe Tones GAA]] club grounds in [[Shannon, County Clare|Shannon]], before going thru [[Clarecastle]] on the way to Ennis.{{cite web|url= https://www.clare.fm/news/35000-fans-welcome-heroes-2024-clare-ireland-homecoming/|title=Over 35,000 Fans Welcome Heroes Of 2024 At Clare All-Ireland Homecoming|date=23 July 2024|work=Clare FM|accessdate=23 July 2024}} The players and manager were introduced on stage by RTÉ's [[Marty Morrissey]]. {{cite web|url= https://www.rte.ie/news/regional/2024/0722/1461140-clare-hurling-homecoming/|title=Ennis homecoming to be held for triumphant Clare hurlers|date=22 July 2024|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=22 July 2024}}{{cite web|url= https://www.clareecho.ie/homecoming-celebration-in-ennis-for-clares-hurling-heroes/|title=Homecoming celebration in Ennis this evening |date=22 July 2024|work=Clare Echo|accessdate=22 July 2024}}{{cite web|url= https://www.rte.ie/news/regional/2024/0722/1461140-clare-hurling-homecoming/|title=Over 30,000 hail triumphant Clare hurlers at homecoming|date=23 July 2024|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=23 July 2024}} ==References== {{Reflist}} {{GAA 2024}} {{Hurling All-Irelands}} [[Category:2024 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1]] [[Category:All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship finals]] [[Category:GAA finals at Croke Park]] [[Category:July 2024 sports events in Ireland|Hurling]] [[Category:2020s in Dublin (city)]] [[Category:Clare county hurling team matches]] [[Category:Cork county hurling team matches]] [[Category:2024 in Irish sport]]

{{small|(21)}} | details = | date = {{start date|2025|7|20|df=y}} | stadium = [[Croke Park]] | city = [[Dublin]] | man_of_the_match1a = [[Ronan Maher (hurler)|Ronan Maher]]{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/ronan-maher-man-of-the-match-6768678-Jul2025/|title=Ronan Maher lands All-Ireland hurling final man of the match award|website=www.the42.ie|first=Emma|last=Duffy|date=20 July 2025|accessdate=21 July 2025}} | referee = Liam Gordon (Galway) | weather = {{cvt|20|C}}, windy{{cite web|url=https://world-weather.info/forecast/ireland/dublin/20-july/|title=Weather in Dublin, 20 July 2025|date=21 July 2025|work=World Weather Info|accessdate=22 July 2025}} | previous = [[2024 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2024]] | next = [[2026 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2026]] }} The '''2025 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final''' was a [[hurling]] match played at [[Croke Park]] in [[Dublin]] on 20 July 2025{{Cite web|url=https://www.tippmidwestradio.com/2025/03/27/2025-county-club-championships-to-be-drawn-this-evening/|title=2025 County Club Championships To Be Drawn This Evening|first=Tipp Mid West|last=Radio|date=27 March 2025}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/hurling/1673818/limerick-s-2025-allianz-hurling-and-football-league-fixture-details-revealed.html|title=Limerick's 2025 Allianz Hurling and Football League fixture details revealed|first=Colm |last=Kinsella|date=5 December 2024|website=www.limerickleader.ie}} between [[Cork county hurling team|Cork]] and [[Tipperary county hurling team|Tipperary]], the culmination of the [[2025 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]]. It was the [[List of All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship finals|138th final]] of that sport's primary competition, the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]]. Cork were strong favourites and led by six points at half time.{{Cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/transformed-tipperary-crowned-all-ireland-champions-after-stunning-second-half-comeback-against-cork/a2013734460.html|title=Transformed Tipperary crowned All-Ireland champions after stunning second-half comeback against Cork|date=20 July 2025|website=www.independent.ie}} However, they collapsed in the second half, with Tipperary outscoring them 3–14 to 0–2 to win by fifteen.{{Cite web|url=https://www.gaa.ie/article/all-ireland-shc-final-glory-for-tipperary|title=All-Ireland SHC Final: Glory for Tipperary|date=20 July 2025|website=www.gaa.ie}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/2025/07/21/the-anatomy-of-a-collapse-how-cork-managed-to-lose-the-second-half-by-3-14-to-0-2/|title=The anatomy of a collapse – how Cork managed to lose the second half by 3–14 to 0–2|website=The Irish Times}} The match was televised nationally on [[RTÉ2]] as part of ''[[The Sunday Game]]'' live programme, presented by [[Joanne Cantwell]] from the Croke Park studio with analysis by [[Anthony Daly (hurler)|Anthony Daly]], [[Dónal Óg Cusack]] and [[Liam Sheedy]]. Commentary on the game was provided by [[Marty Morrissey]] alongside [[Michael Duignan (hurler)|Michael Duignan]].{{cite web|url=https://www.hoganstand.com/Article/Index/337170|title=Duignan commentates on his 25th All-Ireland hurling final|date=21 July 2025|work=Hogan Stand|accessdate=22 July 2025}} {{cite web|url=https://www.irishmirror.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/hurling-news/who-rte-commentary-duty-sundays-35565586|title=Who will be on RTE commentary duty for Sunday's Cork-Tipperary All-Ireland hurling final?|date=16 July 2025|work=Irish Mirror|accessdate=18 July 2025}} The game was also televised on [[BBC Two Northern Ireland]], presented by [[Sarah Mulkerrins]] who hosted the Hurling final for the 2nd year in a row, punditry came from Neil McManus,All-Ireland winners Shane O'Donnell, Paul Murphy and Séamus Flanagan. Commentary is by Thomas Niblock, Jamesie O’Connor and Sean Flanagan with pitch-side updates from Mark Sidebottom, Séamus Callanan and Diarmuid O'Sullivan. https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/m002g6cv The match drew an average TV audience of 980,000 viewers on RTÉ2 and peaked at 1,119,000 towards the end of the game.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishmirror.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/tipperary-ireland-triumph-over-cork-35592748?int_source=nba|title=Tipperary All-Ireland triumph over Cork breaks RTE online record and reaches huge TV audience|date=21 July 2025|work=Irish Mirror|accessdate=22 July 2025}}{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/irish-news/tipperarys-stunning-all-ireland-final-display-was-viewed-by-over-one-million-people/a1353212936.html|title=Tipperary’s stunning All-Ireland Final display was viewed by over one million people|date=21 July 2025|work=Irish Independent|accessdate=22 July 2025}} ==Background== {{Main|Cork–Tipperary hurling rivalry}} *{{GG|Cork|hurling}} were aiming to win their first title since [[2005 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2005]]; they are the second most successful county in the championship's history, with [[Cork GAA honours|30 wins]]; their current streak of 19 consecutive seasons without an All-Ireland was the longest in their history.https://www.msn.com/en-us/sports/soccer/cork-v-dublin-live-updates-from-croke-park-as-rebels-fight-dubs-for-a-place-in-the-all-ireland-senior-hurling-championship-final/{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2025/0720/1523756-cork-can-shoulder-great-expectations-in-novel-final/|title=Preview: Cork can shoulder great expectations in novel All-Ireland hurling final against Tipperary|date=20 July 2025|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=22 July 2025}} *{{GG|Tipperary|hurling}} won their first title since [[2019 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2019]] and their [[Tipperary GAA honours|29th title]] in total.{{cite web | title=Tipperary manager Liam Cahill has 'no complaints at all' with red card during epic Croke Park battle with Kilkenny | url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/tipperary-book-place-in-all-ireland-final-against-cork-after-epic-croke-park-battle-with-kilkenny/a1753864375.html }} *First meeting of Cork and Tipperary in the [[List of All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship finals|final]]. Such a meeting was only possible since [[1997 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1997]], as prior to that only one Munster county could reach the final. However, both counties had been in 8 finals each since then, but never in the same year.{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2025/0706/1522075-supersub-odonoghue-fires-14-man-tipperary-into-final/|title=Super sub Oisin O'Donoghue fires 14-man Tipperary past Kilkenny and into All-Ireland final|date=7 July 2025|work=RTÉ Sport|accessdate=9 July 2025}}{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2025/0717/1524081-all-ireland-hurling-final-all-you-need-to-know/|title=All-Ireland hurling final: All you need to know|date=18 July 2025|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=18 July 2025}} *The sixth final to involve two [[Munster GAA|Munster]] teams, after [[1997 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|1997]] (Clare beat Tipperary), [[2013 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2013]] (Clare beat Cork), [[2020 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2020]] (Limerick beat Waterford), [[2021 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2021]] (Limerick beat Cork), [[2024 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2024]] (Clare beat Cork). ==Paths to the final== {{col-begin}} {{col-2}} {| class="wikitable" |+ Cork |- !Round!! {{GG|Kilkenny|hurling}} || [[Croke Park]] (N) || align="center"| Win ||align="center"| 2 || align="center"|4–20 to 0–30 || {{Cite news|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/2025/07/06/kilkenny-v-tipperary-live-updates-all-ireland-hurling-semi-final/|title=Kilkenny 0–30 Tipperary 4–20 FT: Superb Oisín O'Donoghue goal wins it for Tipp – As it happened|newspaper=The Irish Times}} |} {{col-end}} ==Pre-match== ===Transport=== By 10 June, shortly after [[Cork county hurling team|Cork]] and [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick]] had contested the [[2025 Munster Senior Hurling Championship final]], it was reported that the [[Iarnród Éireann]] website had announced all tickets on its morning trains to Dublin from [[Cork Kent railway station]] and [[Limerick Colbert railway station]] for 20 July had sold out.{{cite news|url=https://hoganstand.com/article/index/336673|title=Cork and Limerick trains sold out for All-Ireland final day|work=Hogan Stand|date=10 June 2025}} However, instead it was [[Tipperary county hurling team|Tipperary]] who met Cork in the final. There was criticism (including from Cork-based TDs [[Colm Burke]] and [[Thomas Gould (politician)|Thomas Gould]]) of motorway toll barriers delaying supporters as they travelled to the semi-finals, and requests to have the barriers removed on the day of the final. This was rejected by [[Transport Infrastructure Ireland]] (TII).{{cite news|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/news/munster/arid-41665790.html|title=Motorway toll barriers will not be lifted for fans driving to All-Ireland hurling final|work=Irish Examiner|first=Eoin|last=English|date=8 July 2025}} ===Tickets=== Tickets for the match were distributed by the clubs with no public sale and priced at €100 for the stands and €55 for the terrace.{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/brainstorm/2025/0707/1518663-gaa-croke-park-all-ireland-final-ticket-allocations-hurling-football/|title=How do you get your hands on All Ireland final tickets?|date=14 July 2025|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=15 July 2025}} ===Officials=== On 8 July, the GAA named [[Galway GAA|Galway]]'s Liam Gordon of Killimor as the referee for the final, his first All-Ireland SHC decider. He previously refereed the [[2019 All-Ireland Under-20 Hurling Championship final]], and the [[2023 Munster Senior Hurling Championship final]]. Sean Stack and Thomas Walsh were named to assist, Stack filling the role of stand-by referee.{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2025/0708/1522519-gordon-appointed-as-all-ireland-hurling-final-ref/|title=Liam Gordon appointed as All-Ireland hurling final ref|date=8 July 2025|work=RTÉ Sport|accessdate=9 July 2025}} ===Jubilee teams=== The [[Kilkenny county hurling team|Kilkenny]] team that won the [[2000 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2000 All-Ireland SHC final]] was presented to the crowd before the match, on the [[silver jubilee]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41669252.html|title=Brian Cody set to miss jubilee celebration of his first All-Ireland win as manager|date=14 July 2025|work=Irish Examiner|accessdate=15 July 2025}} Absent from the presentation was [[D. J. Carey]], [[man of the match]] in the 2000 final but recently disgraced after pleading guilty to defrauding a number of people out of money while falsely claiming to have [[cancer]]. His name was announced to audible [[booing|boos]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/irish-news/disgraced-hurler-dj-carey-absent-as-kilkennys-jubilee-team-are-honoured-on-all-ireland-final-day/a695403691.html|title=Disgraced hurler DJ Carey absent as Kilkenny's Jubilee team are honoured on All-Ireland final day|date=20 July 2025|website=Irish Independent}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.theweb.ie/dj-carey-absent-croke-park-6768527-Jul2025/|title=DJ Carey conspicuously absent from Kilkenny jubilee celebration|first=Press|last=Association|date=20 July 2025|website=TheJournal.ie}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/news/arid-41673197.html|title=DJ Carey misses Kilkenny jubilee team celebration at Croke Park|first=Cillian|last=Sherlock|date=20 July 2025|website=Irish Examiner}} ===Team news=== On 17 July the Cork team was named with no changes to the starting line-up from the semi-final win over [[Dublin GAA|Dublin]]. [[Séamus Harnedy]] returned to the panel after missing the semi-final with a hamstring injury.{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2025/0717/1524078-harnedy-returns-to-squad-as-cork-named-unchanged-team/|title=Seamus Harnedy returns to squad as Cork name unchanged team|date=17 July 2025|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=18 July 2025}} On 18 July the Tipperary team was named, also with no changes to the starting line-up from the semi-final win over [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]]. There was one change to the panel with Under-20's forward [[Paddy McCormack (Tipperary hurler)|Paddy McCormack]] replacing [[Seán Kenneally]].{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2025/0718/1524136-tipperary-team-to-play-cork-in-all-ireland-final-2025/|title=Tipperary named unchanged team for All-Ireland final against Cork|date=18 July 2025|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=18 July 2025}} ==Match== ===Summary=== ==== First Half ==== The match was played in dry conditions with a slight breeze into the canal end in front of a sell-out crowd of 82,331. Cork playing with the light breeze in the first half opened the scoring with a point from [[Diarmuid Healy]]. [[Bryan O'Mara]] was playing as an extra man sweeper for Tipperary in the full back line with [[Willie Connors]] dropping in at wing-back and [[Sam O'Farrell]] also moving into midfield.{{cite web|url=https://www.balls.ie/gaa/when-they-said-it-we-were-looking-around-saying-what-is-this-about-tipperary-sweeper-hero-636442|title=Tipperary Sweeper Admits Team Were Baffled By Cahill's Tactical Switch|date=21 July 2025|work=Balls.ie|accessdate=24 July 2025}}{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41673392.html|title=From day one this season, Bevans saw something 'different' about Tipperary|date=20 July 2025|work=Irish Examiner|accessdate=24 July 2025}} After 12 minutes, Cork had a 0–4 to 0–3 lead with five wides from Tipperary. In the 20th minute, [[Eoghan Connolly]] found himself out on the left and went for goal with a low effort thar was just wide to the right at the hill 16 end. In the 34th minute, [[Jason Forde]] scored a goal with a flick to the net after a high ball into the square from Eoghan Connolly which was disallowed when the referee called a square ball. In the 2nd of the two minutes of added time, [[Shane Barrett]] scored a goal for Cork after running in from the left before shooting low to the right corner to put Cork into a six-point lead at half time on a 1–16 to 0–13 scoreline.{{cite web|url=https://www.gaa.ie/article/all-ireland-shc-final-glory-for-tipperary|title=All-Ireland SHC Final: Glory for Tipperary|date=21 July 2025|work=GAA.ie|accessdate=23 July 2025}} ==== Second Half ==== In the first minute [[Patrick Horgan]] sent a free wide for Cork at the hill 16 end. A minute later [[Andrew Ormond]] scored a point and got another point in the 41st minute to narrow the gap to four. [[Darragh McCarthy]] then added another point and a free to put one point between the sides. In the 45th minute, Tipperary scored a goal, Cork goalkeeper [[Patrick Collins (hurler)|Patrick Collins]] batted out a high ball which was picked up by [[John McGrath (Tipperary hurler)|John McGrath]] before he slotted into the net to put Tipperary into a two-point lead.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41673179.html|title=A second half for the ages as Tipperary blow Cork away to secure 29th All-Ireland hurling title|date=21 July 2025|work=Irish Examiner|accessdate=23 July 2025}} In the 53rd minute, Tipperary are awarded a penalty when John McGrath was pulled down by [[Eoin Downey]] who was already on a yellow and received a red card. Darragh McCarthy took the penalty and scored with a powerful shot to the left to put seven points between the sides. In the 60th minute Tipperary got a third goal and a second for John McGrath when he flicked the ball right handed to the net past the advancing goalkeeper after a high ball into the square from Eoghan Connolly, putting twelve points between the sides.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishmirror.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/cork-v-tipperary-live-score-35586265|title=Cork v Tipperary score recap and result from the All-Ireland hurling final at Croke Park|date=21 July 2025|work=Irish Mirror|accessdate=23 July 2025}} In the 69th minute, Tipperary goalkeeper [[Rhys Shelly]] scored a point from play to increase the lead to thirteen points, it was the first ever point scored by a goalkeeper from open play in an All-Ireland final.{{cite web|url=https://www.balls.ie/gaa/tipperary-rhys-shelly-all-ireland-final-636513#:~:text=Shelly%20played%20a%20big%20role,an%20All%2DIreland%20hurling%20final.|title=Tipperary 'Keeper And Andrea Pirlo Had Same Preparation For Match Of Their Lives|date=20 July 2025|work=Ball.ie|accessdate=24 July 2025}} In added time Cork were awarded a penalty when [[Brian Hayes (dual player)|Brian Hayes]] was fouled, Rhys Shelley dived to his right to save the penalty from [[Conor Lehane]]. Darragh McCarthy then scored from a free before passing to [[Noel McGrath (hurler)|Noel McGrath]] to get the final point of the game with Tipperary winning by 3–27 to 1-18.{{cite web|url=https://www.gaa.ie/article/noel-mcgrath-loving-life-and-hurling|title=Noel McGrath loving life and hurling|date=22 July 2025|work=GAA.ie|accessdate=24 July 2025}} They won the second half by 21 points with Cork only scoring two points.{{cite web|url=https://www.echolive.ie/corksport/arid-41673188.html|title=All-Ireland SHC final: Tipperary take the title as Cork flounder in second '''Manager:''' |- |colspan="4"|[[Liam Cahill]] |} {{col-end}} ===Trophy presentation=== Tipperay captain [[Ronan Maher (hurler)|Ronan Maher]] accepted the [[Liam MacCarthy Cup]] from GAA president [[Jarlath Burns]] in the Hogan Stand and the team then did a victory lap around Croke Park with the trophy.{{cite web|url=https://hoganstand.com/Tipperary/Article/Index/337165|title=Ronan Maher pays hearfelt tribute to Dillon Quirke|date=20 July 2025|work=Hogan Stand|accessdate=21 July 2025}} In his speech, Maher paid tribute to former team mate [[Dillon Quirke]], who died in 2022.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishmirror.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/emotional-scenes-tipperary-captain-pays-35587230|title=Emotional scenes as Tipperary captain pays tribute to the late Dillon Quirke after All-Ireland win|date=20 July 2025|work=Irish Mirror|accessdate=21 July 2025}} ===Reaction=== Tipperary manager [[Liam Cahill]] never doubted his players saying "The honesty of that group of players – I never doubted them. I know we were all a little bit sensitive after last year with what happened, and some of the criticism was probably deserved at times, but I knew the quality of these men".{{cite web|url=https://www.hoganstand.com/Article/Index/337166|title=Cahill always believed in Tipp players|date=21 July 2025|work=Hogan Stand|accessdate=22 July 2025}}{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2025/0720/1524417-cahill-praises-the-honesty-and-character-of-tipp-team/|title='I never doubted them' - Liam Cahill praises the honesty and character of All-Ireland-winning Tipperary team|date=21 July 2025|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=22 July 2025}} Cork manager [[Pat Ryan (Cork hurler)|Pat Ryan]] speaking after the game felt that Tipperary deserved the win saying "Look, credit to Tipperary. They came out and worked really, really hard. We were in a good position at half-time, but we got blown away in the second half.”{{cite web|url=https://www.hoganstand.com/County/National/Article/Index/337173|title=Our energy was terrible in the second half'|date=21 July 2025|work=Hogan Stand|accessdate=22 July 2025}}{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2025/0720/1524419-cork-energy-and-effort-lacking-in-second-half-ryan/|title=Cork energy and effort lacking in second half - Pat Ryan|date=21 July 2025|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=22 July 2025}} Highlights of the final were shown on ''The Sunday Game'' programme which aired at 9:30pm that night on RTÉ2 and was presented by [[Jacqui Hurley]] with match analysis from [[Jackie Tyrrell]], [[Brendan Cummins (GAA player)|Brendan Cummins]], [[Dónal Óg Cusack]], [[Joe Canning]], [[Henry Shefflin]], and [[Ursula Jacob]]. On the man of the match award shortlist were captain [[Ronan Maher (hurler)|Ronan Maher]], [[John McGrath (Tipperary hurler)|John McGrath]] and [[Darragh McCarthy]] with Ronan Maher winning the award which was presented by GAA president Jarlath Burns at the post match Tipperary function at the Grand Hotel in Malahide in Dublin. ===Homecoming=== Members of the Tipperary team and management visited [[Children's Health Ireland at Crumlin|Crumlin Children's Hospital]] on the morning after the game and also stopped off at the Palace Bar in Dublin before arriving back in [[Thurles]] at a reception at [[Semple Stadium]].{{cite web|url=https://www.tipperarylive.ie/news/all-ireland-final/1854071/in-pictures-see-the-tipperary-hurlers-bring-smiles-to-kids-in-crumlin-children-s-hospital.html|title=IN PICTURES: See the Tipperary hurlers bring smiles to kids in Crumlin Children's Hospital!|date=21 July 2025|work=Tipperary Live|accessdate=22 July 2025}}{{cite web|url=https://www.tipperarylive.ie/video/all-ireland-final/1854318/watch-inspiring-scenes-as-tipperary-s-hurling-heroes-arrive-back-in-semple-stadium-on-monday.html|title=Tipperary's hurling heroes arrive back in Semple Stadium on Monday|date=21 July 2025|work=Tipperary Live|accessdate=22 July 2025}} A temporary stage was set up along the side-line of the new stand for the event with the crowd on the pitch. The team arrived at 8:15pm with approximately 45,000 in attendance to greet them on stage in Thurles. The Tipperary senior back-room team were introduced before all the players and captain Ronan Maher and manager Liam Cahill. Entertainment was provided by Seskin Lane, Callini Lua, Acquiesce, [[Una Healy]], and [[The 2 Johnnies]]. In Cork it was agreed by the county board, not by the players, that there would be no homecoming event held.{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2025/0721/1524528-cork-opt-against-homecoming-after-all-ireland-loss/|title=Cork opt against homecoming after All-Ireland final loss|date=21 July 2025|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=22 July 2025}}{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2026/1008/1594652-horgan-slams-cork-county-board-over-ryan-departure/|title= Patrick Horgan unhappy with Cork county board's handling of Pat Ryan's departure as manager|date=9 October 2026|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=20 October 2026}} {{cite web|url=https://www.irishmirror.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/hurling-news/tipperary-homecoming-details-liam-cahills-35589575|title=Tipperary homecoming details as Liam Cahill's men set to return to Premier County|date=20 July 2025|work=Irish Mirror|accessdate=21 July 2025}}{{cite web|url=https://tipperary.gaa.ie/tipperary-senior-all-ireland-hurling-winning-team-homecoming/|title=Tipperary Senior All Ireland Hurling Winning Team Homecoming|date=20 July 2025|work=Tipperary GAA|accessdate=21 July 2025}}{{cite web|url=https://www.tipperarylive.ie/news/all-ireland-final/1853808/revealed-everything-you-need-to-know-about-tipp-homecoming-in-thurles-tonight.html|title=REVEALED: Everything you need to know about Tipp Homecoming in Thurles tonight|date=20 July 2025|work=Tipperary Live|accessdate=21 July 2025}}{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/news/ireland/2025/0721/1524501-tipperary-homecoming/|title='Stuff of dreams' as Tipp squad greeted by 45,000 fans in Thurles|date=21 July 2025|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=22 July 2025}} ===Miscellaneous=== [[Darragh McCarthy]] scoring 1-13(1 pen, 9f 4pts) 93.33% efficiency, was the 4th top scorer in an All Ireland final history. Behind [[Mick 'Gah' Ahern]], [[Nicky English]] & [[Eddie Keher]]. The 20 year old registered 1 wide from 15 shots taken at goal.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/2025/07/20/tipperary-player-ratings-darragh-mccarthy-shines-on-famous-day-at-croke-park/|title=Tipperary player ratings Darragh McCarthy shines on famous day at croke park|date=20 July 2025 |access-date=23 July 2025|publisher=Irish Times |author=|first=Ian|last=O'Riordan}} [[Noel McGrath (hurler)|Noel McGrath]] pocketed his fourth all Ireland medal, first Tipp hurler to do so in 54 years. [[Jason Forde]] had a contentious goal ruled out for a square just before half time, as he beat [[Patrick Collins (hurler)|Patrick Collins]] to a long range delivery before half time, flicking the ball to the net. [[Eoin Downey]] became at the least the 9th player to be red carded in an All Ireland Senior hurling final, after he received second yellow for fouling [[John McGrath (Tipperary hurler)|John McGrath]] in the penalty box, in the 53rd minute. ==References== {{Reflist}} {{GAA 2025}} {{Hurling All-Irelands}} [[Category:2025 in hurling|1]] [[Category:2025 in Irish sport]] [[Category:All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship finals]] [[Category:July 2025 sports events in Ireland|Hurling]]

{{small|(21)}} | details = | date = {{start date|2026|7|19|df=y}} | stadium = [[Croke Park]] | city = [[Dublin]] | man_of_the_match1a = [[Cathal O'Neill]]{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/cathal-oneill-limerick-man-of-the-match-7107664-Jul2026/|title=Cathal O'Neill's brilliant 1-4 earns him All-Ireland final Man of the Match award|first=Niall|last=Kelly|website=www.the42.ie|date=20 July 2026|accessdate=20 July 2026}} | referee = Colm Lyons (Cork) | weather = {{cvt|21|C}}, sunny{{Cite web |date=19 July 2026 |title=Weather in Dublin, 19 July 2026 |url=https://world-weather.info/forecast/ireland/dublin/19-july/ |access-date=20 July 2026 |website=World Weather Info}} | previous = [[2025 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2025]] | next = [[2027 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2027]] }} The '''2026 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final''' was a [[hurling]] match played at [[Croke Park]] in [[Dublin]] on 19 July 2026 between [[Galway county hurling team|Galway]] and [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick]],{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2026/0704/1581739-galway-devour-shell-shocked-cork-to-reach-decider/|title= Galway devour shell-shocked Cork to reach decider|date=4 July 2026|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=6 July 2026}}{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2026/0705/1581834-oconnor-goal-sees-limerick-snatch-victory-at-the-death/|title= Aidan O'Connor goal sees Limerick snatch victory at the death|date=5 July 2026|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=6 July 2026}} the culmination of the [[2026 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]]. It was the [[List of All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship finals|139th final]] of that sport's primary competition, the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]]. Limerick won the match on a scoreline of 1–29 to 1–18, it was their sixth All-Ireland title since 2018.{{cite web|url= https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2026/0719/1584049-limerick-regain-crown-with-emphatic-demolition-of-galway/|title=Limerick regain hurling crown with emphatic demolition of Galway|date=19 July 2026|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=24 July 2026}}{{cite web|url= https://www.limerickleader.ie/sport/gaa/all-ireland-final/irresistible-limerick-regain-all-ireland-title-with-stunning-win-over-galway-8809558|title=Irresistible Limerick regain All-Ireland title with stunning win over Galway|date=19 July 2026|work=Limerick Leader|accessdate=24 July 2026}}{{cite web|url= https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/2026/07/19/galway-v-limerick-live-all-ireland-hurling-final-updates-western-forces-clash-at-croke-park/|title=All-Ireland hurling final: Limerick beat Galway by 11 points – as it happened|date=19 July 2026|work=Irish Times|accessdate=24 July 2026}} The match was televised nationally on [[RTÉ2]] as part of ''[[The Sunday Game]]'' live programme, presented by [[Joanne Cantwell]] from the Croke Park pitch with analysis by [[Joe Canning]], [[Dónal Óg Cusack]] and [[Liam Sheedy]]. Commentary on the game was provided by [[Marty Morrissey]] alongside [[Michael Duignan (hurler)|Michael Duignan]]. The game was also televised on [[BBC Two]], and streamed on [[iPlayer]] and [[GAA+]].{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2026/0714/1583304-all-ireland-hurling-final-all-you-need-to-know/|title= All-Ireland hurling final: All you need to know|date=16 July 2026|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=16 July 2026}} {{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/articles/cgl3rww488lo|title= Galway must make 'a good start' against Limerick|date=16 July 2026|work=BBC Sport|accessdate=16 July 2026}}{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/mediacentre/2026/live-coverage-gaa-all-ireland-finals|title= Live coverage across the BBC of the GAA All-Ireland Senior Hurling and Football Championship finals|date=16 July 2026|work=BBC|accessdate=16 July 2026}} ==Background== {{Main|Galway–Limerick hurling rivalry}} *{{GG|Limerick|hurling}} were aiming to win their 13th All-Ireland title, and their first since [[2023 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2023]]; they had been the dominant team in hurling in recent years, with All-Irelands in 2018, 2020, 2021, 2022 and 2023 and [[National Hurling League]] wins in 2019, 2020, 2023 and 2026.{{Cite web|url=https://www.limerick.ie/council/newsroom/news/limericks-historic-links-with-the-gaa|title=Limerick's historic links with the GAA|date=20 July 2023|website=www.limerick.ie}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2026/0317/1563852-allianz-hurling-league-r7-all-you-need-to-know/|title=Allianz Hurling League R7: All You Need to Know|first=Conor|last=Neville|date=17 March 2026|via=www.rte.ie}} *{{GG|Galway|hurling}} were aiming to win their 6th All-Ireland title and their first since [[2017 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2017]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.galwaygaa.ie/history/all-ireland-winning-teams/|title=All Ireland Winning Teams – Galway GAA}}{{cite web|url= https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2026/0717/1583905-all-ireland-final-a-crown-jewel-amongst-sporting-riches/|title=All-Ireland SHC final a crown jewel amongst sporting riches|date=18 July 2026|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=24 July 2026}} *The fourth meeting of Galway and Limerick in the [[List of All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship finals|final]]. Limerick won in the [[2018 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2018 final]], while Galway were the winners when the two counties met in [[1923 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|1923]] and [[1980 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|1980]].{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2018/0815/985359-from-1973-to-now-limericks-long-wait-for-glory/ |title =From 1973 to now: Limerick's long wait for glory|date=18 August 2018|work=RTE Sport|access-date=21 August 2018}} ==Paths to the final== {{col-begin}} {{col-2}} {| class="wikitable" |+ Galway |- !Round!! border-top:3px solid black" | All-Ireland SHC semi-final || 5 July 2026 || [[File:Colours of Clare.svg|border|20x20px]] {{GG|Clare|hurling}} || [[Croke Park]] (N) || align="center"| Win ||align="center"| 2 || align="center"|1–21 to 1–19 || {{Cite web|url=https://www.echolive.ie/corksport/arid-41874398.html|title=Late goal sees Limerick survive intense Clare test to book All-Ireland final return|date=5 July 2026|website=echo live}} |} {{col-end}} ==Pre-match== ===Tickets=== Tickets for the match sold-out and were distributed by the clubs with no public sale and priced at €100 for the stands and €55 for the terrace.{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/brainstorm/2025/0707/1518663-gaa-croke-park-all-ireland-final-ticket-allocations-hurling-football/|title=How do you get your hands on All Ireland final tickets?|date=14 July 2025|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=15 July 2025}} ===Officials=== On 8 July, the GAA named [[Cork GAA|Cork]]'s Colm Lyons from [[Nemo Rangers GAA|Nemo Rangers]] as the referee for the final, his second All-Ireland SHC decider, he previously refereed the [[2022 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2022 final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.gaa.ie/article/colm-lyons-to-referee-all-ireland-shc-final-x9710|title=Colm Lyons to referee All-Ireland SHC Final|date=8 July 2026|work=GAA.ie|accessdate=9 July 2026}} It was his 39th All-Ireland Championship game to referee since his first in 2012. His umpires were Ciarán Hanley, Jim McEvoy, Philip Mackey and Finian Mullane. Line umpires were Wexford’s James Owens and Dublin’s Chris Mooney. James Owens was also the standby referee, and the sideline official was Niall Malone from Clare. David Grogan from Tipperary was the [[Hawk-Eye]] official.{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2026/0708/1582428-lyons-appointed-to-referee-all-ireland-hurling-final/|title=Colm Lyons appointed to referee All-Ireland Hurling Championship final|date=8 July 2026|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=9 July 2026}} ===Jubilee team=== The [[Tipperary county hurling team|Tipperary]] team that won the [[2001 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2001 All-Ireland SHC final]] was presented to the crowd before the match, on the [[silver jubilee]].{{Cite web|url=https://tipperary.gaa.ie/2001-all-ireland-senior-hurling-champions-jubilee-golf-classic/|title=2001 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Champions Jubilee Golf Classic|first=Tipp GAA|last=Admin|date=29 May 2026}}{{cite web|url=https://www.tipperarylive.ie/sport/gaa/watch-tipperary-2001-team-honoured-in-croke-park-ahead-of-all-ireland-final-8810192|title= WATCH: Tipperary 2001 team honoured in Croke Park ahead of All-Ireland final|date=20 July 2026|work=Tipperary Live|accessdate=22 July 2026}} ===Team news=== For Limerick, captain [[Cian Lynch]] was recalled to the starting team in midfield, with Darragh O'Donovan dropping out. [[Mike Casey (hurler)|Mike Casey]] also started at full-back. The Galway team announced was unchanged from the semi-final win against Cork.{{cite web|url= https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2026/0717/1583800-aishc-final-team-news-galway-unchanged-from-semi-final/|title=AISHC final team news: Cian Lynch returns, Galway unchanged from semi-final|date=17 July 2026|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=24 July 2026}} ==Match== ===Details=== {{GAAmatchbox |date={{start date|2026|7|19|df=y}} |time=15:30 {{small|[[Irish Standard Time|IST]] ([[UTC+1]])}} |round=Final |team1=[[Galway county hurling team|Galway]] [[File:Colours of Galway.svg|border|20x20px]] |score1=1–18 {{small|(21)}} |score2= {{small|(32)}} 1–29 |HT=0-8 – 0-13 |report=[https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41882305.html Report] |team2=[[File:Colours of Limerick.svg|border|20x20px]] [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick]] |goals1=Conor Cooney 1(pen) |points1=Aaron Niland 10 (8fs, 1 '65'), Conor Cooney 2 (1f), Thomas Monaghan 2, Cathal Mannion 1, Darragh Neary 1, Jason Rabbitte 1, Colm Molloy 1 |goals2=Cathal O’Neill 1 |points2=Aidan O’Connor 5 (3fs), Cathal O’Neill 4, Aaron Gillane 4, Peter Casey 4, Diarmaid Byrnes 4 (2fs, 1 '65'), Kyle Hayes 2, Adam English 2, Cian Lynch 2, Barry Nash 1, David Reidy 1 |location=[[Dublin]] |venue=[[Croke Park]] |attendance=82,300 |referee= Colm Lyons ([[Cork GAA|Cork]]) |standby = James Owens ([[Wexford GAA|Wexford]]) |linesman = Chros Mooney ([[Dublin GAA|Dublin]]) |sideline = Niall Malone ([[Clare GAA|Clare]]) |umpires = Ciarán Hanley ([[Brian Dillons GAA|Brian Dillons]]), Jim McEvoy ([[Blarney GAA|Blarney]]), Philip Mackey & Finian Mullane ([[Nemo Rangers GAA|Nemo Rangers]]) |TV=[[RTÉ2]]
